title: DRC: European Union Urges Immediate Opening of Humanitarian Corridor in the East
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The European Union (EU) has called for the urgent establishment of a humanitarian corridor in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, to enable the delivery of aid and the resumption of humanitarian…
title_en: DRC: European Union Urges Immediate Opening of Humanitarian Corridor in the East
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The European Union (EU) has called for the urgent establishment of a humanitarian corridor in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, to enable the delivery of aid and the resumption of humanitarian…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The European Union (EU) has called for the urgent establishment of a humanitarian corridor in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, to enable the delivery of aid and the resumption of humanitarian flights to conflict-affected areas.

The appeal was made on Wednesday, November 5, by Johan Borgstram, the EU’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, during a visit to Kinshasa. Borgstram voiced deep concern over the resurgence of violence linked to the M23 rebellion, which he said is supported by Rwanda and constitutes a violation of Congolese territorial integrity.

While commending the diplomatic efforts of Qatar and the United States to revive peace talks, Borgstram urged all parties to respect the ceasefire and adhere to the principles of international humanitarian law.

The EU envoy is expected to continue his mission in Kampala, where he will hold regional consultations aimed at restoring stability in the Great Lakes region.

title: Kinshasa Hosts 31st ICGLR Meeting on Combating Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The capital hosted the 31st meeting of the Regional Committee of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) on November 7-8, 2025, bringing together government officials, civil…
title_en: Kinshasa Hosts 31st ICGLR Meeting on Combating Illegal Exploitation of Natural Resources
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The capital hosted the 31st meeting of the Regional Committee of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) on November 7-8, 2025, bringing together government officials, civil…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The capital hosted the 31st meeting of the Regional Committee of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) on November 7-8, 2025, bringing together government officials, civil society representatives, and technical partners to tackle the illegal exploitation of natural resources.

Organized under the auspices of the Congolese Minister of Mines, the forum focused on coordinating regional policies, strengthening security cooperation, and establishing a common legal framework. Participants also examined the links between illegal mining and armed conflict, aiming to ensure that strategic resources such as coltan, cobalt, and tin contribute to sustainable development.

The ICGLR meeting comes three weeks after the National Forum on socio-economic and mining issues, which addressed peace agreements and resource management in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.

The meeting also focused on strengthening bilateral relations between Kinshasa and Doha ahead of the Emir’s planned visit to the DRC. Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to promoting peace, social development, and mutually beneficial economic cooperation.

title: Doha: President Tshisekedi Highlights Congolese Resilience and Calls for Equitable International Cooperation

excerpt_en: Doha, Qatar - On the sidelines of the second World Summit on Social Development in Doha, Congolese President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, to review peace…
body_en:
Doha, Qatar - On the sidelines of the second World Summit on Social Development in Doha, Congolese President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, to review peace processes in the Democratic Republic of Congo and strengthen bilateral ties.

At the summit, President Tshisekedi lauded the resilience of the Congolese people after three decades of armed conflict and outlined reforms aimed at promoting social justice, including universal health coverage, free primary education, and a development program covering all 145 territories of the country.

He also called for international cooperation grounded in equity and reciprocity, advocating for a new global framework where social justice and lasting peace are recognized as fundamental rights for all peoples.

title: DRC: Parliamentary Concerns Grow Over Delay in Reviewing 2026 Budget
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - With less than 45 days remaining in the ordinary parliamentary session, which is primarily dedicated to budget matters, delays in reviewing the 2026 draft finance law are raising alarm among lawmakers…
title_en: DRC: Parliamentary Concerns Grow Over Delay in Reviewing 2026 Budget
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - With less than 45 days remaining in the ordinary parliamentary session, which is primarily dedicated to budget matters, delays in reviewing the 2026 draft finance law are raising alarm among lawmakers…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - With less than 45 days remaining in the ordinary parliamentary session, which is primarily dedicated to budget matters, delays in reviewing the 2026 draft finance law are raising alarm among lawmakers and civil society.

The election of a new Speaker of the National Assembly, scheduled for November 13, has contributed to concerns over institutional paralysis. Christian Mwando of the opposition party Ensemble pour la République blames the delay on “political distractions” linked to internal petitions, while Gary Sakata of the ruling Sacred Union highlights that the law allows 60 days for both chambers to adopt the budget.

Parliamentary sources indicate that the review of the draft law is expected to begin only after the installation of the new leadership, seen as a prerequisite for the effective resumption of parliamentary work.

title: Maniema: Vice-President of Provincial Assembly Re-elected Amid Impeachment Motion
excerpt: Kindu, Maniema, DRC - Théophile Buleli Docta, Vice-President of the Maniema Provincial Assembly, retained his position after a motion of impeachment filed by three members of his own party was rejected.
title_en: Maniema: Vice-President of Provincial Assembly Re-elected Amid Impeachment Motion
excerpt_en: Kindu, Maniema, DRC - Théophile Buleli Docta, Vice-President of the Maniema Provincial Assembly, retained his position after a motion of impeachment filed by three members of his own party was rejected.
body_en:
Kindu, Maniema, DRC - Théophile Buleli Docta, Vice-President of the Maniema Provincial Assembly, retained his position after a motion of impeachment filed by three members of his own party was rejected.

Accused of holding multiple positions deemed incompatible with his parliamentary responsibilities, the Kabambare representative received broad support from provincial deputies during the plenary session on November 4: 17 votes against the motion, 3 in favor, and one abstention.

According to Assembly rapporteur Papy Omeonga Tchopa, the complaints appeared to stem more from internal party disputes than from Buleli’s institutional duties, underscoring the renewed confidence of the assembly in its vice-president.

excerpt_en: London, UK - On the sidelines of the CNN Global Perspectives on Africa conference on November 3, Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka outlined her government’s vision centered on peace, good governance, and…
body_en:
London, UK - On the sidelines of the CNN Global Perspectives on Africa conference on November 3, Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka outlined her government’s vision centered on peace, good governance, and sustainable resource management.

Addressing ongoing insecurity in eastern DRC, she held Rwanda responsible for the capture of Goma and Bukavu by M23 rebels, while stressing that achieving lasting peace remains the top priority of her mandate after three decades of deadly conflict.

Prime Minister Suminwa also called for equitable economic partnerships, highlighting that the DRC’s mineral resources should benefit local development, support transparent supply chains, and create jobs for Congolese youth.

title: DRC: National Assembly to Elect New Speaker on November 13
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Jacques Djoli, rapporteur of the National Assembly, announced on November 4 that the election of the new Speaker of the lower house, along with the deputy rapporteur, is scheduled for November 13, 2025.
title_en: DRC: National Assembly to Elect New Speaker on November 13
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Jacques Djoli, rapporteur of the National Assembly, announced on November 4 that the election of the new Speaker of the lower house, along with the deputy rapporteur, is scheduled for November 13, 2025.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Jacques Djoli, rapporteur of the National Assembly, announced on November 4 that the election of the new Speaker of the lower house, along with the deputy rapporteur, is scheduled for November 13, 2025.

The decision, made during a meeting of the bureau and the conference of presidents, sets the stage for the succession of Vital Kamerhe. MP Aimé Boji has been designated as the sole candidate of the Sacred Union of the Nation for the Speaker position.

Three candidates are contesting the deputy rapporteur role: Clotilde Mutita (Together for the Republic), Gratien Iracan, and Christelle Vuanga (independent). Candidate registration will remain open for three days under Article 27 of the rules of procedure, followed by a campaign on November 11-12. The formal plenary vote on November 13 will officially invest the newly elected members and allow the resumption of parliamentary work.

Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani urged the suspension of no-confidence motions and petitions in provincial assemblies during wartime, emphasizing the need to preserve institutional stability amid recurring political crises.

Speaking at a meeting with governors, vice-governors, and members of provincial assembly bureaus, Shabani called on officials to ensure transparent and rigorous management of public resources and to maintain continuous dialogue with their assemblies. He also warned that the central government could invoke strong constitutional measures to prevent situations of ungovernability.

title: Doha Hosts Framework Agreement Between Congolese Government and AFC/M23 to Restart Peace Talks
excerpt: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel movement have signed a framework agreement in Doha aimed at reviving negotiations toward a comprehensive peace deal.
title_en: Doha Hosts Framework Agreement Between Congolese Government and AFC/M23 to Restart Peace Talks
excerpt_en: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel movement have signed a framework agreement in Doha aimed at reviving negotiations toward a comprehensive peace deal.
body_en:
The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel movement have signed a framework agreement in Doha aimed at reviving negotiations toward a comprehensive peace deal.

The agreement, reached on Saturday, November 15, outlines both the methodology and the timeline for upcoming discussions. Although the full text is still being finalized, the document calls for the drafting-within two weeks-of several protocols that will guide talks on key issues including humanitarian access, security arrangements, disarmament and reintegration (DDR), the restoration of state authority, the return of displaced populations, economic recovery, and transitional justice.

It also highlights the need to address the root causes of the conflict, such as discrimination, national cohesion, and inclusive governance.

Despite this diplomatic breakthrough, the situation on the ground in North and South Kivu remains volatile. Clashes continue between the FARDC and AFC/M23, with both sides accusing each other of violating ceasefire commitments.

title: National Assembly: Aimé Boji Elected President, Clotilde Mutita Becomes Deputy Rapporteur
excerpt: The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has elected Aimé Boji Sangara as the new President of the Lower House, following a vote held on Thursday, November 13, at the People’s Palace in Kinshasa.
title_en: National Assembly: Aimé Boji Elected President, Clotilde Mutita Becomes Deputy Rapporteur
excerpt_en: The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has elected Aimé Boji Sangara as the new President of the Lower House, following a vote held on Thursday, November 13, at the People’s Palace in Kinshasa.
body_en:
The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has elected Aimé Boji Sangara as the new President of the Lower House, following a vote held on Thursday, November 13, at the People’s Palace in Kinshasa. Boji secured 413 votes out of 423, succeeding Vital Kamerhe.

The interim president of the chamber, Jean-Claude Tshilumbayi, officially confirmed Boji’s election in line with the Assembly’s rules of procedure.

During the same plenary session, opposition lawmaker Clotilde Mutita Kalunga was elected Deputy Rapporteur of the Bureau. She received 389 votes out of 424, taking over from Dominique Munongo.

title: Kinshasa: Félix Tshisekedi and Isaac Herzog Strengthen DRC-Israel Cooperation
excerpt: President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi on Tuesday, November 11, received his Israeli counterpart Isaac Herzog in Kinshasa for a working visit aimed at deepening bilateral relations and promoting a mutually beneficial…
title_en: Kinshasa: Félix Tshisekedi and Isaac Herzog Strengthen DRC-Israel Cooperation
excerpt_en: President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi on Tuesday, November 11, received his Israeli counterpart Isaac Herzog in Kinshasa for a working visit aimed at deepening bilateral relations and promoting a mutually beneficial…
body_en:
President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi on Tuesday, November 11, received his Israeli counterpart Isaac Herzog in Kinshasa for a working visit aimed at deepening bilateral relations and promoting a mutually beneficial partnership between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Israel.

During a joint press briefing, Tshisekedi highlighted the investment opportunities available to Israeli companies in the mining, infrastructure, education, and health sectors. He also reaffirmed the DRC’s support for Israel and its security.

For his part, Isaac Herzog emphasized the historical and spiritual ties connecting the two nations and praised ongoing international efforts - particularly those of U.S. President Donald Trump - to advance peace in Central Africa, especially in the eastern DRC.

This meeting marks another step in the strengthening of diplomatic, economic, and security cooperation between Kinshasa and Tel-Aviv.

title: Boma: The FCDHD Rejects Suspension of Motions in Provincial Assemblies
excerpt: The Fédération congolaise des droits de l’homme et de développement (FCDHD) has voiced strong opposition to the Ministry of Interior and Security’s decision to suspend motions within provincial assemblies.
title_en: Boma: The FCDHD Rejects Suspension of Motions in Provincial Assemblies
excerpt_en: The Fédération congolaise des droits de l’homme et de développement (FCDHD) has voiced strong opposition to the Ministry of Interior and Security’s decision to suspend motions within provincial assemblies.
body_en:
The Fédération congolaise des droits de l’homme et de développement (FCDHD) has voiced strong opposition to the Ministry of Interior and Security’s decision to suspend motions within provincial assemblies. The reaction was delivered on Tuesday, November 11, during a public statement in Boma.

According to Gabriel Makiese, a senior official within the FCDHD, the measure encourages poor governance and opaque management of resources in Kongo Central by restricting the provincial assembly’s essential oversight and accountability role over the executive.

Makiese called on Vice Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani to reverse the decision and urged provincial lawmakers to prioritize the interests of the province over personal or political agendas. He also condemned what he described as interference from Kinshasa in local governance.

title: DRC: Kinshasa and French Delegation Discuss MONUSCO Mandate Renewal
excerpt: Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, received a French delegation in Kinshasa on November 12, 2025.
title_en: DRC: Kinshasa and French Delegation Discuss MONUSCO Mandate Renewal
excerpt_en: Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, received a French delegation in Kinshasa on November 12, 2025.
body_en:
Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, received a French delegation in Kinshasa on November 12, 2025. The delegation was led by Frédéric Jung, Director of the United Nations Department at the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, and accompanied by Ambassador Rémi Maréchaux.

The meeting focused on the upcoming renewal of MONUSCO’s mandate, amid ongoing security concerns in the eastern DRC. Frédéric Jung stressed the importance of heightened attention to civilian protection and humanitarian access, praising the constructive nature of the discussions.

The current MONUSCO mandate is set to expire on December 20, 2025.

excerpt: Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka opened the 19th meeting of the ICGLR Regional Inter-Ministerial Committee in Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, ahead of the Summit of Heads of State.
title_en: Kinshasa: Judith Suminwa Opens 19th ICGLR Meeting, Calls for Regional Action on Peace
excerpt_en: Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka opened the 19th meeting of the ICGLR Regional Inter-Ministerial Committee in Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, ahead of the Summit of Heads of State.
body_en:
Congolese Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka opened the 19th meeting of the ICGLR Regional Inter-Ministerial Committee in Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, ahead of the Summit of Heads of State. The gathering took place amid high regional tensions.

Held under the theme “Consolidating Peace and Security for Sustainable Development in the Great Lakes Region,” the meeting provided a platform for the Prime Minister and Minister of Regional Integration, Floribert Anzuluni, to reaffirm commitments under the 2006 Nairobi Pact and denounce alleged armed aggression against the DRC by a member state.

Both officials stressed the urgency of turning political commitments into concrete actions, urging member states to strengthen the regional monitoring mechanism to foster effective cooperation for peace, security, and development.

The session brought together high-level regional and international officials, setting the stage for the ICGLR Summit, scheduled for November 15.

title: DRC: Joris Salden Warns Against Fraudulent Schengen Visa Agencies
excerpt: During a visit to Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, 2025, Joris Salden, Director General of Consular Affairs at the Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, issued a warning to Schengen visa applicants about the fraudulent…
title_en: DRC: Joris Salden Warns Against Fraudulent Schengen Visa Agencies
excerpt_en: During a visit to Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, 2025, Joris Salden, Director General of Consular Affairs at the Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, issued a warning to Schengen visa applicants about the fraudulent…
body_en:
During a visit to Kinshasa on Thursday, November 13, 2025, Joris Salden, Director General of Consular Affairs at the Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, issued a warning to Schengen visa applicants about the fraudulent practices of some intermediary agencies.

Salden highlighted that certain agencies demand exorbitant fees for appointments or application processing, despite having no access to the official appointment booking platforms. He emphasized that the European Visa Center (EVC) cannot sell appointment slots, making such claims technically impossible.

He also denounced the use of forged documents by these agencies, which often results in visa refusals and penalties for applicants.

Salden urged applicants to follow official procedures through the CEV website and to report fraud when encountered. He reminded the public that the official cost of a Schengen visa is 90 euros, far below the inflated charges demanded by unscrupulous intermediaries.

Preparatory work for the 9th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) was officially launched on Tuesday, November 11, in Kinshasa, under the chairmanship of Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Jacquemain Shabani.

This launch follows two days of consultations among regional experts and marks the beginning of preparations for the summit, scheduled for November 15, 2025, under the theme "Consolidating Peace and Security in the Great Lakes Countries."

According to the Minister, these discussions are essential for strengthening stability, security, and sustainable development in the region, enabling the Great Lakes countries to develop their natural resources and contribute fully to the global economy.

excerpt: Bunia, Ituri, DRC - On Wednesday, November 5, 2025, hundreds of trucks carrying petroleum and essential goods were stranded on National Route 27 (RN27) between Bunia and Mahagi, as the deteriorating Pont Tchulu-Jina…
title_en: Ituri: Hundreds of Trucks Stranded as Bunia-Mahagi Road Crumbles
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri, DRC - On Wednesday, November 5, 2025, hundreds of trucks carrying petroleum and essential goods were stranded on National Route 27 (RN27) between Bunia and Mahagi, as the deteriorating Pont Tchulu-Jina…
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri, DRC - On Wednesday, November 5, 2025, hundreds of trucks carrying petroleum and essential goods were stranded on National Route 27 (RN27) between Bunia and Mahagi, as the deteriorating Pont Tchulu-Jina section, about 40 kilometers north of Bunia, became virtually impassable following heavy rains.

The quagmire threatens the timely supply of essential goods to the region, sparking concern among local communities and traders. The civil society group Forces Vives de l’Ituri criticized the ongoing ineffectiveness of roadworks carried out for over two years by ORC Construct, calling for the termination of the contract to prevent disputes over toll payments and warning of potential price hikes in Bunia’s markets.

ORC Construct has not yet responded to the accusations. Local authorities are assessing emergency measures to restore traffic and prevent a wider economic impact.

title: DRC: SEGUSE Digitizes Import-Export Numbers to Streamline Foreign Trade
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Integrated Single Window for Foreign Trade (SEGUSE) launched the digitization of procedures for obtaining and renewing import-export numbers in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
title_en: DRC: SEGUSE Digitizes Import-Export Numbers to Streamline Foreign Trade
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Integrated Single Window for Foreign Trade (SEGUSE) launched the digitization of procedures for obtaining and renewing import-export numbers in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Integrated Single Window for Foreign Trade (SEGUSE) launched the digitization of procedures for obtaining and renewing import-export numbers in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Under the new system, economic operators can now submit applications online through the SEGUSE digital platform, receive payment notifications from the General Directorate of Administrative and State Revenue (DGRAD), make payments via bank transfer, and obtain their numbers directly in their accounts.

Officials say the reform will reduce processing delays, minimize errors, and prevent the loss of documents. The initiative is part of broader efforts to modernize foreign trade, improve the business climate, and encourage compliance, with authorities warning that non-compliance may result in legal penalties.

title: South Kivu: AFC-M23 Permanently Shuts Lomera Mining Site
excerpt: Lomera, South Kivu, DRC - The Lomera mining site in the Luhihi group, north of Kabare territory, was permanently closed on November 4, 2025, by the armed group AFC-M23.
title_en: South Kivu: AFC-M23 Permanently Shuts Lomera Mining Site
excerpt_en: Lomera, South Kivu, DRC - The Lomera mining site in the Luhihi group, north of Kabare territory, was permanently closed on November 4, 2025, by the armed group AFC-M23.
body_en:
Lomera, South Kivu, DRC - The Lomera mining site in the Luhihi group, north of Kabare territory, was permanently closed on November 4, 2025, by the armed group AFC-M23. Artisanal gold miners were ordered to dismantle equipment, including crushers and motorized pumps, effectively halting operations.

The reasons behind the closure have not been disclosed, but the decision has sparked concern among residents and local stakeholders. The citizen movement Pamoja kwa Amani highlighted that the site was a critical source of income for thousands of families.

Experts warn that the shutdown could worsen poverty and unemployment in the region, with potential social repercussions, including increased crime and violence. Many miners who had taken loans to invest in the operation are now left vulnerable and financially exposed.

Kindu, Maniema, DRC - The construction of the Ulundi bridge on National Route 31 (RN31), which links Kindu to Kisangani, Goma, and Bukavu, has reached a key milestone with the release of funds by the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa (BADEA) and the OPEC Fund (OFID).

The announcement was made on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, by Matthieu Kamulete Amisi, acting provincial coordinator of the Inclusive and Resilient Rural Development Support Program (PADRIR), during the second conference on mining, energy, and infrastructure in Maniema.

Technical studies are scheduled to begin in 2026, with construction expected to start in 2027. Situated between Kailo and Punia, the strategic bridge is designed to improve connectivity within Maniema, stimulate economic recovery, and facilitate the transport of agricultural products and inputs to local markets.

Led by Governor Mussa Kabwankubi, the conference aimed to review progress since the first edition, identify ongoing challenges, and strengthen governance in key sectors to accelerate socio-economic development across the province.

title: DRC Introduces $30 Tax on International Flights in Addition to Go-Pass
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has implemented a new $30 tax on all international flights, both arrivals and departures, in addition to the existing Go-Pass fee.
title_en: DRC Introduces $30 Tax on International Flights in Addition to Go-Pass
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has implemented a new $30 tax on all international flights, both arrivals and departures, in addition to the existing Go-Pass fee.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has implemented a new $30 tax on all international flights, both arrivals and departures, in addition to the existing Go-Pass fee. The announcement follows a partnership signed on October 18, 2025, with U.S.-based Securiport LLC, a company specializing in securing transportation infrastructure.

Under the agreement, 15% of the revenue will go to the Congolese state, while 85% will fund the private partner’s implementation of modern security systems designed to prevent document fraud and counter transnational threats.

Officials, including Jacquemain Shabani and Jean-Pierre Bemba, said the initiative aims to strengthen border controls and bring the DRC’s aviation security in line with international standards. With the new tax, total airport fees for a round-trip international flight now reach $115.

title_en: DRC: Mukoko Samba Assures Senate on Congolese Franc Stability and Protecting Purchasing Power
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 4, 2025, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba reassured the Senate of the government’s commitment to maintaining the stability of the Congolese franc and…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On November 4, 2025, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba reassured the Senate of the government’s commitment to maintaining the stability of the Congolese franc and safeguarding citizens’ purchasing power.

Responding to questions from Senator Janvier Mwisha Kasiwa regarding the gap between the currency’s apparent appreciation and the economic realities faced by the population, Mukoko Samba cited measures including budgetary discipline, coordination with the Central Bank, mobilization of domestic revenue, and ongoing structural reforms.

He noted that these efforts have already contributed to lowering prices for certain essential goods and stressed the importance of building public confidence in the national currency, which he described as a cornerstone of economic sovereignty.

title: DRC, IMF Conclude Second Review of Preliminary Agreement Amid Economic Resilience
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Congolese government and International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff concluded the second review of their Preliminary Agreement, following a mission led by Calixte Ahokpossi.
title_en: DRC, IMF Conclude Second Review of Preliminary Agreement Amid Economic Resilience
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Congolese government and International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff concluded the second review of their Preliminary Agreement, following a mission led by Calixte Ahokpossi.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On November 5, 2025, the Congolese government and International Monetary Fund (IMF) staff concluded the second review of their Preliminary Agreement, following a mission led by Calixte Ahokpossi. Discussions were also held in Haut-Katanga province.

The review highlighted the resilience of the Congolese economy, with projected growth exceeding 5% for 2025 and 2026 and inflation reduced to 2.5% in October. Both parties praised fiscal discipline, coordinated economic policies, and accelerated structural reforms, while noting the continuing impact of conflict in the eastern regions on public finances and humanitarian needs.

A report summarizing the findings will be submitted to the IMF Executive Board for consideration under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) and the Climate Resilience Facility (CRF).

title: DRC: Inflation Falls to 2.7%, Signaling Slowdown in Cost of Living Increases
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Economic Situation Committee announced on November 7, 2025, that inflation in the Democratic Republic of Congo has fallen to 2.7%, well below the projected 7.8% for the year.
title_en: DRC: Inflation Falls to 2.7%, Signaling Slowdown in Cost of Living Increases
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Economic Situation Committee announced on November 7, 2025, that inflation in the Democratic Republic of Congo has fallen to 2.7%, well below the projected 7.8% for the year.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Economic Situation Committee announced on November 7, 2025, that inflation in the Democratic Republic of Congo has fallen to 2.7%, well below the projected 7.8% for the year. Authorities attribute the decrease to stable market prices and a slowdown in the rising cost of living.

The government, led by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, credited fiscal discipline, the stability of the Congolese franc, and measures to control public spending for the favorable outcome. Officials emphasized that ongoing efforts aim to strengthen economic resilience and sustain the downward trend in inflation.

body_en:
The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, finalized the revision of the regulatory framework governing small businesses and retail trade in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Thursday, November 13, 2025, in Kinshasa.

The workshop, held from October 9 to 15, aimed to modernize regulations, protect local economic actors, and strengthen national competitiveness, while promoting formalized and fair trade.

Minister Mukoko Samba reaffirmed his commitment to implementing the reforms in collaboration with all stakeholders and announced that the draft texts would be submitted to Prime Minister Judith Suminwa for review by an inter-ministerial committee before adoption by the Council of Ministers.

The workshop brought together representatives from relevant ministries, the private sector, trade unions, and small business associations.

title: DRC: Active Participation in 6th African Conference on Land Policies in Addis Ababa
excerpt: The Democratic Republic of Congo has been represented in Addis Ababa since November 10, 2025, at the 6th African Conference on Land Policies by a delegation led by Solange Kwinja, a land governance expert.
title_en: DRC: Active Participation in 6th African Conference on Land Policies in Addis Ababa
excerpt_en: The Democratic Republic of Congo has been represented in Addis Ababa since November 10, 2025, at the 6th African Conference on Land Policies by a delegation led by Solange Kwinja, a land governance expert.
body_en:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has been represented in Addis Ababa since November 10, 2025, at the 6th African Conference on Land Policies by a delegation led by Solange Kwinja, a land governance expert.

The conference, which gathers representatives from African governments, international organizations, and civil society, aims to strengthen land policies for sustainable development.

The DRC delegation presented key challenges including land conflicts in the eastern provinces, the securing of land rights for local communities, and initiatives to modernize land management.

Congolese participants advocated for resolutions promoting equitable access to land, conflict prevention, and the promotion of agricultural investment, aiming to bolster the country’s stability and socio-economic development.

title: Maniema Launches Historic Road Paving Program Across Seven Territories
excerpt: Kindu, Maniema - In an unprecedented move since the province’s independence, the government of Maniema has unveiled an ambitious road and bridge modernization program spanning all seven territories.
title_en: Maniema Launches Historic Road Paving Program Across Seven Territories
excerpt_en: Kindu, Maniema - In an unprecedented move since the province’s independence, the government of Maniema has unveiled an ambitious road and bridge modernization program spanning all seven territories.
body_en:
Kindu, Maniema - In an unprecedented move since the province’s independence, the government of Maniema has unveiled an ambitious road and bridge modernization program spanning all seven territories. The announcement was made on Monday, November 3, 2025, by Minister of Infrastructure and Public Works John Banza during the 2nd Provincial Conference on Mines, Energy, and Infrastructure in Kindu.

The project, planned in two phases, will first focus on improving the roads of Kasongo, Pangi, and Kibombo, before extending to Kabambare, Kailo, and Lubutu. In addition to rural roads, the program includes the paving of urban streets in Kindu and the rehabilitation of critical bridges, currently under technical assessment.

“The goal is to open up the province, strengthen connectivity with neighboring regions, and foster local economic growth,” Minister Banza said, emphasizing the government’s commitment to national unity and sustainable development.

Local officials and business leaders welcomed the initiative, noting that improved infrastructure will facilitate trade, mobility, and access to essential services, marking a historic step for Maniema’s development.

title: Kinshasa Floods Paralyze Neighborhoods After Torrential Rains
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Torrential rains on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, caused severe flooding across multiple neighborhoods of Kinshasa, disrupting traffic and daily life for residents.
title_en: Kinshasa Floods Paralyze Neighborhoods After Torrential Rains
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Torrential rains on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, caused severe flooding across multiple neighborhoods of Kinshasa, disrupting traffic and daily life for residents.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Torrential rains on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, caused severe flooding across multiple neighborhoods of Kinshasa, disrupting traffic and daily life for residents.

In Lingwala, the districts of Lokole, Niangwe, and Kalembelembe were submerged, while in Kalamu, overflowing rivers and accumulated debris intensified the situation. Barumbu also faced major flooding, with Itaga Avenue completely submerged and Saint-Charles Lwanga Catholic School forced to suspend evening classes.

The floods triggered a power outage after the Funa transformer substation was inundated. Residents are criticizing the authorities for poor maintenance of drainage ditches, which they say worsened the impact of the rains.

Local authorities are reportedly assessing the damage and coordinating emergency responses to restore normalcy in the affected areas.

excerpt: Katogota, Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - Heavy rains on November 4, 2025, left around 100 families homeless in Katogota, Uvira territory, as 143 houses were destroyed and the roofs of two primary schools and the local 8th…
title_en: South Kivu: Torrential Rains Leave Over 100 Families Homeless in Katogota
excerpt_en: Katogota, Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - Heavy rains on November 4, 2025, left around 100 families homeless in Katogota, Uvira territory, as 143 houses were destroyed and the roofs of two primary schools and the local 8th…
body_en:
Katogota, Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - Heavy rains on November 4, 2025, left around 100 families homeless in Katogota, Uvira territory, as 143 houses were destroyed and the roofs of two primary schools and the local 8th CEPAC church were severely damaged.

Some residents were reportedly swept away by the Ruzizi River, though the exact number remains unclear. Mulala Ngwasi Delphin, coordinator of the Union for Peace and Integral Development (UPDI), issued an urgent appeal to humanitarian organizations to provide immediate assistance to the affected families.

Delphin also warned that ongoing violence in the area, including sexual assaults by combatants, is compounding the security and humanitarian crisis, leaving residents increasingly vulnerable.

title: DRC: English to Be Introduced as Oral Exam in Baccalaureate from 2026
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship has announced that an oral English exam will be officially introduced in the baccalaureate starting in 2026.
title_en: DRC: English to Be Introduced as Oral Exam in Baccalaureate from 2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship has announced that an oral English exam will be officially introduced in the baccalaureate starting in 2026.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship has announced that an oral English exam will be officially introduced in the baccalaureate starting in 2026. The reform will apply to all humanities tracks and aims to strengthen English proficiency among Congolese students, in line with Framework Law No. 14/004 of February 11, 2014, governing national education.

Exam boards for the oral English test will follow the same model as the oral French exam, with equivalent weighting, and results will be recorded using form “E80.” Authorities describe the move as a significant step toward modernizing the Congolese education system and better preparing young people for a globalized academic and professional environment.

title: Kinshasa: Torrential Rains on November 12-14 Cause Deaths, Floods, and Major Damage
excerpt: The Congolese capital, Kinshasa, was hit by torrential rains on the night of Tuesday, November 12, into Wednesday, November 13, and again on Friday, November 14, 2025.
title_en: Kinshasa: Torrential Rains on November 12-14 Cause Deaths, Floods, and Major Damage
excerpt_en: The Congolese capital, Kinshasa, was hit by torrential rains on the night of Tuesday, November 12, into Wednesday, November 13, and again on Friday, November 14, 2025.
body_en:
The Congolese capital, Kinshasa, was hit by torrential rains on the night of Tuesday, November 12, into Wednesday, November 13, and again on Friday, November 14, 2025. The storms resulted in at least two deaths, left many homeless, and caused significant material damage.

Neighborhoods situated below the city limits, including Limete, Selembao, Bumbu, Masina, N’djili, and Kintambo, were particularly affected. The flooding, worsened by the Ndjili, Nsanga, and Makelele rivers, inadequate drainage systems, and sand accumulation in riverbeds, damaged houses, plots of land, markets, and major infrastructure, including two bridges between Kauka and Matonge. Some roads became impassable, forcing residents of the Ndanu neighborhood to seek refuge on their rooftops.

These recurring floods highlight the population’s vulnerability due to poor drainage infrastructure and climate change, emphasizing the need for urgent action by authorities to protect exposed areas and mitigate humanitarian and material impacts.

title: Kasai-Central: Ravine Cuts Off Railway Line in Demba, Civil Society Calls for Emergency Action
excerpt: Heavy rains that struck Kasai-Central earlier this week caused significant damage, notably cutting the railway line in Benaleka, Demba territory, paralyzing rail traffic between Kasai and Kasai-Central.
title_en: Kasai-Central: Ravine Cuts Off Railway Line in Demba, Civil Society Calls for Emergency Action
excerpt_en: Heavy rains that struck Kasai-Central earlier this week caused significant damage, notably cutting the railway line in Benaleka, Demba territory, paralyzing rail traffic between Kasai and Kasai-Central.
body_en:
Heavy rains that struck Kasai-Central earlier this week caused significant damage, notably cutting the railway line in Benaleka, Demba territory, paralyzing rail traffic between Kasai and Kasai-Central.

The disruption isolates Kananga from Mweka, a key supplier of essential agricultural products such as maize, raising concerns of a potential local economic and food crisis. National Route 41 has also been damaged, further complicating road traffic, while the Catholic parish of Benaleka is threatened by the advancing ravine.

In response, the New Congolese Civil Society of Demba has launched an appeal to provincial and national authorities for urgent intervention to rehabilitate infrastructure, protect the population, and restore rail and road connectivity.

title: Tanganyika: Launch of Community Primary Healthcare Project in Kalemie and Kansimba
excerpt: On November 10, 2025, Tanganyika health authorities launched the “Mradi wa Afya Ziwa Tanganyika” (Tanganyika Primary Healthcare) community project, targeting 18 villages in the Kalemie and Kansimba health districts.
title_en: Tanganyika: Launch of Community Primary Healthcare Project in Kalemie and Kansimba
excerpt_en: On November 10, 2025, Tanganyika health authorities launched the “Mradi wa Afya Ziwa Tanganyika” (Tanganyika Primary Healthcare) community project, targeting 18 villages in the Kalemie and Kansimba health districts.
body_en:
On November 10, 2025, Tanganyika health authorities launched the “Mradi wa Afya Ziwa Tanganyika” (Tanganyika Primary Healthcare) community project, targeting 18 villages in the Kalemie and Kansimba health districts.

The project aims to raise awareness about disease prevention, particularly cholera, and to reduce maternal mortality. This three-year pilot initiative, implemented by the Moravian Church of Eastern Congo with financial support from the Danish International Development Cooperation Agency (DICAD), seeks to engage local residents and decision-makers to identify healthcare challenges and propose appropriate solutions, including access to clean water and improved birthing conditions.

The initiative addresses ongoing public health concerns, as communities continue to rely on Lake Tanganyika water for domestic and sanitary purposes.

title: Bukavu: Citizens Launch Peace Campaign in Eastern DRC
excerpt: A citizens’ campaign for peace in eastern DRC was launched on November 11, 2025, in Bukavu, South Kivu, at the Concordia Hall of the Archbishop’s Palace.
title_en: Bukavu: Citizens Launch Peace Campaign in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: A citizens’ campaign for peace in eastern DRC was launched on November 11, 2025, in Bukavu, South Kivu, at the Concordia Hall of the Archbishop’s Palace.
body_en:
A citizens’ campaign for peace in eastern DRC was launched on November 11, 2025, in Bukavu, South Kivu, at the Concordia Hall of the Archbishop’s Palace.

Initiated through consultations between civil society, citizen movements, and religious groups, the campaign seeks to amplify the voices of communities affected by armed conflict and to involve them in efforts to establish lasting peace.

According to Miki Mutiki, one of the campaign initiators, the initiative aims to promote a social program for peace that integrates social, economic, cultural, and environmental dimensions, while recognizing social actors as essential stakeholders in the ongoing peace process.

title: DRC: Dollar Depreciation Fails to Lower Prices of Basic Necessities
excerpt: Nearly a month after the US dollar fell against the Congolese franc, prices for basic necessities in Kinshasa’s markets remain largely unchanged, according to observations on Monday, November 10, 2025, in the Ngaliema…
title_en: DRC: Dollar Depreciation Fails to Lower Prices of Basic Necessities
excerpt_en: Nearly a month after the US dollar fell against the Congolese franc, prices for basic necessities in Kinshasa’s markets remain largely unchanged, according to observations on Monday, November 10, 2025, in the Ngaliema…
body_en:
Nearly a month after the US dollar fell against the Congolese franc, prices for basic necessities in Kinshasa’s markets remain largely unchanged, according to observations on Monday, November 10, 2025, in the Ngaliema district.

While some fresh products like fish and meat have seen slight decreases, other staples-including cassava flour, plantains, and vegetables-have not benefited, and certain items, such as soap, have even increased in price.

Traders attribute this to the lack of agricultural infrastructure and high transportation costs, which negate the effects of the dollar’s depreciation. Consumers in Kinshasa are awaiting concrete measures to ensure that exchange rate stability translates into real relief for household budgets.

title: DRC: Teachers Denounce Payment Delays and Threaten Strike
excerpt: Across the Democratic Republic of Congo, teachers are expressing discontent over recurring salary delays.
title_en: DRC: Teachers Denounce Payment Delays and Threaten Strike
excerpt_en: Across the Democratic Republic of Congo, teachers are expressing discontent over recurring salary delays.
body_en:
Across the Democratic Republic of Congo, teachers are expressing discontent over recurring salary delays. They are criticizing the absence of salary reform and irregular recruitment practices, which complicate personnel management.

In South Ubangi province, the situation is particularly critical for teachers in Kungu territory, who have not received their September and October 2025 salaries. According to Emmanuel Bamolokola, spokesperson for the Espoir de Kungu teachers’ union, some educators are forced to take out loans at exorbitant interest rates, worsening their precarious situation.

Faced with these challenges, teachers are threatening to strike starting November 15 if no solution is implemented. Provincial and national authorities have pledged to engage in discussions to regularize payments and improve working conditions.

title: North Kivu and South Kivu: Torrential Rains Ravage Schools, Disrupt Start of School Year
excerpt: In late October and early November 2025, torrential rains severely damaged school infrastructure in the territories of Rutshuru (North Kivu) and Kalehe (South Kivu), destroying the roofs of at least 22 schools and…
title_en: North Kivu and South Kivu: Torrential Rains Ravage Schools, Disrupt Start of School Year
excerpt_en: In late October and early November 2025, torrential rains severely damaged school infrastructure in the territories of Rutshuru (North Kivu) and Kalehe (South Kivu), destroying the roofs of at least 22 schools and…
body_en:
In late October and early November 2025, torrential rains severely damaged school infrastructure in the territories of Rutshuru (North Kivu) and Kalehe (South Kivu), destroying the roofs of at least 22 schools and forcing hundreds of students to attend classes in precarious conditions-outdoors, under trees, or in makeshift shelters.

In Rutshuru, the primary schools of Kamusenda, Safi, and Selemani were particularly affected, while in Kalehe, a dozen schools in the Kalonge area suffered significant damage.

Teachers and local officials are warning of the urgent need for rapid reconstruction to ensure student safety and the continuity of education, calling on the government and humanitarian organizations to intervene without delay.

title: Ituri: Modernization of Morongo Airport (Bunia) to Boost Regional Economy
excerpt: Modernization work at Morongo Airport (Bunia) in Ituri province is advancing rapidly, with a 90% completion rate, according to Paul Bunagana, provincial commander of the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA), on Friday…
title_en: Ituri: Modernization of Morongo Airport (Bunia) to Boost Regional Economy
excerpt_en: Modernization work at Morongo Airport (Bunia) in Ituri province is advancing rapidly, with a 90% completion rate, according to Paul Bunagana, provincial commander of the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA), on Friday…
body_en:
Modernization work at Morongo Airport (Bunia) in Ituri province is advancing rapidly, with a 90% completion rate, according to Paul Bunagana, provincial commander of the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA), on Friday, November 14, 2025.

Funded by the central government and executed by the Mont Gabaon company, the project includes widening the runway, constructing a new terminal, installing a control tower, building a fire station, and developing an aircraft parking area.

Scheduled for completion in March 2026, this modern infrastructure will accommodate wide-body aircraft, improve connectivity within the province, and stimulate trade, contributing to economic recovery and opening up a region long affected by armed violence.

title: Ituri: Road Users Concerned About Critical Condition of Bunia-Kasenyi Road
excerpt: The approximately 60-kilometer Bunia-Kasenyi road is in very poor condition, making travel extremely difficult for vehicles, motorcycles, and trucks that rely on it daily for cross-border trade with Uganda.
title_en: Ituri: Road Users Concerned About Critical Condition of Bunia-Kasenyi Road
excerpt_en: The approximately 60-kilometer Bunia-Kasenyi road is in very poor condition, making travel extremely difficult for vehicles, motorcycles, and trucks that rely on it daily for cross-border trade with Uganda.
body_en:
The approximately 60-kilometer Bunia-Kasenyi road is in very poor condition, making travel extremely difficult for vehicles, motorcycles, and trucks that rely on it daily for cross-border trade with Uganda.

Torrential rains have damaged the road surface, weakened several bridges, and caused flooding that has blocked traffic, resulting in at least twenty heavy goods vehicle accidents in October and frequent vehicle breakdowns.

Drivers and traders are urging the provincial government to intervene swiftly, through the toll company, to rehabilitate this strategic road, essential for the transport of goods and fish products. No official response has yet been received.

title: Mbuji-Mayi: Normal Air Traffic Resumes After Runway Upgrade
excerpt: The runway upgrade at Bipemba Airport in Mbuji-Mayi was completed on November 9, 2025, allowing air traffic to resume on November 10.
title_en: Mbuji-Mayi: Normal Air Traffic Resumes After Runway Upgrade
excerpt_en: The runway upgrade at Bipemba Airport in Mbuji-Mayi was completed on November 9, 2025, allowing air traffic to resume on November 10.
body_en:
The runway upgrade at Bipemba Airport in Mbuji-Mayi was completed on November 9, 2025, allowing air traffic to resume on November 10.

Launched in August, the project involved widening and extending the runway, laying a second layer of asphalt, and adapting the infrastructure to accommodate Airbus A320 aircraft, increasing the runway length to 2,320 meters.

The previous closure, which lasted approximately two weeks, stranded many travelers and missionaries, who were able to reach their destinations as soon as the runway reopened.

This upgrade is part of the national airport infrastructure modernization program, which aims to improve safety, streamline traffic flow, and strengthen regional connectivity. Construction of complementary infrastructure will continue until next year.
body_fr:
The runway upgrade at Bipemba Airport in Mbuji-Mayi was completed on November 9, 2025, allowing air traffic to resume on November 10.

Launched in August, the project involved widening and extending the runway, laying a second layer of asphalt, and adapting the infrastructure to accommodate Airbus A320 aircraft, increasing the runway length to 2,320 meters.

The previous closure, which lasted approximately two weeks, stranded many travelers and missionaries, who were able to reach their destinations as soon as the runway reopened.

This upgrade is part of the national airport infrastructure modernization program, which aims to improve safety, streamline traffic flow, and strengthen regional connectivity. Construction of complementary infrastructure will continue until next year.

In South Kivu, mobile clinics staffed by midwives have been deployed to support maternity wards in peri-urban and rural areas affected by conflict, particularly in the territories of Kabare, Kalehe, and Walungu.

These mobile units provide medical and logistical support to local facilities and train and mentor midwives in techniques adapted to contexts of conflict, sexual violence, and gender-based violence.

Currently stationed in Kalehe for a two-month mission, the teams will then travel to Walungu (Kaniola and Mubumbano) after completing work in the health zones of Kavumu, Karhanda, and Fomulac Katana.

Nestor Bafunyembaka, vice-president of the midwives’ association, urged local and government authorities to guarantee the safety of the teams in the field.

title: North Kivu: Sharp Resurgence of Measles, Cholera, and Smallpox in Rubaya Health Zone
excerpt: The Rubaya Reference Health Center, in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, is reporting a worrying increase in cases of measles, smallpox, and cholera since June 2025.
title_en: North Kivu: Sharp Resurgence of Measles, Cholera, and Smallpox in Rubaya Health Zone
excerpt_en: The Rubaya Reference Health Center, in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, is reporting a worrying increase in cases of measles, smallpox, and cholera since June 2025.
body_en:
The Rubaya Reference Health Center, in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, is reporting a worrying increase in cases of measles, smallpox, and cholera since June 2025.

Approximately twenty measles cases have required hospitalization, while many other patients are treated in the community by traditional healers, increasing the risk of disease spread.

François Ntambara Bwenge, a state-certified nurse, highlights the lack of isolation facilities and difficulties in accessing patients. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) confirms that the situation is worsened by massive population displacements due to armed conflict, complicating vaccination coverage and facilitating the rapid transmission of diseases.

MSF also notes that comorbidities, including severe malnutrition affecting 12% of cases, exacerbate infections. Logistical obstacles, driven by insecurity and poor road conditions, delay the delivery of medical supplies and the rapid deployment of teams in the field.

title: France: Roger Lumbala Refuses to Appear Before Paris Assize Court, Requests Extradition to DRC
excerpt: The trial of Roger Lumbala Tshitenga, a former Congolese warlord and minister, opened on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, before the Paris Assize Court for alleged complicity in crimes against humanity committed between…
title_en: France: Roger Lumbala Refuses to Appear Before Paris Assize Court, Requests Extradition to DRC
excerpt_en: The trial of Roger Lumbala Tshitenga, a former Congolese warlord and minister, opened on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, before the Paris Assize Court for alleged complicity in crimes against humanity committed between…
body_en:
The trial of Roger Lumbala Tshitenga, a former Congolese warlord and minister, opened on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, before the Paris Assize Court for alleged complicity in crimes against humanity committed between 2002 and 2003 in the provinces of Ituri and North Kivu.

From the outset, the accused dismissed his lawyers and refused to appear, arguing that the French justice system was neither competent nor legitimate to try him, and requested extradition to the Democratic Republic of Congo.

His lawyer, Tshibangu Kalala, criticized the lack of on-the-ground investigation by the French prosecutor’s office, which relied on NGO reports written twenty years after the events, stressing that the production of incriminating evidence is a central issue in the trial.

This procedure falls under the principle of universal jurisdiction, allowing a State to prosecute alleged perpetrators of serious crimes, regardless of where the crimes were committed.

excerpt_en: During the public and solemn opening session of the 2025-2026 judicial year at the Council of State, held on Thursday, November 13, 2025, at the People’s Palace, several speakers advocated for more accessible and…
body_en:
During the public and solemn opening session of the 2025-2026 judicial year at the Council of State, held on Thursday, November 13, 2025, at the People’s Palace, several speakers advocated for more accessible and better-regulated administrative justice.

The president of the National Bar Association called for free legal aid in disputes involving the administration, particularly in cases of demolition and expropriation. Attorney General Jean Paul Mukolo Nkokesha denounced abuses related to summary proceedings and urged more rigorous oversight of appeals.

First President Brigitte Nsensele wa Nsensele highlighted the efficiency of the judicial administration and welcomed the historic appointment of a woman to head the High Court, which oversees the administrative courts and courts of appeal in the DRC.

title: DRC: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights Officially Recognizes Congolese Genocide
excerpt: The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, welcomed the recognition of the Congolese genocide by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (ACHPR) and African civil society on Monday, November 10, 2025, in…
title_en: DRC: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights Officially Recognizes Congolese Genocide
excerpt_en: The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, welcomed the recognition of the Congolese genocide by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (ACHPR) and African civil society on Monday, November 10, 2025, in…
body_en:
The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, welcomed the recognition of the Congolese genocide by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (ACHPR) and African civil society on Monday, November 10, 2025, in Kinshasa.

He described this decision as a victory for advocacy efforts led by the presidential couple, the government, and numerous actors in Congolese civil society. According to him, the two resolutions adopted at the 85th session of the ACHPR-one from African civil society and the other from the Commission itself-constitute a decisive step toward justice for the victims.

Samuel Mbemba encouraged all Congolese citizens to take ownership of this struggle so that the perpetrators and those who ordered the genocide are held accountable. He emphasized that the recognition also reflects the commitment of President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa to compensating the victims, and he believes this development will pave the way for new international positions.

title: DRC: UNPC Demands Justice for Slain Journalists and Greater Protection for the Press
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists on November 2, the National Union of Journalists of Congo (UNPC) renewed its call for truth, justice, and vigilance…
title_en: DRC: UNPC Demands Justice for Slain Journalists and Greater Protection for the Press
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists on November 2, the National Union of Journalists of Congo (UNPC) renewed its call for truth, justice, and vigilance…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists on November 2, the National Union of Journalists of Congo (UNPC) renewed its call for truth, justice, and vigilance in the face of continuing violence against media professionals.

Speaking in Kinshasa, UNPC President Kamanda Wa Kamanda Muzembe urged Congolese authorities to shed light on the unsolved murders of journalists Franck Ngike Kangundu, Bapuwa Mwamba, and Baudouin Kayembe, whose killings remain unpunished years later.

Kamanda denounced the fragility of press freedom in a country marked by insecurity and persistent threats to journalists, emphasizing that impunity continues to embolden perpetrators. He also called on media practitioners to exercise caution and responsibility in their work while honoring the memory of colleagues who lost their lives in the pursuit of truth - both in the Democratic Republic of Congo and around the world.

title: Kinshasa: Warrant Officer Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison in Honorine Porsche Case
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Kinshasa-Gombe Military Court has delivered its verdict in the Honorine Porsche case, linked to the Rawbank Victoire robbery of October 16.
title_en: Kinshasa: Warrant Officer Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison in Honorine Porsche Case
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Kinshasa-Gombe Military Court has delivered its verdict in the Honorine Porsche case, linked to the Rawbank Victoire robbery of October 16.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Kinshasa-Gombe Military Court has delivered its verdict in the Honorine Porsche case, linked to the Rawbank Victoire robbery of October 16. On Thursday, November 6, 2025, the court sentenced a warrant officer to ten years in prison for the mistreatment of the victim, while acquitting the police officers involved.

The court also ordered the payment of $5,000 in damages to Honorine Porsche, who was assaulted during the incident. Both the defense and prosecution have announced plans to appeal the decision.

Meanwhile, the separate trial concerning the robbery itself is still ongoing, with a reconstruction of events scheduled for November 7 at the Rawbank Victoire branch in Kinshasa.

excerpt_en: Bunia, DRC - The Ituri Provincial Civil Society has denounced what it describes as a large-scale misappropriation of oil revenue collected at the Mahagi border post with Uganda, claiming that the Congolese state loses…
body_en:
Bunia, DRC - The Ituri Provincial Civil Society has denounced what it describes as a large-scale misappropriation of oil revenue collected at the Mahagi border post with Uganda, claiming that the Congolese state loses an estimated US$1.8 million per month.

Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, in Bunia, Dieudonné Lossa, the group’s coordinator, revealed that only 171 of the 750 tanker trucks that crossed the border in August 2025 were officially registered, suggesting the presence of a mafia-style network siphoning off state funds.

Civil society leaders have called on provincial authorities to open an investigation and hold those responsible accountable. The governor’s spokesperson responded that the allegations would be reviewed to ensure transparency and protect public interests.

body_en:
Bunia, DRC - More than 200 soldiers from the TIGRE special unit of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have completed a four-week intensive training program on combat tactics and international humanitarian law.

The training, conducted by MONUSCO peacekeepers at the Diango military training center, concluded on Wednesday, November 5, and aimed to strengthen discipline, enhance civilian protection, and improve the effectiveness of military operations against armed groups active in Ituri province.

During the closing ceremony, Ituri’s military governor, General Johnny Luboya, praised the collaboration and urged the soldiers to uphold courage, professionalism, and respect for human rights in their missions.

MONUSCO announced that additional specialized training sessions will be organized in December, as part of ongoing efforts to bolster the capacity of the Congolese armed forces in conflict-affected regions.

Kinshasa, DRC - Former U.S. Special Envoy for the Great Lakes and Sahel region, Peter Pham, held talks with Congolese defense officials during a visit to Kinshasa on November 3 and 4, focusing on efforts to strengthen national security and improve the welfare of veterans.

Pham met with Deputy Prime Minister of National Defense Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita and Minister Delegate for Veterans Affairs Eliezer Ntambwe to discuss the security situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, international defense cooperation, and the professionalization of the Armed Forces (FARDC).

During the meeting, Pham proposed initiatives to consolidate strategic partnerships aimed at achieving lasting peace in the region. He also praised the Congolese government’s efforts to honor military veterans and recognize their contribution to the country’s stability.

The mission is part of the FEC program (Training, Equipment, Barracks), designed to strengthen the professionalization and modernization of the Congolese army, in line with President Félix Tshisekedi’s vision for national defense reform.

During his visit, Kabombo is expected to assess the operational readiness of troops deployed in the region and to encourage soldiers engaged in defending the country’s territorial integrity, as tensions continue between government forces and the AFC-M23 rebels, despite ongoing peace efforts under the Doha process.

title_en: North Kivu: 18 Civilians Injured in Clashes Between AFC-M23 Rebels and Wazalendo Fighters
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, DRC - At least 18 civilians were injured on Tuesday, November 4, in Mashango, Rutshuru Territory (North Kivu), following violent clashes between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters from the Collective of…
body_en:
Rutshuru, DRC - At least 18 civilians were injured on Tuesday, November 4, in Mashango, Rutshuru Territory (North Kivu), following violent clashes between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters from the Collective of Movements for Change (CMC/NYATURA).

Local sources reported that the victims, who were caught in crossfire while taking part in community work, were transported to Mwesso Referral Hospital in neighboring Masisi Territory for treatment.

The Bwito chiefdom, where the fighting occurred, remains mired in insecurity and mass displacement, with residents fleeing toward Mwesso, Birambizo, and Kanyabayonga.

This latest escalation further deepens the humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where ongoing clashes between armed groups continue to endanger civilians and strain relief efforts.

excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently facing severe food insecurity, according to the results of the 24th cycle of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) presented on Tuesday…
title_en: DRC: Nearly 25 Million People Facing Severe Food Insecurity
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently facing severe food insecurity, according to the results of the 24th cycle of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) presented on Tuesday…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently facing severe food insecurity, according to the results of the 24th cycle of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) presented on Tuesday, November 4, 2025, by the Ministry of Agriculture in Kinshasa.

The report indicates that 24.8 million people were affected between September and December 2025, mainly in North Kivu, South Kivu, Tanganyika, and Ituri. It attributes the crisis to armed conflicts, mass displacement, flooding, and weak infrastructure, warning that conditions could further deteriorate in 2026.

Validated by Minister Mohindo Nzangi and supported by partners including UNICEF, WFP, FAO, and ACF, the report urges authorities to end conflicts, improve humanitarian access, and stabilize food and oil prices through social protection programs.

title: Walikale Faces Severe Hunger as WFP and UNICEF Mobilize Aid
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - The World Food Programme (WFP) and UNICEF have issued an urgent warning over a critical nutritional crisis in Walikale, threatening thousands of displaced families.
title_en: Walikale Faces Severe Hunger as WFP and UNICEF Mobilize Aid
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - The World Food Programme (WFP) and UNICEF have issued an urgent warning over a critical nutritional crisis in Walikale, threatening thousands of displaced families.
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - The World Food Programme (WFP) and UNICEF have issued an urgent warning over a critical nutritional crisis in Walikale, threatening thousands of displaced families. The territory, already classified as Phase 4 of food insecurity - just below famine - is facing an estimated malnutrition rate of 46%.

During a meeting in Beni with North Kivu’s vice-governor, Ollo Sib, the acting WFP Country Director in the DRC announced the imminent deployment of a joint WFP-UNICEF mission to assess conditions and restart humanitarian operations.

UN agencies are calling for strengthened international coordination to swiftly address the urgent food, health, and protection needs of the vulnerable populations in Walikale.

“The situation is alarming, and immediate action is required to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe,” the WFP official said, highlighting the scale of the crisis.

title: DRC: Nearly 25 Million People Face Acute Food Insecurity, IPC Warns
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently grappling with a food crisis or emergency, with the hardest hit regions in eastern DRC, according to the latest report from the Integrated Food Security Phase…
title_en: DRC: Nearly 25 Million People Face Acute Food Insecurity, IPC Warns
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently grappling with a food crisis or emergency, with the hardest hit regions in eastern DRC, according to the latest report from the Integrated Food Security Phase…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Nearly 25 million Congolese are currently grappling with a food crisis or emergency, with the hardest hit regions in eastern DRC, according to the latest report from the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) released on November 4, 2025.

The provinces most affected include Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tanganyika, and Maniema, where armed conflict, mass displacement, deteriorating infrastructure, and reduced humanitarian aid are fueling hunger. Of those affected, 3.2 million are in an emergency situation requiring immediate humanitarian assistance.

The IPC warns that the situation could worsen by June 2026, potentially putting over 26 million people at risk of severe food insecurity. The report calls for urgent measures to strengthen rural community resilience and expand humanitarian aid to avert a deepening crisis.

title: Deadly ADF Attack in Byambwe: 20 Civilians Killed, Including 18 Patients from Health Center
excerpt: At least 20 civilians, including 18 bedridden patients, were killed overnight Friday to Saturday in an attack attributed to ADF rebels on the Byambwe referral health center, located 42 km from Butembo in North Kivu.
title_en: Deadly ADF Attack in Byambwe: 20 Civilians Killed, Including 18 Patients from Health Center
excerpt_en: At least 20 civilians, including 18 bedridden patients, were killed overnight Friday to Saturday in an attack attributed to ADF rebels on the Byambwe referral health center, located 42 km from Butembo in North Kivu.
body_en:
At least 20 civilians, including 18 bedridden patients, were killed overnight Friday to Saturday in an attack attributed to ADF rebels on the Byambwe referral health center, located 42 km from Butembo in North Kivu.

According to local sources, the attackers targeted the health facility, looted medicines, and set fire to neighboring houses, leaving behind a scene of devastation. Two other victims were found burned beyond recognition along the Mabiango road.

Civil society in the Bapere sector is calling for large-scale military operations to secure the area and restore the isolation of Mangurejipa, while its president, Kakule Samuel, warns of growing panic and the exodus of residents toward Butembo.

As of Saturday, November 15, 2025, the administrative authorities had not yet issued a response.

body_en:
The national coordinator of the P-DDRCS, Jean-Désiré Ntanga Ntita, appealed on Thursday, November 13, 2025, during a meeting in Kinshasa with UN agencies and several NGOs, for increased support from partners to enable the program's deployment in six additional provinces: Maï-Ndombe, Kwango, Kasaï Central, and Kasaï.

He emphasized the need for strategic alignment to avoid duplication and optimize resources, stressing that the objective for the next three months is to expand the program's activities in support of the peace vision championed by the Head of State.

The deputy coordinator presented the mandate of the mechanism and its operational prospects, an approach aimed at strengthening stabilization, socio-economic reconciliation, and peacebuilding, in accordance with the call made by President Félix Tshisekedi at the 79th United Nations General Assembly.

excerpt: On Tuesday, November 11, 2025, the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) reinforced their presence on National Route 27 between Bunia and Mahagi, significantly improving the safety of road users long exposed to attacks by…
title_en: Ituri: FARDC Reinforces Security on National Route 27 Despite Advanced State of Disrepair
excerpt_en: On Tuesday, November 11, 2025, the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) reinforced their presence on National Route 27 between Bunia and Mahagi, significantly improving the safety of road users long exposed to attacks by…
body_en:
On Tuesday, November 11, 2025, the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) reinforced their presence on National Route 27 between Bunia and Mahagi, significantly improving the safety of road users long exposed to attacks by armed groups, particularly in the Djugu territory.

Thanks to closer military deployments and mobile patrols day and night, ambushes are now rare, according to several accounts. However, the poor condition of this 185 km road, exacerbated by the rains, continues to immobilize hundreds of vehicles for several days.

Despite the persistent presence of certain militias, road users welcome the improved security and call on the government to redouble efforts to establish lasting peace and urgently rehabilitate this vital road for Ituri.

title: Masisi: Violent Clashes Between M23 and Wazalendo Worsen Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Violent fighting erupted on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo armed groups in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, particularly affecting the localities of Ngululu and Kataandwa.
title_en: Masisi: Violent Clashes Between M23 and Wazalendo Worsen Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Violent fighting erupted on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo armed groups in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, particularly affecting the localities of Ngululu and Kataandwa.
body_en:
Violent fighting erupted on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo armed groups in the Masisi territory of North Kivu, particularly affecting the localities of Ngululu and Kataandwa.

According to local sources, the Wazalendo seized control of the village of Mulema, while AFC/M23 established a presence in Karere, about 3 km from the center of Kazinga. The exchanges of fire caused mass displacement of residents to safer areas and a climate of panic, notably in Mwesso and Mbuhi, where a civilian was wounded by a stray bullet.

These clashes are disrupting access to humanitarian aid and exacerbating the security and humanitarian crisis in the region.

title: North Kivu: Province-Wide Arms and Ammunition Collection Campaign Launched
excerpt: The military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakulé Somo, launched a large-scale operation on Tuesday, November 11, to collect firearms, ammunition, and explosive devices throughout the province.
title_en: North Kivu: Province-Wide Arms and Ammunition Collection Campaign Launched
excerpt_en: The military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakulé Somo, launched a large-scale operation on Tuesday, November 11, to collect firearms, ammunition, and explosive devices throughout the province.
body_en:
The military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakulé Somo, launched a large-scale operation on Tuesday, November 11, to collect firearms, ammunition, and explosive devices throughout the province.

The campaign aims to reduce armed violence, ensure public safety, and restore state authority. A special national commission will oversee the operation, supported by local commissions composed of representatives from government authorities, FARDC, the police, civil society, and religious leaders.

Citizens who voluntarily surrender their weapons will receive a financial reward proportional to the type of weapon and quantity of ammunition. Surrenders will be confidential and without legal repercussions, with collected weapons centralized in Beni before being handed over to the FARDC command.

Funded by the government and its partners, the campaign also aims to raise public awareness of the risks associated with illegal possession of weapons.
