excerpt: Nearly 4,000 displaced people remain around the MONUSCO base in the Gina area of Djugu territory, Ituri, more than three months after clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and CRP…
title_en: Ituri: Displaced Persons in Gina Call for Increased Security to Return Home
excerpt_en: Nearly 4,000 displaced people remain around the MONUSCO base in the Gina area of Djugu territory, Ituri, more than three months after clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and CRP…
body_en:
Nearly 4,000 displaced people remain around the MONUSCO base in the Gina area of Djugu territory, Ituri, more than three months after clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and CRP militias (Republican People's Corps).

The displaced population is demanding increased security to safely return to their villages. During a meeting on Tuesday, November 11, with a UN delegation, they denounced the persistent insecurity that prevents them from cultivating their land and resuming normal life. Many are living in precarious conditions, sometimes sleeping outdoors.

They called for a strengthened FARDC presence, increased patrols by UN peacekeepers, and the resumption of intercommunal dialogue to restore social cohesion. MONUSCO assured the community that it continues to secure the area and facilitate the safe return of the population.

title_en: DRC: Moves to Strengthen Military Cooperation with Burkina Faso, Niger, and Russia
excerpt_en: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, reaffirmed on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, the DRC’s commitment to enhancing military cooperation with Burkina Faso, Niger, and the…
body_en:
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, reaffirmed on Wednesday, November 12, 2025, the DRC’s commitment to enhancing military cooperation with Burkina Faso, Niger, and the Russian Federation.

He made the statement at the first African Defense and Security Exhibition, “BAMZEX 25,” held in Bamako, Mali. During discussions with African and international counterparts, Minister Kabombo emphasized experience-sharing and military training, in line with President Félix Tshisekedi's vision of a security-autonomous Africa.

The Congolese minister highlighted that Africa possesses the human, technical, and moral resources necessary for its own security, and stressed the need to revitalize the Congolese defense industry. The exhibition was themed “Africa at the heart of global defense innovations.”

On Thursday, November 13, 2025, fighting erupted between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters, members of the AVAFAC militia, in the Kabare territory of South Kivu, particularly in the localities of Mutshshemi, Kabukungu, Mucheni, and Kabulungu.

The clashes caused panic and population displacement, with exchanges of heavy and light weapons fire lasting nearly three hours. Civil society condemned what it called a flagrant violation of the Doha ceasefire agreement, accusing the M23 of conducting a belligerent campaign near Kahuzi-Biega National Park.

These incidents occurred while peace talks were ongoing in Washington, prompting civil society to call on national authorities and international partners to intervene urgently to prevent an escalation of the conflict in eastern DRC.

body_en:
On Thursday, November 12, 2025, MONUSCO’s Disarmament, Demobilization, Reintegration and Stabilization (DDRS) section repatriated 17 Rwandan citizens, including 5 former FDLR combatants and 9 children, to Rwanda via the Grande Barrière border crossing between Goma and Gisenyi.

The repatriated individuals were welcomed by Rwandan authorities and will participate in a national social reintegration program. This operation marks the second repatriation this week, bringing the total number of former FDLR members and their families repatriated since January 2025 to 166, as part of MONUSCO’s efforts to promote peace and stability in eastern DRC.

title: North Kivu: Armed Bandits Rob Travelers on National Route 2 in Rutshuru
excerpt: On Thursday, November 13, 2025, a public transport vehicle was intercepted by armed bandits on National Route 2, between Kiwanja and Kanyabayonga, in the Rutshuru territory of North Kivu.
title_en: North Kivu: Armed Bandits Rob Travelers on National Route 2 in Rutshuru
excerpt_en: On Thursday, November 13, 2025, a public transport vehicle was intercepted by armed bandits on National Route 2, between Kiwanja and Kanyabayonga, in the Rutshuru territory of North Kivu.
body_en:
On Thursday, November 13, 2025, a public transport vehicle was intercepted by armed bandits on National Route 2, between Kiwanja and Kanyabayonga, in the Rutshuru territory of North Kivu.

At gunpoint, passengers were forced to exit the vehicle and lie on the ground before being robbed of phones, money, merchandise, and other valuables. This marks the third attack on this stretch of road in a month, following the October 29 incident that left two people dead.

Authorities warn that this event reflects the resurgence of violence on this strategic road, where armed groups regularly operate, disrupting traffic and endangering the civilian population.

title: Kabambare, Kasongo, and Shabunda: Wazalendo Linked to 68 Murders in Three Months
excerpt: Between August and November 2025, at least 68 murders were attributed to fighters claiming allegiance to Wazalendo in the territories of Kabambare and Kasongo (Maniema province), as well as Shabunda (South Kivu)…
title_en: Kabambare, Kasongo, and Shabunda: Wazalendo Linked to 68 Murders in Three Months
excerpt_en: Between August and November 2025, at least 68 murders were attributed to fighters claiming allegiance to Wazalendo in the territories of Kabambare and Kasongo (Maniema province), as well as Shabunda (South Kivu)…
body_en:
Between August and November 2025, at least 68 murders were attributed to fighters claiming allegiance to Wazalendo in the territories of Kabambare and Kasongo (Maniema province), as well as Shabunda (South Kivu), according to Walubangi Katuta Albert, administrator of Kabambare, who raised the alarm on Friday, November 14.

The most recent incident, occurring about ten days ago, involved a merchant shot dead, mistakenly identified as a member of M23. Local authorities denounce the impunity enjoyed by these militiamen and are calling for a joint intervention by the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) from the affected provinces to protect the population.

The community is also urging the central government and provincial authorities to strengthen security and restore peace in these territories, which have been severely impacted by Wazalendo’s violence.
body_fr:
Between August and November 2025, at least 68 murders were attributed to fighters claiming allegiance to Wazalendo in the territories of Kabambare and Kasongo (Maniema province), as well as Shabunda (South Kivu), according to Walubangi Katuta Albert, administrator of Kabambare, who raised the alarm on Friday, November 14.

The most recent incident, occurring about ten days ago, involved a merchant shot dead, mistakenly identified as a member of M23. Local authorities denounce the impunity enjoyed by these militiamen and are calling for a joint intervention by the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) from the affected provinces to protect the population.

The community is also urging the central government and provincial authorities to strengthen security and restore peace in these territories, which have been severely impacted by Wazalendo’s violence.

title_en: Kabare: Clashes Renew Between M23 and Wazalendo Despite Doha Ceasefire
excerpt_en: On Thursday, November 13, fighting erupted in the Kabare territory of South Kivu, pitting M23 rebels against Wazalendo fighters (AVAFAC), particularly in the areas of Mutshshemi, Kabukungu, and around the “Chez Mbayo”…
body_en:
On Thursday, November 13, fighting erupted in the Kabare territory of South Kivu, pitting M23 rebels against Wazalendo fighters (AVAFAC), particularly in the areas of Mutshshemi, Kabukungu, and around the “Chez Mbayo” plantation, causing widespread panic and population displacement.

Local sources reported that the hostilities lasted nearly three hours, featuring intense exchanges of light and heavy weapons fire, following an M23 attack on Wazalendo positions.

Civil society in Kabare denounced this resumption of fighting as a violation of the Doha ceasefire and accused M23 of pursuing a belligerent strategy by approaching Kahuzi-Biega National Park, a designated neutral zone.

While peace negotiations continue in Washington, tensions remain high on the ground, with the FARDC and M23 accusing each other of not respecting commitments in several areas of South and North Kivu, prompting civil society to demand urgent intervention from the authorities and international partners.

title_en: Beni: WFP Integrates Community Priorities into Five-Year Plan
excerpt_en: On Thursday, November 13, the World Food Programme (WFP) launched a consultation process in Beni, involving provincial authorities, development actors, and civil society in North Kivu.
body_en:
On Thursday, November 13, the World Food Programme (WFP) launched a consultation process in Beni, involving provincial authorities, development actors, and civil society in North Kivu. The initiative aims to integrate the real needs of local communities into the formulation of WFP’s five-year plan.

The process was welcomed by Éric Kisa Kayobera, Senior Coordinator of the Provincial Administration, as part of a participatory governance approach designed to identify priorities on the ground and strengthen collaboration with the Congolese government.

He emphasized the importance of collecting data in remote areas to ensure that the future program is community-rooted and addresses the basic needs of the population.

title: CICR Reaffirms Humanitarian Commitment in Eastern DRC
excerpt: On Friday, November 14, 2025, in Goma, the Regional Director for Africa of the International Committee of the Red Cross (CICR), Patrick Youssef, reaffirmed his organization’s determination to intensify humanitarian aid…
title_en: CICR Reaffirms Humanitarian Commitment in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: On Friday, November 14, 2025, in Goma, the Regional Director for Africa of the International Committee of the Red Cross (CICR), Patrick Youssef, reaffirmed his organization’s determination to intensify humanitarian aid…
body_en:
On Friday, November 14, 2025, in Goma, the Regional Director for Africa of the International Committee of the Red Cross (CICR), Patrick Youssef, reaffirmed his organization’s determination to intensify humanitarian aid to vulnerable populations in eastern DRC, despite unstable security conditions and growing financial constraints.

Accompanied by the Secretary-General of the Swedish Red Cross, he praised the resilience of local communities and the dedication of the 10,000 volunteers mobilized in the region. Highlighting ongoing efforts, including the distribution of seeds and food to 5,600 families in the Ikobo group, North Kivu, Youssef called on international donors to maintain focus on this persistent crisis, stressing the need for rapid and dignified assistance to those affected.

The first half of November 2025 for the Democratic Republic of Congo was marked by a stark contrast between high-level diplomatic and economic activities and a severe, deteriorating humanitarian reality, particularly in the east.

Internationally, the period saw a surge in diplomatic efforts focused on the eastern conflict, with the EU demanding a humanitarian corridor , President Tshisekedi engaging with Qatar on the peace process , and Prime Minister Suminwa calling for equitable partnerships in London. Macro-economically, the government projected stability, citing a resilient economy , a stable Congolese franc , and a significant drop in inflation , which was supported by the IMF's second review.

However, this high-level optimism was overshadowed by a deepening crisis on the ground. The humanitarian situation reached a critical point, with reports indicating nearly 25 million Congolese face severe food insecurity. The crisis is particularly acute in areas like Walikale, which is on the brink of famine with a 46% malnutrition rate. This situation is fueled by ongoing armed conflicts, which continue to injure civilians and displace populations , as well as by armed groups shutting down key economic sites.

Domestically, the government is navigating internal political and structural challenges. This includes parliamentary delays in reviewing the 2026 budget , calls by the Interior Minister to suspend no-confidence motions during wartime , and persistent issues of impunity and alleged large-scale corruption. Furthermore, critical infrastructure failures, such as major flooding in Kinshasa and South Kivu and the collapse of a key route in Ituri, continue to disrupt daily life and supply chains.

title: Qatar and DRC Sign Six Bilateral Agreements to Strengthen Cooperation
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - During an official visit to Kinshasa, the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and the President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, presided over the signing…
title_en: Qatar and DRC Sign Six Bilateral Agreements to Strengthen Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - During an official visit to Kinshasa, the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and the President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, presided over the signing…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - During an official visit to Kinshasa, the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and the President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, presided over the signing of six bilateral agreements aimed at deepening cooperation between the two nations.

The memoranda of understanding cover a range of strategic areas, including port management between Mwani Qatar and the Congolese National Transport Office (ONATRA), legal cooperation, visa exemptions for holders of diplomatic and special passports, and partnerships focused on youth and sports development.

The two governments also established a mechanism for regular political consultations and signed a memorandum between the Qatar Fund for Development and the Congolese Ministry of Social Affairs to support a multi-sectoral emergency response in South Kivu, addressing urgent humanitarian and development needs.

This series of agreements builds on previous commitments, notably the letters of intent signed in September 2025, which outlined an investment portfolio worth US$21 billion, signaling a significant boost in bilateral economic and strategic relations.

The agreements highlight both countries’ commitment to enhancing political, economic, and social collaboration, fostering sustainable development and regional stability.

title: Crisis in Eastern DRC: Sama Lukonde Urges African Parliaments to Show Greater Solidarity
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - At the opening of the 47th Conference of Speakers of African Parliaments, President of the Congolese Senate Sama Lukonde called on legislators across Africa to demonstrate stronger…
title_en: Crisis in Eastern DRC: Sama Lukonde Urges African Parliaments to Show Greater Solidarity
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - At the opening of the 47th Conference of Speakers of African Parliaments, President of the Congolese Senate Sama Lukonde called on legislators across Africa to demonstrate stronger…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 21, 2025 - At the opening of the 47th Conference of Speakers of African Parliaments, President of the Congolese Senate Sama Lukonde called on legislators across Africa to demonstrate stronger solidarity in addressing the ongoing insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

Describing the situation as a “silent genocide”, Lukonde highlighted the toll of millions of deaths and nearly 7 million displaced persons, stressing the urgent need for a coordinated continental response. He urged African parliamentary bodies to actively support ongoing peace initiatives, including those led in Washington and Doha, while advocating for parliaments to serve as “laboratories of solutions” tailored to African realities.

In response, the African Parliamentary Union (APU), represented by Vice-President Abdoul Esikiye, reaffirmed its solidarity with populations affected by humanitarian crises in both the DRC and Sudan.

The conference, held as part of the 84th session of the APU Executive Committee, concluded with a commitment to strengthen continental parliamentary cooperation and enhance unified action in addressing Africa’s security and humanitarian challenges.

title: DRC and Rwanda Reaffirm Security Commitments at 4th Joint Mechanism Meeting in Washington
excerpt: Washington, D.C., November 19-20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda convened the fourth meeting of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism in Washington, D.C., with participation from…
title_en: DRC and Rwanda Reaffirm Security Commitments at 4th Joint Mechanism Meeting in Washington
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C., November 19-20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda convened the fourth meeting of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism in Washington, D.C., with participation from…
body_en:
Washington, D.C., November 19-20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda convened the fourth meeting of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism in Washington, D.C., with participation from representatives of the United States, Qatar, and Togo, acting as the African Union mediator.

The talks aimed to accelerate the implementation of the Peace Agreement signed on June 27, 2025, with both parties reaffirming their commitment to the Order of Operations (OPORD) and the Concept of Operations (CONOPS) of the Harmonized Plan. This framework focuses on neutralizing the FDLR, disengaging Rwandan forces, and lifting Rwandan defensive measures.

The meeting assessed progress in the first phase of ongoing security operations, including intelligence sharing and awareness-raising activities led by the DRC, while addressing the challenges of the second phase, which emphasizes neutralization and disengagement.

Participants underscored the alignment between the Washington and Doha peace processes, welcoming the recent Doha Framework Agreement signed between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 coalition. A high-level follow-up meeting is scheduled for January 17, 2026, in Togo, intended to consolidate progress in the Great Lakes peace process.

title_en: Eastern DRC: AFC/M23 Claims Neutralization of Armed Groups under Doha Agreement
excerpt_en: Goma, November 21, 2025 - The AFC/M23 movement announced that it had "neutralized" all local and foreign armed groups operating in eastern DRC, in accordance with the Doha Framework Agreement recently signed with the…
body_en:
Goma, November 21, 2025 - The AFC/M23 movement announced that it had "neutralized" all local and foreign armed groups operating in eastern DRC, in accordance with the Doha Framework Agreement recently signed with the Congolese government.

According to Benjamin Mbonimpa, permanent secretary of AFC/M23, the agreement commits both parties to:

Neutralize foreign forces such as the FDLR and the ADF;

Establish transitional security mechanisms to protect civilians.

The announcement comes amid ongoing fighting in the Walikale, Masisi, Rutshuru, and Lubero territories, despite the Doha ceasefire. The Congolese army claims to have regained control of several localities, including Katoyi, highlighting the persistent instability in the region.

title: DRC and Tunisia Strengthen Trade and Investment Ties
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tunisia have agreed to boost trade and intensify bilateral investments during the Tunisia-DRC Business Forum held in Kinshasa.
title_en: DRC and Tunisia Strengthen Trade and Investment Ties
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tunisia have agreed to boost trade and intensify bilateral investments during the Tunisia-DRC Business Forum held in Kinshasa.
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Tunisia have agreed to boost trade and intensify bilateral investments during the Tunisia-DRC Business Forum held in Kinshasa.

The forum brought together 17 Tunisian companies and numerous Congolese business leaders to explore opportunities for collaboration. Mike Tambwe, Director General of ANAPEX, emphasized the importance of creating value chains to increase the visibility of “Made in DRC” products on the Tunisian market.

Minister of Foreign Trade Julien Paluku encouraged Tunisian investors to form mutually beneficial partnerships with Congolese private enterprises, highlighting the potential for growth in key sectors such as technologies, innovation, and agro-industry.

The Tunisian ambassador to the DRC, Mahrez Ferchichi, reaffirmed the willingness of Tunisian entrepreneurs to invest in these sectors, a move welcomed by the Federal Economic Council (CEF), which noted that the DRC remains among Tunisia's main trading partners.

title_en: Geneva: Prime Minister Suminwa Leads Strategic Meeting on Congolese Mineral Traceability
excerpt_en: Geneva, November 20, 2025 - The transparency and traceability of critical minerals from eastern DRC were at the center of a high-level roundtable convened by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa at the Henri Dunant Centre for…
body_en:
Geneva, November 20, 2025 - The transparency and traceability of critical minerals from eastern DRC were at the center of a high-level roundtable convened by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa at the Henri Dunant Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue.

The meeting brought together international investors, development partners, and representatives of major global mining companies to design a strengthened system for tracking minerals from extraction to export. The initiative aims to curb smuggling of minerals to neighboring countries and enhance the DRC’s credibility in mining governance.

Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba denounced ongoing hypocrisy surrounding the current trade, highlighting the urgent need for accountability and structured oversight. Alexandre Liebeskind of the Henri Dunant Centre emphasized that improved traceability could transform Congolese resources into a driver of regional stability, development, and lasting peace.

title: Mongala: Vice-Governor Cédric Ayaka Kuma Dismissed by Provincial Assembly
excerpt: Mongala, November 17, 2025 - The Mongala Provincial Assembly voted to remove Vice-Governor Cédric Ayaka Kuma from office.
title_en: Mongala: Vice-Governor Cédric Ayaka Kuma Dismissed by Provincial Assembly
excerpt_en: Mongala, November 17, 2025 - The Mongala Provincial Assembly voted to remove Vice-Governor Cédric Ayaka Kuma from office.
body_en:
Mongala, November 17, 2025 - The Mongala Provincial Assembly voted to remove Vice-Governor Cédric Ayaka Kuma from office. The motion, approved by 19 assembly members, cited allegations of fraud, breach of trust, and forgery, and was supported by a court ruling declaring the position vacant and ordering partial elections.

Mr. Kuma, who is currently in Kinshasa for professional reasons, expressed surprise at the decision and has not yet officially responded to the accusations or the removal process.

Mr. Kuma, who is currently in Kinshasa for professional reasons, expressed surprise at the decision and has not yet officially responded to the accusations or the removal process.

title_en: DRC: Martin Fayulu Calls for Inclusive National Dialogue, Warns of Balkanization Risks
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - Opposition leader Martin Fayulu, head of the Lamuka coalition, renewed his call for an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - Opposition leader Martin Fayulu, head of the Lamuka coalition, renewed his call for an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo. He warned that the country is at a critical juncture, facing what he described as a risk of balkanization.

Fayulu criticized the recent economic integration agreement signed between the DRC and Rwanda under U.S. mediation, labeling it a potential threat to national sovereignty. Addressing young Congolese, he urged vigilance and active participation in defending the country’s territorial integrity.

“No external agreement can precede the reconciliation of the children of Congo,” Fayulu emphasized, adding that “a united people will never be defeated.”

Belgrade, November 28, 2025 - During a meeting in Belgrade, Presidents Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Aleksandar Vučić of Serbia reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation between the two nations in key sectors such as agriculture, defense, education, health, and youth development.

The leaders discussed initiatives including scholarships for Congolese students, technology transfer, training, modernization of agricultural practices, and the enhancement of military cooperation.

title: Kinshasa: UN Urges Greater Youth Participation in Decision-Making
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The UN Assistant Secretary-General for Youth, Felipe Paullier, called on Congolese authorities on November 25, 2025, to create more formal spaces for youth participation in decision-making bodies.
title_en: Kinshasa: UN Urges Greater Youth Participation in Decision-Making
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The UN Assistant Secretary-General for Youth, Felipe Paullier, called on Congolese authorities on November 25, 2025, to create more formal spaces for youth participation in decision-making bodies.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The UN Assistant Secretary-General for Youth, Felipe Paullier, called on Congolese authorities on November 25, 2025, to create more formal spaces for youth participation in decision-making bodies. The appeal came during a meeting with the Minister of Youth, Grâce Kutino.

Highlighting a global gap between demographics-50% of the population under 30-and the low representation of young people in governance, Paullier urged joint efforts to institutionalize youth participation, remove barriers to political life, and facilitate integration into the civil service.

This initiative follows recommendations made in December 2024 by the Group of Experts for Resolution 2250, which encouraged the appointment of young people to positions of responsibility in the DRC.

title: DRC: National Mobilization Against Violence Against Women, Between Digital Action and Community Engagement
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, commemorated annually on November 25 in honor of the Mirabal sisters, the Ministry of Gender, Family and Children…
title_en: DRC: National Mobilization Against Violence Against Women, Between Digital Action and Community Engagement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, commemorated annually on November 25 in honor of the Mirabal sisters, the Ministry of Gender, Family and Children…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, commemorated annually on November 25 in honor of the Mirabal sisters, the Ministry of Gender, Family and Children launched a national awareness campaign targeting digital violence against women and girls. This initiative, conducted in partnership with UNFPA, runs until December 10 as part of the 16 Days of Activism.

During the launch, Minister Micheline Ombae urged young people to use digital tools responsibly, emphasizing that they should "unite, not divide," while denouncing online harassment, hate speech, and other forms of digital abuse. UNFPA representative Ikoli Mireille highlighted the necessity of strict law enforcement to hold perpetrators accountable, particularly in a context where over 460,000 cases of gender-based violence were recorded in the DRC between 2021 and 2024.

In addition, Doctors Without Borders (MSF) provided medical care to more than 25,000 survivors of sexual violence in 2023, including over 17,000 cases in North Kivu from January to May 2024. These statistics underscore the persistent severity of gender-based violence in the country.

On November 25, 2025, multiple marches and demonstrations were organized nationwide by women’s rights organizations, focusing on denouncing digital violence, promoting citizen engagement, and reinforcing the broader fight against all forms of gender-based violence, from sexual assault to forced marriage.

This campaign represents a dual approach, combining digital advocacy with community mobilization, aiming to raise public awareness, pressure authorities, and foster collective action to protect women and girls across the DRC.

title: Crisis in Eastern DRC: Kagame Accuses Kinshasa, DRC Firmly Rejects Allegations
excerpt: Kigali/Kinshasa - On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame accused the Congolese government of refusing to assume its responsibilities in managing the security crisis in eastern DRC.
title_en: Crisis in Eastern DRC: Kagame Accuses Kinshasa, DRC Firmly Rejects Allegations
excerpt_en: Kigali/Kinshasa - On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame accused the Congolese government of refusing to assume its responsibilities in managing the security crisis in eastern DRC.
body_en:
Kigali/Kinshasa - On Thursday, November 27, 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame accused the Congolese government of refusing to assume its responsibilities in managing the security crisis in eastern DRC. He specifically criticized Kinshasa for refusing dialogue with the M23, an armed group accused by the United Nations of receiving support from the Rwandan army, a claim Kigali denies.

Concerning the reopening of Goma airport, sought for humanitarian reasons, Kagame stated that the decision should be discussed “directly with the rebels who control the city.”

Kinshasa immediately rejected these remarks, reminding Rwanda of its obligation to respect bilateral agreements. Through government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, the DRC referred to Paul Kagame as the “father” of the M23, underscoring the seriousness of the accusations.

These verbal tensions occur amid ongoing instability in the region, despite diplomatic efforts deployed in Washington and Doha to stabilize the eastern DRC.

body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka inaugurated the 11th Makutano International Business Forum, a high-level event bringing together public decision-makers, investors, economic experts, and other stakeholders for a two-day discussion on the future of the Congolese economy.

The forum, themed "Contracts in Congo: Time to Choose," aims to establish structural guidelines to foster a more competitive, connected, and sovereign economy. Discussions focused on four key sectors: governance, mining, energy, and transportation, addressing both challenges and opportunities for economic growth.

The initiative, launched by Nicole Sulu, received strong support from the Prime Minister, who highlighted the importance of diversifying the Congolese economy and enhancing local transformation, particularly in the mining sector, to reduce dependency on raw exports and strengthen domestic value chains.

The forum is expected to produce actionable recommendations that will guide public policy, investment strategies, and regulatory frameworks, reinforcing the DRC’s drive toward economic sovereignty and sustainable development.

title: Kinshasa Officially Launches DRC-UK Trade Partnership
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United Kingdom officially inaugurated their new trade partnership, aimed at strengthening bilateral commerce and diversifying the…
title_en: Kinshasa Officially Launches DRC-UK Trade Partnership
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United Kingdom officially inaugurated their new trade partnership, aimed at strengthening bilateral commerce and diversifying the…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United Kingdom officially inaugurated their new trade partnership, aimed at strengthening bilateral commerce and diversifying the Congolese economy.

The agreement allows Congolese spices, coffee, and cocoa to access the British market duty-free, marking a major step in reducing reliance on the mining sector. The ceremony was presided over by the Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku, and UK Ambassador Alyson King, highlighting the strategic importance of this initiative for both nations.

The partnership seeks to increase bilateral trade from $100 million to $1.5 billion by 2030, with 99.8% of Congolese exports now eligible for duty-free access to the United Kingdom. The inauguration also launched a trade support program, backed by the International Trade Centre, TradeMark Africa, and the British Standards Institute (BSI), designed to assist Congolese businesses in meeting international standards and maximizing the benefits of the agreement.

Minister Paluku emphasized that this program will be implemented nationally to support export capacity building, market competitiveness, and the sustainable diversification of the Congolese economy.

title_en: DRC: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Highlights Domestic Debt Management at Makutano 2025
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - At the opening of the 11th Makutano International Business Forum on Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa addressed domestic debt management, placing it at the center of the…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - At the opening of the 11th Makutano International Business Forum on Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa addressed domestic debt management, placing it at the center of the government's economic priorities.

The Prime Minister announced a new plan to distinguish between legitimate and fictitious claims, clarifying that only debts arising from regular purchase procedures would be honored, while “fictitious cases” would not be settled. She acknowledged that the conflict in eastern DRC had disrupted repayment schedules but reassured participants that the State is committed to fulfilling obligations to genuine creditors.

Ms. Suminwa emphasized that this initiative aligns with broader efforts to strengthen transparency, public finance reform, and economic governance, aiming to restore confidence among domestic and international partners. The announcement comes as the DRC prepares an ambitious budget for 2026, seeking to balance fiscal responsibility with investment in key sectors.

title: AU-EU Summit: Félix Tshisekedi Advocates Respect for Sovereignty in Strategic Partnership
excerpt: Luanda, Angola - At the conclusion of the 7th African Union-European Union Summit on November 25, 2025, leaders from both organizations adopted a declaration aiming to strengthen their strategic partnership.
title_en: AU-EU Summit: Félix Tshisekedi Advocates Respect for Sovereignty in Strategic Partnership
excerpt_en: Luanda, Angola - At the conclusion of the 7th African Union-European Union Summit on November 25, 2025, leaders from both organizations adopted a declaration aiming to strengthen their strategic partnership.
body_en:
Luanda, Angola - At the conclusion of the 7th African Union-European Union Summit on November 25, 2025, leaders from both organizations adopted a declaration aiming to strengthen their strategic partnership. The agreement prioritizes the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), the reform of international debt architecture, the digital transition, and access to clean energy for 100 million Africans by 2030. It also emphasizes sustainable agricultural development, in line with the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme (CAADP).

The discussions highlighted European initiatives such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the EU Regulation on Deforestation and Forest Reduction (RDEB), which are viewed by African leaders as potentially restrictive for exports.

Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi made a strong statement, denouncing any disregard for sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference. He stressed that no economic or migration program could succeed without addressing the human tragedies that continue to affect the continent.

The summit’s pragmatic approach now sets the stage for a critical test: the implementation of these commitments ahead of the next meeting scheduled for 2028, marking a decisive moment in Africa-EU relations.

excerpt: Isiro, Haut-Uele - A motion of censure targeting Governor Jean Bakomito was officially submitted on Wednesday, November 26, 2025, to the Provincial Assembly of Haut-Uele, despite a national directive from Kinshasa…
title_en: Haut-Uele: Motion of Censure Filed Against Governor Bakomito Despite Kinshasa’s Suspension Call
excerpt_en: Isiro, Haut-Uele - A motion of censure targeting Governor Jean Bakomito was officially submitted on Wednesday, November 26, 2025, to the Provincial Assembly of Haut-Uele, despite a national directive from Kinshasa…
body_en:
Isiro, Haut-Uele - A motion of censure targeting Governor Jean Bakomito was officially submitted on Wednesday, November 26, 2025, to the Provincial Assembly of Haut-Uele, despite a national directive from Kinshasa calling for the suspension of such initiatives to ensure institutional stability.

The four members of parliament behind the motion accuse the governor of “blatant cronyism”, showing favoritism toward a small circle, and “manifest incompetence” in public administration. They further criticize him for deviating from the governance vision promoted by President Félix Tshisekedi and for being frequently absent from the provincial capital, Isiro.

Although the central government urged a pause on motions and petitions to avoid destabilizing the provinces, the Haut-Uele legislators maintain that their action meets all legal conditions of admissibility, noting that at least nine provinces in the country are currently experiencing similar attempts to remove provincial executives.

This move underscores growing tensions between provincial assemblies and the central government, raising questions about governance, accountability, and political stability in the DRC’s provinces.

title: DRC: Senate Adopts Banking Reform, Joint Committee to Resolve Remaining Differences
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 27, 2025, the Senate adopted on second reading the bill reforming the activities and oversight of credit institutions, in a version differing from that passed by the National Assembly.
title_en: DRC: Senate Adopts Banking Reform, Joint Committee to Resolve Remaining Differences
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On November 27, 2025, the Senate adopted on second reading the bill reforming the activities and oversight of credit institutions, in a version differing from that passed by the National Assembly.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On November 27, 2025, the Senate adopted on second reading the bill reforming the activities and oversight of credit institutions, in a version differing from that passed by the National Assembly.

The Senate’s version notably reduces the compliance period stipulated in Article 190 from 60 months to 36 months, compared with the 120-month deadline originally proposed by MP Olivier Katuala. The reform, initially submitted on September 16, 2024, aims to modernize the banking framework, focusing on governance, competence of decision-making bodies, and external audits, while addressing constraints related to capital dilution, which were deemed incompatible with African standards.

After its adoption by the National Assembly on June 15, 2025 (354 votes in favor out of 363), and now by the Senate (73 votes for, 1 abstention), a joint committee will be convened to harmonize the two versions. Should an agreement not be reached, the Constitution stipulates that the Assembly’s text will take precedence before submission to the President of the Republic.

Fayulu emphasized that the Congolese people have a right to know the contents of the agreement before any official signing. The call underscores rising political tensions and growing demands for transparency regarding bilateral negotiations that are expected to impact the security and stability of eastern DRC.

Fayulu emphasized that the Congolese people have a right to know the contents of the agreement before any official signing. The call underscores rising political tensions and growing demands for transparency regarding bilateral negotiations that are expected to impact the security and stability of eastern DRC.

Kinshasa, DRC - On Monday, November 24, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi appointed Bienvenu Ilambo as Special Advisor for Communication through a presidential decree read on national television.

In his new role, Ilambo is tasked with coordinating all communications for the Head of State and the Presidency. The President’s spokesperson, his deputy, and all communication services will report directly to him.

Holding the rank of Minister, Ilambo will lead a team composed of five assistants, seven research officers, a special advisor, a private secretary, two bodyguards, an administrative secretary, two data entry operators, and two mailroom employees.

This appointment reflects the President’s focus on strengthening communication strategies and ensuring a cohesive messaging structure across the Presidency.

excerpt: Kisangani, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the acting governor of Tshopo, Didier Lomoyo Iteku, presented the draft 2026 provincial budget to the Provincial Assembly.

Kisangani, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, the acting governor of Tshopo, Didier Lomoyo Iteku, presented the draft 2026 provincial budget to the Provincial Assembly. The budget totals 420.4 billion Congolese francs and is reported as balanced between revenue and expenditure.

The budget prioritizes three main areas: strengthening security through measures to combat urban crime; rehabilitating infrastructure, notably the road linking the Canon roundabout to the Congo Palace, supporting presidential modernization projects in Kisangani; and consolidating good governance and institutional stability.

The President of the Provincial Assembly, Mattheus Kanga, emphasized that a thorough review of the document is expected during the upcoming September session, ensuring alignment with provincial and national development objectives.

Matadi, DRC - During an inter-institutional meeting held on Wednesday, November 26, 2025, the Kongo-Central Provincial Assembly denounced the persistent lack of budgetary support for the provincial executive, which has hindered the execution of its duties over the past several months.

The discussions also reviewed the progress of major provincial projects and led to the adoption of a moratorium temporarily suspending motions and petitions to ease political tensions.

The rapporteur, Billy Ntunga, stressed that the meeting sought to clarify misunderstandings between institutions, noting that the province is not in crisis but is experiencing political misunderstandings that fuel a climate of mistrust.

Kamina, DRC - The Haut-Lomami Provincial Assembly finalized its leadership on Thursday, November 27, 2025, electing Jean Tayari as president and Idriss Nsenga as treasurer, both representing the Sacred Union party.

This renewal follows the removal of their predecessors a month earlier, who were accused of embezzling salaries meant for provincial deputies, parliamentary assistants, and administrative staff for the months of March 2024 and May 2025, allegations detailed in a memorandum submitted to the Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior.

Observers consider this election a significant step toward reinforcing governance and institutional stability in Haut-Lomami.

title: Kinshasa Rejects Paul Kagame’s Accusations, Reaffirms Bilateral Commitments
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government responded firmly to Rwandan President Paul Kagame, who accused Kinshasa of "refusing to assume its responsibilities" in addressing the security crisis in eastern DRC.
title_en: Kinshasa Rejects Paul Kagame’s Accusations, Reaffirms Bilateral Commitments
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government responded firmly to Rwandan President Paul Kagame, who accused Kinshasa of "refusing to assume its responsibilities" in addressing the security crisis in eastern DRC.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government responded firmly to Rwandan President Paul Kagame, who accused Kinshasa of "refusing to assume its responsibilities" in addressing the security crisis in eastern DRC.

At a press conference on Thursday, November 27, 2025, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya emphasized that Rwanda remains bound by bilateral commitments under the Washington and Doha processes. Muyaya also referred to Paul Kagame as the "creator of the M23," the rebel group active in the region, and rejected any notion of negotiating with the armed movement.

The Congolese government reaffirmed that Rwanda must respect existing agreements, particularly after Kagame suggested that the reopening of Goma airport be discussed "directly with the rebels." These remarks come amid ongoing tensions between the two countries.

title: DRC: Prime Minister Suminwa Unveils 2026 Budget Prioritizing Security, Economy, and Social Protection
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa presented the Democratic Republic of Congo’s 2026 draft budget to the National Assembly, totaling 59.021 billion Congolese francs (approximately US$25…
title_en: DRC: Prime Minister Suminwa Unveils 2026 Budget Prioritizing Security, Economy, and Social Protection
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa presented the Democratic Republic of Congo’s 2026 draft budget to the National Assembly, totaling 59.021 billion Congolese francs (approximately US$25…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa presented the Democratic Republic of Congo’s 2026 draft budget to the National Assembly, totaling 59.021 billion Congolese francs (approximately US$25 billion), marking a 16% increase compared to the revised 2025 budget.

The budget prioritizes national security and defense (11.896 billion), economic development including infrastructure, agriculture, and industry (11.972 billion), education (6.657 billion), health (5.579 billion), and social protection (1.211 billion).

Suminwa detailed the overall allocation: a general budget of 53.654 billion, supplementary budgets of 962 billion, and special accounts totaling 4.404 billion. She emphasized that the funds are intended to strengthen military capabilities, drive economic growth, and improve social services, while remaining adaptable to evolving macroeconomic conditions.

title: DRC Mining Sector Attracts $2 Billion in Annual Foreign Investment
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 19, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector continues to attract significant foreign investment, with an average of $2 billion per year over the past two decades, according to Deputy…
title_en: DRC Mining Sector Attracts $2 Billion in Annual Foreign Investment
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 19, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector continues to attract significant foreign investment, with an average of $2 billion per year over the past two decades, according to Deputy…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 19, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector continues to attract significant foreign investment, with an average of $2 billion per year over the past two decades, according to Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba.

He highlighted that this investment has enabled the country to surpass 3 million tons of copper production, making the DRC the second-largest copper producer in the world.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Emir of Qatar’s visit to Kinshasa, Mukoko Samba encouraged Qatari investors to prioritize integrated regional projects and enhance internal connectivity and logistics to maximize the country’s economic potential. The remarks followed the signing of letters of intent with Al Mansour Holding for a $21 billion investment portfolio, underscoring the continued attractiveness of the Congolese mining sector to international investors.

title: DRC: FEC Requests Postponement of Standardized Invoice Implementation
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - The Federation of Congolese Businesses (FEC) has requested a postponement of the rollout of the standardized invoice system, originally scheduled for December 1, 2025.
title_en: DRC: FEC Requests Postponement of Standardized Invoice Implementation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - The Federation of Congolese Businesses (FEC) has requested a postponement of the rollout of the standardized invoice system, originally scheduled for December 1, 2025.
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - The Federation of Congolese Businesses (FEC) has requested a postponement of the rollout of the standardized invoice system, originally scheduled for December 1, 2025.

The FEC cited technical and security challenges with the platform, including the absence of a multi-user system for businesses with multiple points of sale. Thierry Ngoy Kasumba, Director General of the FEC, presented these concerns during a tax information session organized by the General Directorate of Taxes (DGI).

The DGI, for its part, encourages businesses to attend support sessions and make use of the assistance program in place. Authorities reiterated that the reform aims to modernize VAT collection, strengthen transaction transparency, and combat tax fraud.

title: DRC: Government Sets Strict Schedule for Resumption of Cobalt Exports
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has announced the imminent resumption of cobalt exports, following a suspension that began on February 22, 2025 and was extended until October 15, 2025.
title_en: DRC: Government Sets Strict Schedule for Resumption of Cobalt Exports
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has announced the imminent resumption of cobalt exports, following a suspension that began on February 22, 2025 and was extended until October 15, 2025.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has announced the imminent resumption of cobalt exports, following a suspension that began on February 22, 2025 and was extended until October 15, 2025. The temporary halt had been imposed to address a price collapse caused by overproduction in the global market.

Effective October 16, 2025, the government lifted the ban and implemented a quota system, allowing the export of 18,125 tons of cobalt by the end of the year. The allocation is 3,625 tons for October, and 7,250 tons each for November and December.

Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, confirmed that exports will resume from November 27, 2025, emphasizing that the new policy-including an annual ceiling of 96,600 tons starting in 2026-is designed to protect national revenues, stabilize international prices, and strengthen the DRC’s sovereignty over this strategic mineral resource.

The government’s move underscores the DRC’s commitment to responsible resource management while supporting the stability of the global cobalt market, a critical input for electric vehicles and high-tech batteries.

title: Kolwezi Plane Accident: All Passengers Safe Despite Fire
excerpt: Kolwezi, November 17, 2025 - An Embraer ERJ-145 operated by Airjet Angola veered off the runway and caught fire at Kolwezi Airport, causing significant material damage.
title_en: Kolwezi Plane Accident: All Passengers Safe Despite Fire
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, November 17, 2025 - An Embraer ERJ-145 operated by Airjet Angola veered off the runway and caught fire at Kolwezi Airport, causing significant material damage.
body_en:
Kolwezi, November 17, 2025 - An Embraer ERJ-145 operated by Airjet Angola veered off the runway and caught fire at Kolwezi Airport, causing significant material damage. The aircraft was carrying 26 passengers and 3 crew members, including Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba on an emergency mission to Lualaba following the Kalando mining disaster.

Officials confirmed no casualties, as all occupants were evacuated safely before the fire engulfed the plane. The Permanent Bureau of Investigation and Analysis for Aviation Accidents (BPEA) has been dispatched to determine the cause of the accident and assign responsibility.

title_en: DRC Hosts Over 500,000 Refugees as UNHCR Steps Up Reintegration Efforts

body_en:
Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - The Democratic Republic of Congo currently hosts nearly 510,000 refugees, primarily from Rwanda and other Central African countries, Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde, Director of the UNHCR Regional Bureau, announced following a meeting with Prime Minister Judith Suminwa.

The UN agency, which also registers around 1.2 million Congolese refugees abroad, including 83,000 in Rwanda and over 600,000 in Uganda, intends to intensify programs facilitating the return, social, and economic reintegration of displaced populations. These efforts will be conducted in close coordination with the Congolese government and aligned with the existing legal framework governing refugee protection and reintegration.

excerpt: Nkonko, Kasai-Central, November 17, 2025 - The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in partnership with provincial authorities and local organizations, handed over 800 land titles and 78 houses to…
title_en: Kasai-Central: UNHCR Provides Land Titles and Housing to Returning Angolan Refugees
excerpt_en: Nkonko, Kasai-Central, November 17, 2025 - The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in partnership with provincial authorities and local organizations, handed over 800 land titles and 78 houses to…
body_en:
Nkonko, Kasai-Central, November 17, 2025 - The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in partnership with provincial authorities and local organizations, handed over 800 land titles and 78 houses to returning Angolan refugees in Nkonko, Kasai-Central province.

These former refugees had fled the Kamuina Nsapu militia conflict between 2016 and 2017. The ceremony was attended by UNHCR Regional Director for West and Central Africa, Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde, and the provincial governor.

The initiative is designed to guarantee land tenure security and provide decent housing for the returning families, promoting sustainable reintegration while contributing to peacebuilding and community empowerment in a region long affected by conflict.

Kinshasa, November 18, 2025 - President Félix Tshisekedi inaugurated the National Roundtable on Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship in Kinshasa, a platform designed to create professional opportunities and support the private initiatives of young Congolese.

The forum brings together institutional, economic, and social stakeholders to develop unified strategies and implement concrete, high-impact measures.

title: Sankuru River: Whaling Boat Capsizes, Around Fifty Survivors
excerpt: Ilebo, Kasai Province, November 17, 2025 - A whaling boat capsized on the Sankuru River on Monday, leaving around fifty survivors out of the 120 passengers on board.
title_en: Sankuru River: Whaling Boat Capsizes, Around Fifty Survivors
excerpt_en: Ilebo, Kasai Province, November 17, 2025 - A whaling boat capsized on the Sankuru River on Monday, leaving around fifty survivors out of the 120 passengers on board.
body_en:
Ilebo, Kasai Province, November 17, 2025 - A whaling boat capsized on the Sankuru River on Monday, leaving around fifty survivors out of the 120 passengers on board.

Local civil society sources reported that the vessel, which had departed from Kole, was overloaded with passengers and cargo. The boat struck a tree trunk near Dibulansenba, close to its confluence with the Kasai River, in an area known for dangerous whirlpools.

Rescue efforts are ongoing as authorities continue search operations for the missing passengers.

excerpt: Shabunda, South Kivu, November 18, 2025 - Torrential rains accompanied by strong winds caused widespread destruction on Wednesday in the Shabunda territory.
title_en: Shabunda: Torrential Rains Destroy Nearly 1,500 Homes
excerpt_en: Shabunda, South Kivu, November 18, 2025 - Torrential rains accompanied by strong winds caused widespread destruction on Wednesday in the Shabunda territory.
body_en:
Shabunda, South Kivu, November 18, 2025 - Torrential rains accompanied by strong winds caused widespread destruction on Wednesday in the Shabunda territory. Authorities report that around 1,500 homes were destroyed, while public infrastructure, including Kisubi and Mankulu primary schools and the Congolese National Police (PNC) detention center, suffered significant damage.

The Bangoma group in the Bakisi chiefdom was the hardest hit, with nearly 800 brick houses and 600 huts made of branches destroyed. A ten-year-old child was injured, and several families were forced to spend the night outdoors.

Local organizations, including the New Civil Society of Congo (NSCC), have issued an urgent appeal to the government and NGOs for humanitarian assistance for the affected families.

title_en: Beni: Children’s Rights Under Threat Amid Insecurity and Displacement
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu, November 20, 2025 - On the occasion of International Children’s Day, the Gender, Family and Childhood Office in Beni sounded the alarm over the worsening situation for children in the region, who are…
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu, November 20, 2025 - On the occasion of International Children’s Day, the Gender, Family and Childhood Office in Beni sounded the alarm over the worsening situation for children in the region, who are severely impacted by ongoing armed violence and mass population displacement.

According to Ruth Sabuni, head of the office, children face violence, rape, economic exploitation, abandonment, and forced recruitment by armed groups. Access to health services, nutrition, and quality education remains extremely limited.

Despite interventions by MONUSCO and other child protection partners, enormous challenges persist in ensuring respect for the fundamental rights of children in this crisis zone.

title_en: West and Central Africa: UNHCR Warns Over 19 Million People in Distress
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - During a six-day mission to the Democratic Republic of Congo, UNHCR Regional Director Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde raised the alarm about the worsening humanitarian situation in West and Central…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - During a six-day mission to the Democratic Republic of Congo, UNHCR Regional Director Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde raised the alarm about the worsening humanitarian situation in West and Central Africa, where an estimated 5 million refugees and 14 million internally displaced persons urgently need assistance.

Gnon-Konde highlighted that funding shortages, particularly a 60% reduction in U.S. contributions, have forced the closure of 30 UNHCR offices in the region, including several in the DRC. He called on international donors to renew their commitments and support efforts to restore the dignity and survival of affected populations.

body_en:
Kinshasa, November 22, 2025 - During an inspection of the Kinshasa Bypass construction site, Secretary General for Infrastructure Georges Koshi announced that 105 landowners will receive compensation in the project’s second phase, totaling US$4 million.

Koshi expressed satisfaction with the progress of the works and the consensus reached with residents, assuring that no one would be left behind, in line with presidential directives. Following 99 payments in the first phase, the inter-ministerial expropriation commission continues to assist families without property titles to regularize their claims.

The 72-kilometer Rocades road, financed under the Sino-Congolese program and executed by CREC 4 and CREC 8 under ACGT supervision, aims to permanently ease congestion in Kinshasa.

excerpt_en: Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga, November 2025 - Heavy rains in Haut-Katanga province have caused flooding, landslides, and structural collapses, affecting more than 400 homes in Kampemba, Katuba, Kambove, and Kasenga.
body_en:
Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga, November 2025 - Heavy rains in Haut-Katanga province have caused flooding, landslides, and structural collapses, affecting more than 400 homes in Kampemba, Katuba, Kambove, and Kasenga.

Although no fatalities have been reported, hundreds of families are now homeless and exposed to harsh conditions, facing significant property losses. Kingombe Faray Lazare, head of the disaster management and humanitarian emergency office, called for urgent support from provincial and national authorities and emphasized the need for preventive measures, including road maintenance and dredging waterways, as the rainy season continues.

title: South Kivu: Civil Society Denounces Massacres and Calls for International Intervention
excerpt: Bukavu, November 28, 2025 - Civil society organizations and socio-political actors in South Kivu condemned deadly operations allegedly carried out by a coalition of FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) soldiers, Wazalendo…
title_en: South Kivu: Civil Society Denounces Massacres and Calls for International Intervention
excerpt_en: Bukavu, November 28, 2025 - Civil society organizations and socio-political actors in South Kivu condemned deadly operations allegedly carried out by a coalition of FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) soldiers, Wazalendo…
body_en:
Bukavu, November 28, 2025 - Civil society organizations and socio-political actors in South Kivu condemned deadly operations allegedly carried out by a coalition of FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) soldiers, Wazalendo militias, FDLR (Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda), Mai-Mai militias, and elements of the Burundian army.

The coalition is accused of targeting civilians in multiple areas of the province, including the massacre of Banyamulenge community members in Mikenge, the bombing of Minembwe airfield, the bombing of Nzibira from Kisangani, and violence against young Banyamulenge in the Uvira highlands, as well as massacres in Luvungi.

These organizations argue that such acts constitute violations of international humanitarian law and urge humanitarian and human rights organizations to intervene on behalf of the victims. They also criticize the military strategy implemented by the central government under President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo.

Finally, the statement calls on the inhabitants of South Kivu to unite around a federalist ideal, aiming to build a strong nation that respects the rights of every citizen.

title: North Kivu: Road Rehabilitation and Airport Expansion Project Launched in Walikale
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Governor Major General Kakule Somo Evariste inaugurated a road rehabilitation project in Walikale territory, targeting long-isolated areas.
title_en: North Kivu: Road Rehabilitation and Airport Expansion Project Launched in Walikale
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Governor Major General Kakule Somo Evariste inaugurated a road rehabilitation project in Walikale territory, targeting long-isolated areas.
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Tuesday, November 25, 2025, Governor Major General Kakule Somo Evariste inaugurated a road rehabilitation project in Walikale territory, targeting long-isolated areas. The initiative covers the Walikale-Kibuwa road (85 km), Walikale-Itebero road, and several avenues in the town of Walikale, including the construction of eight bridges.

Funded by the North Kivu Agricultural Sector Support Project (PASA N-K) and executed by four companies, the eight-month project aims to improve transportation of agricultural products to urban centers and reduce isolation caused by the M23 insurgency, which has pressured local communities for nearly a year.

In parallel, the governor announced the expansion of the Kigoma airfield runway from 1,113 to 1,800 meters, a strategic infrastructure investment supported by the provincial government. Residents see these projects as a sign of hope for economic development and improved connectivity in conflict-affected North Kivu.

title: Kinshasa: Martyrs Stadium Staff Protest Over Thirteen Years of Back Pay
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Staff at Martyrs Stadium staged a protest on Tuesday, November 25, demanding thirteen years of unpaid salaries, estimated at 60,000 Congolese francs (US$26) per person.
title_en: Kinshasa: Martyrs Stadium Staff Protest Over Thirteen Years of Back Pay
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Staff at Martyrs Stadium staged a protest on Tuesday, November 25, demanding thirteen years of unpaid salaries, estimated at 60,000 Congolese francs (US$26) per person.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Staff at Martyrs Stadium staged a protest on Tuesday, November 25, demanding thirteen years of unpaid salaries, estimated at 60,000 Congolese francs (US$26) per person.

Protesters gathered at both Martyrs Stadium and Tata Raphaël Stadium, where they burned tires, vandalized archives, and erected barricades. The unrest disrupted several activities at the sports facilities, including two LINAFOOT matches scheduled for Wednesday, November 26: OC Renaissance vs. AS Maniema Union and AS Vita Club vs. Anges Verts.

Authorities have yet to respond, leaving employees frustrated and the sports schedule in disarray.

title: DRC: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Equal Opportunities in Youth Employment
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has reiterated its commitment to ensuring equitable access to decent employment for all young people.
title_en: DRC: Government Reaffirms Commitment to Equal Opportunities in Youth Employment
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has reiterated its commitment to ensuring equitable access to decent employment for all young people.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has reiterated its commitment to ensuring equitable access to decent employment for all young people. Minister of Entrepreneurship, Justin Kalumba, made this declaration on Wednesday, November 26, 2025, during a joint press conference with the Minister of Communication and Media.

Kalumba announced that the National Employment Office will implement a skills-based recruitment system, replacing practices previously influenced by nepotism, tribalism, or other forms of favoritism. This reform is designed to strengthen transparency, promote fairness in the labor market, and provide every young Congolese citizen with genuine opportunities to build a sustainable professional future.

The announcement underscores the government's broader efforts to empower youth, improve employment governance, and align labor practices with principles of meritocracy and equal opportunity across the DRC.

title: ADIS 2025: Raïssa Malu Champions Digital Transformation and STEM Education for Youth
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - At the opening roundtable of the African Digital Innovation Summit (ADIS 2025), Minister of State Raïssa Malu highlighted the strides made in the digital transformation of the Congolese education system…
title_en: ADIS 2025: Raïssa Malu Champions Digital Transformation and STEM Education for Youth
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - At the opening roundtable of the African Digital Innovation Summit (ADIS 2025), Minister of State Raïssa Malu highlighted the strides made in the digital transformation of the Congolese education system…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - At the opening roundtable of the African Digital Innovation Summit (ADIS 2025), Minister of State Raïssa Malu highlighted the strides made in the digital transformation of the Congolese education system, calling for an accelerated shift toward technology and innovation.

She praised the implementation of the e-diploma system and stressed the urgent need to guide young Congolese towards STEM fields to nurture a generation capable of driving African innovation. Minister Malu emphasized that “digital technology is an opportunity, not a threat”, warning that without appropriate education, social inequalities could worsen. She called for strengthened digital literacy and practical solutions addressing real needs.

Joined by Ministers Frédéric Kibassa Maliba and Julien Paluku, and moderated by Dominique Migisha, she underscored the role of digital technology in combating fraud, reducing processing times, and improving public services.

On the sidelines, a gala evening on November 24 at the Fleuve Congo Hotel celebrated Raïssa Malu as Digital Africa’s “Digital Champion 2025”, recognizing her reforms, including the integration of AI in national exam marking, the decentralization of digitization, the expansion of distance learning, and the introduction of electronic diplomas.

excerpt: Kinshasa-Gombe, November 18, 2025 - During the trial of the foiled October 16 robbery at Rawbank’s Victoire branch, prosecutors asked the military court to sentence Honorine Porsche, alleged mastermind, to life imprisonment.
title_en: Kinshasa: Life Sentence Sought in Rawbank Robbery Trial
excerpt_en: Kinshasa-Gombe, November 18, 2025 - During the trial of the foiled October 16 robbery at Rawbank’s Victoire branch, prosecutors asked the military court to sentence Honorine Porsche, alleged mastermind, to life imprisonment.
body_en:
Kinshasa-Gombe, November 18, 2025 - During the trial of the foiled October 16 robbery at Rawbank’s Victoire branch, prosecutors asked the military court to sentence Honorine Porsche, alleged mastermind, to life imprisonment. Her four co-defendants face the death penalty.

Rawbank and the Congolese state are seeking $5 million and $10 million in damages, respectively. Porsche’s defense team has contested the proceedings, citing irregularities, and plans to present these arguments during the closing statements. The hearings continued on November 19 with final arguments before the court delivers its verdict.

title_en: Kananga: 135 Military Magistrates Sworn In to Strengthen FARDC Justice System
excerpt_en: Kananga, November 20, 2025 - A total of 135 new military magistrates from the 2024-2025 class were officially sworn in, marking their integration into the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
body_en:
Kananga, November 20, 2025 - A total of 135 new military magistrates from the 2024-2025 class were officially sworn in, marking their integration into the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC). The ceremony was presided over by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita.

Trained at the Military Academy of the Officer Training School over nine months, the new magistrates pledged to uphold legal integrity, impartiality, and rigorous application of the law, particularly amid ongoing operations against armed groups such as the AFC/M23 coalition. They were called upon to embody discipline, loyalty, and equitable justice in performing their duties.

title: DRC: Two Continental Resolutions Recognizing the Congolese Genocide Presented to the ECC
excerpt: Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, formally presented two resolutions recognizing the genocide committed in the Democratic Republic of Congo to the President of the Church of…
title_en: DRC: Two Continental Resolutions Recognizing the Congolese Genocide Presented to the ECC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, formally presented two resolutions recognizing the genocide committed in the Democratic Republic of Congo to the President of the Church of…
body_en:
Kinshasa, November 20, 2025 - The Minister of Human Rights, Samuel Mbemba, formally presented two resolutions recognizing the genocide committed in the Democratic Republic of Congo to the President of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC), Reverend André Bokundoa. The documents were issued by the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights and African civil society organizations.

Welcoming the ECC’s commitment to disseminating these texts nationwide, Mbemba described this step as a significant breakthrough in the struggle that has lasted more than three decades for the recognition of atrocities attributed to Rwanda.

The Minister highlighted that this achievement was made possible by the sustained advocacy of President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, whose efforts helped bring the issue to the forefront of continental institutions. He urged the Congolese population to rally behind this initiative so that the perpetrators and masterminds of the genocide are eventually held accountable.

title: Kinshasa: Advocacy for Full Implementation of Law Eliminating Court Fees for Gender-Based Violence Victims
excerpt: On November 28, 2025, an advocacy workshop was held in Kinshasa as part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence.
title_en: Kinshasa: Advocacy for Full Implementation of Law Eliminating Court Fees for Gender-Based Violence Victims
excerpt_en: On November 28, 2025, an advocacy workshop was held in Kinshasa as part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence.
body_en:
On November 28, 2025, an advocacy workshop was held in Kinshasa as part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. The meeting brought together representatives from the judiciary, security services, government, and civil society to promote the effective implementation of the decree-law of September 11, 2023, which eliminates court fees for victims of gender-based violence.

Under the auspices of the Gender and Women's Rights Network, participants called for the removal of financial barriers to accessing justice, the training and capacity building of magistrates, and the dissemination of information about the law, particularly regarding new offenses such as forced marriage of widows, blackmail, and gender-based intimidation.

Authorities were urged to strengthen control mechanisms and provide adequate logistical resources to combat impunity and ensure better protection for women and girls across the DRC.

title: Kinshasa: 105 Residents Compensated Under Ring Road Project
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Interministerial Commission overseeing expropriations for the Ring Road project paid compensation on Tuesday, November 26 to 105 people affected by the planned route.
title_en: Kinshasa: 105 Residents Compensated Under Ring Road Project
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Interministerial Commission overseeing expropriations for the Ring Road project paid compensation on Tuesday, November 26 to 105 people affected by the planned route.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Interministerial Commission overseeing expropriations for the Ring Road project paid compensation on Tuesday, November 26 to 105 people affected by the planned route. Out of 3,442 registered cases, 200 have been processed.

The operation, conducted at the General Secretariat for Infrastructure in Lingwala, represents significant progress in freeing up land for the continuation of this strategic 72-kilometer project, executed by the Chinese companies CREC 4 and CREC 8 under the coordination of Agence Congolaise des Grands Travaux (ACGT).

Beneficiaries expressed satisfaction with the process, while the Commission urged other affected residents to remain patient, assuring them of rigorous and transparent handling of each case.

title_en: Rawbank Robbery: Honorine Porsche Sentenced to 10 Years of Hard Labor
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, the Kinshasa-Gombe Garrison Military Court handed down a sentence of ten years of hard labor and a fine of 300 million Congolese francs to Honorine Porsche, after finding…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, the Kinshasa-Gombe Garrison Military Court handed down a sentence of ten years of hard labor and a fine of 300 million Congolese francs to Honorine Porsche, after finding her guilty of armed robbery and acts of terrorism during the highly publicized Rawbank robbery.

In accordance with Article 7 of the Military Penal Code, Judge Freddy Eume imposed the maximum sentence due to the multiple offenses committed. The court acquitted the other defendants for lack of sufficient evidence.

The verdict comes amid widespread public concern over urban crime and is intended as a strong signal from the military justice system in the fight against insecurity in the DRC, demonstrating the authorities’ commitment to maintaining law and order.

title: North Kivu: Military Trial Opens Against 12 Defendants in Walikale
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, a military trial commenced in Walikale, with twelve defendants, including Wazalendo fighters and a private first class, appearing before the Beni garrison…
title_en: North Kivu: Military Trial Opens Against 12 Defendants in Walikale
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, a military trial commenced in Walikale, with twelve defendants, including Wazalendo fighters and a private first class, appearing before the Beni garrison…
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, DRC - On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, a military trial commenced in Walikale, with twelve defendants, including Wazalendo fighters and a private first class, appearing before the Beni garrison military court, sitting in a mobile courtroom.

According to Captain Kabeya Claude, presenting the indictment, the defendants are charged with illegal possession of weapons of war, rape of minors, participation in an insurrection, criminal conspiracy, and misappropriation of ammunition for acts committed between 2024 and May 2025.

The trial, initiated by Military Governor Somo Evariste and expected to last approximately two weeks, began with the identification of the defendants and the reading of charges. Authorities emphasize that the procedure is intended to be exemplary and deterrent, given the fragile security context in the region.

Local civil society, closely monitoring proceedings, highlighted that the assassination of one of its members in 2024 in Hombo is also included in this case, reflecting the trial’s broader significance for justice and accountability in North Kivu.
