title: Rwanda Signs New Aviation Cooperation Agreements With the UK and Panama
excerpt: Punta Cana, Dominican Republic - Rwanda has signed two new air transport cooperation agreements with the United Kingdom and Panama, expanding its international aviation partnerships.
title_en: Rwanda Signs New Aviation Cooperation Agreements With the UK and Panama
excerpt_en: Punta Cana, Dominican Republic - Rwanda has signed two new air transport cooperation agreements with the United Kingdom and Panama, expanding its international aviation partnerships.
body_en:
Punta Cana, Dominican Republic - Rwanda has signed two new air transport cooperation agreements with the United Kingdom and Panama, expanding its international aviation partnerships. The agreements were concluded on 11 November 2025 on the sidelines of the International Conference on the Development of Air Transport Services.

The accord with the United Kingdom was signed by Rwanda’s Ambassador to Canada and the Dominican Republic, Prosper Higiro, and Mark Bosly, the UK Government’s Head of Transport Services. A separate agreement with Panama was signed by Ambassador Higiro and Marcos Castillo Masis, Director General of the Civil Aviation Authority of Panama.

According to the Rwanda Civil Aviation Authority (RCAA), the Bilateral Air Services Agreements (BASAs) are expected to facilitate new air routes, improve connectivity, and expand opportunities for trade, tourism, and investment between Rwanda and the two countries.

"This agreement paves the way for increased cooperation in the aviation sector, opening up new opportunities for trade, tourism and investment, and supporting air travel and economic development through greater competition in the travel sector," the RCAA said.

BASAs typically define key operational parameters for airlines, including designated airports, flight frequency, passenger and cargo limits, pricing, and safety standards. The agreements give airlines from each country the right to operate passenger and other aviation services between the signatory nations.

Rwanda’s new partnerships are part of ongoing efforts to strengthen the country’s global aviation ties and support the long-term growth of its air transport sector.

title: Rwanda Named Best African Country for Tourism Infrastructure at African Tourism Awards
excerpt: London, United Kingdom - Rwanda has been honored as the African country with the best and most advanced tourism infrastructure at the 2025 African Tourism Awards, held in London on November 2.
title_en: Rwanda Named Best African Country for Tourism Infrastructure at African Tourism Awards
excerpt_en: London, United Kingdom - Rwanda has been honored as the African country with the best and most advanced tourism infrastructure at the 2025 African Tourism Awards, held in London on November 2.
body_en:
London, United Kingdom - Rwanda has been honored as the African country with the best and most advanced tourism infrastructure at the 2025 African Tourism Awards, held in London on November 2. The prestigious award recognizes countries, institutions, and individuals who have demonstrated excellence and innovation in promoting tourism across the continent.

Rwandan Ambassador to the UK, Johnston Busingye, announced the win, praising Rwanda’s “internationally renowned hotels, eco-lodges, and world-class conference and event facilities.” The recognition underscores Rwanda’s growing reputation as a premier destination for sustainable and luxury tourism in Africa.

Rwanda’s victory comes amid strong competition in several categories, including Best Country in Tourism and Best Park for Volcanoes National Park. The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) was also nominated in the Best Tourism Institution category, while Visit Rwanda competed in Best Tourism Development Programmes.

The award highlights Rwanda’s consistent investment in high-end hospitality and infrastructure, such as the Kigali Marriott Hotel, Kigali Serena Hotel, Radisson Blu Hotel & Kigali Convention Centre, and the soon-to-open Mövenpick Kigali. These developments have positioned Kigali as one of Africa’s leading hubs for international conferences and events.

Beyond the capital, the government has supported the development of luxury lodges in key tourism regions - including One&Only Gorilla’s Nest and Bisate Wilderness Lodge near Volcanoes National Park - offering visitors premium experiences that blend comfort with conservation.

According to the Rwanda Development Board, the country’s tourism sector generated $647 million in 2024, marking a 4.3% increase from the previous year. The growth was fueled by a 27% rise in gorilla tourism revenues and an 11% uptick in air travel. Rwanda welcomed over 1.36 million visitors and hosted 115 international conferences, attracting more than 52,000 participants and earning $84.8 million from conference tourism alone.

Major facilities such as the BK Arena, Amahoro Stadium, and the Kigali Convention Centre have also strengthened Rwanda’s position as a leading destination for global sports, cultural, and business events.

The African Tourism Awards, popularly known as the Balearica Awards, were established in 2017 and are organized by Africa Tourism Awards Ltd, a UK-based body that celebrates excellence and innovation in Africa’s tourism industry.

Rwanda’s recognition as the continent’s leader in tourism infrastructure affirms its status as a model for sustainable development and a benchmark for African destinations aiming to merge economic growth with environmental stewardship.

LONDON, UK - Rwanda is taking part in the World Travel Market (WTM) 2025, one of the world’s largest international tourism fairs, held in London from November 4 to 6, 2025. The East African nation is showcasing its unique natural attractions, diverse wildlife, and sustainable tourism initiatives to global industry leaders.

The Rwandan delegation includes representatives from the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), the Rwandan Embassy in the UK, RwandAir, and several private sector stakeholders such as Primates Safaris, Hermosa Life Tours, Wilderness, Blue Monkey Tours, Triple Legacy Travels, Kings Safaris, and Wildlife Tours.

Throughout the three-day fair, Rwandan representatives are engaging in business meetings and networking sessions aimed at promoting Rwanda as a premier eco-tourism destination. The country is particularly emphasizing its gorilla trekking experiences in Volcanoes National Park, its growing conference tourism, and its commitment to conservation-led travel.

By participating in WTM 2025, Rwanda aims to further expand its global partnerships and strengthen its position in the international tourism market.

title: Ivan Mbaraga Named Chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce in Rwanda
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - The American Chamber of Commerce in Rwanda (AmCham Rwanda) has appointed Ivan Mbaraga as the new Chairman of its Board of Directors, effective November 4, 2025.
title_en: Ivan Mbaraga Named Chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce in Rwanda
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - The American Chamber of Commerce in Rwanda (AmCham Rwanda) has appointed Ivan Mbaraga as the new Chairman of its Board of Directors, effective November 4, 2025.
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - The American Chamber of Commerce in Rwanda (AmCham Rwanda) has appointed Ivan Mbaraga as the new Chairman of its Board of Directors, effective November 4, 2025.

The appointment was announced as part of AmCham Rwanda’s renewed commitment to strengthening trade, investment, and cooperation between Rwanda and the United States.

Mbaraga, who currently serves as CEO of Oklahoma Christian University Rwanda Campus (OC Rwanda) and Director of Aspire Academy Bugesera, will lead the board for a two-year term. His mandate includes coordinating AmCham Rwanda’s members with government agencies, promoting bilateral trade, and advancing programs that support youth entrepreneurship and education-based investments.

The Chamber, which serves as a bridge between Rwandan and American businesses, aims to promote knowledge-driven investments and projects that create sustainable jobs. The new leadership team includes professionals from the business, education, and technology sectors.

Holding a Master’s degree in Organizational Leadership and Development from Oklahoma Christian University, Mbaraga has extensive experience managing educational and business initiatives in Rwanda and abroad. He is also a co-founder of Aspire Academy, a school serving children from low-income families in Bugesera District.

In a statement, Oklahoma Christian University of Rwanda congratulated Mbaraga on his appointment, praising his “integrity-driven leadership and commitment to impactful collaboration” between Rwanda and the United States.

According to the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), the United States invested $441.3 million in 31 projects in 2024, while bilateral trade in goods and services reached $368.9 million, underscoring the growing partnership between the two nations.

title: Rwanda: 58% of Mining and Construction Inspections Fail to Address Worker Risks, IPAR Study Reveals
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - A new study by the Institute of Policy Analysis and Research (IPAR) has revealed that 58% of inspections in Rwanda’s mining and construction sectors fail to adequately address worker safety risks…
title_en: Rwanda: 58% of Mining and Construction Inspections Fail to Address Worker Risks, IPAR Study Reveals
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - A new study by the Institute of Policy Analysis and Research (IPAR) has revealed that 58% of inspections in Rwanda’s mining and construction sectors fail to adequately address worker safety risks…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - A new study by the Institute of Policy Analysis and Research (IPAR) has revealed that 58% of inspections in Rwanda’s mining and construction sectors fail to adequately address worker safety risks, including the potential for child labor. The findings were presented in Kigali on November 4, 2025, based on data collected between 2019 and 2024.

The research, which covered all regions of the country, involved 400 workers, employers, labor inspectors, government officials, and non-governmental organizations. It sought to evaluate how effectively workplace inspections protect workers in high-risk sectors.

According to the study, most inspections - 58% - focus primarily on wages and employee benefits such as social security and insurance. In contrast, only 7% of inspections examine occupational safety, while a mere 4% address the use of child labor.

The report also found that over 90% of workers are unaware of their rights under Rwanda’s labor laws, and many work without formal contracts due to fear of job loss. Moreover, 95% of safety-related inspections occur after an accident, rather than as preventive measures.

Despite these shortcomings, the study noted that 63% of inspections result in tangible improvements in compliance, while 33% have moderate impact and 4% are ineffective. It also reported that 95.8% of workplace accidents were investigated to address their causes, and 83.3% of these inquiries led to meaningful preventive actions.

The research identified logistical challenges as a major barrier, noting that many inspectors lack equipment to reach remote or mountainous mining areas, which make up around 60% of Rwanda’s terrain.

IPAR’s report recommends strengthening government institutions responsible for labor oversight - including the Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA), the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB), and the Ministry of Public Service and Labor. It also urges authorities to simplify labor laws in Kinyarwanda, enhance technology adoption, and improve the quality and frequency of inspections to ensure safer and fairer working conditions.

title: Minister Sebahizi Assures Fuel Price Hike Will Not Affect Market Goods
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - The recent increase in petroleum product prices is not expected to impact the prices of ordinary goods in Rwanda, according to Minister of Trade and Industry, Sebahizi Prudence.
title_en: Minister Sebahizi Assures Fuel Price Hike Will Not Affect Market Goods
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - The recent increase in petroleum product prices is not expected to impact the prices of ordinary goods in Rwanda, according to Minister of Trade and Industry, Sebahizi Prudence.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - The recent increase in petroleum product prices is not expected to impact the prices of ordinary goods in Rwanda, according to Minister of Trade and Industry, Sebahizi Prudence.

The Regulatory Authority (RURA) recently announced a rise in fuel prices, with gasoline now at Rwf 1,989 per liter and diesel at Rwf 1,900 per liter, reflecting a 5% increase.

Minister Sebahizi emphasized that this modest increase will not translate into higher market prices for goods.

“We do not expect any change in commodity prices because this 5% increase in the price of a liter of diesel, when you put it as a percentage of the price of goods, is very small. A liter of diesel can carry a ton of goods for kilometers, so there is no way to apply this change to goods,” he said.

He further cautioned traders against using the fuel price rise as a pretext to increase goods arbitrarily, noting that basic price calculations would prevent unjustified hikes.

“Traders should do their calculations but should not use them as a basis for raising prices in an unclear way. If consumers report anomalies, we can verify and make the necessary adjustments,” Sebahizi added.

Looking ahead, the minister noted that even if prices rise next month, they are likely to stabilize or decrease during the harvest season, when goods will become more abundant in markets.

Ambassador Jean de Dieu Uwihanganye, Minister of State in the Ministry of Infrastructure, said public transport fares in Kigali City are unlikely to change significantly. However, provincial transport fares may be adjusted following extensive studies.

The government is also encouraging the adoption of electric vehicles as a way to reduce dependency on petroleum.

“We have removed taxes on electric cars and motorbikes and invested in projects such as Kivu Gas, which can be used for cooking and in large vehicles. Within about two years, these alternatives will help reduce our reliance on oil,” Uwihanganye said.

The last fuel price adjustment occurred on July 1, 2025, marking this as the second increase this year.

title: Rwanda-UAE Trade Talks Advance as CEPA Negotiations Near Final Stage
excerpt: Abu Dhabi - Trade negotiations between Rwanda and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are progressing rapidly, with both countries moving closer to signing a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
title_en: Rwanda-UAE Trade Talks Advance as CEPA Negotiations Near Final Stage
excerpt_en: Abu Dhabi - Trade negotiations between Rwanda and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are progressing rapidly, with both countries moving closer to signing a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
body_en:
Abu Dhabi - Trade negotiations between Rwanda and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are progressing rapidly, with both countries moving closer to signing a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). UAE Minister of State for International Trade, Dr. Thani Al Zeyoudi, confirmed the developments during the UAE-Chad Trade and Investment Forum held in Abu Dhabi.

CEPA is the UAE’s flagship trade framework designed to expand global markets for Emirati companies, attract foreign investment, and reduce the country’s dependence on oil revenue. The agreement lowers trade barriers, boosts investment flows, and enhances economic cooperation between partner nations.

Dr. Al Zeyoudi said that the UAE expects to finalize its CEPA with Chad before the end of 2025, followed by Rwanda and Nigeria. Negotiations with Ghana and South Africa are also planned.

"We are in the CEPA negotiations with Chad. We have already finalized the draft agreement and are entering into negotiations on the market. I am very confident that we will conclude before the end of this year," he said.

The minister noted that non-oil trade between the UAE and Chad rose by 32% in 2024 to reach $1.9 billion, underscoring the growing economic ties.

He added that the UAE had “completed almost all the draft agreements with Nigeria” and was “well advanced in the talks with Rwanda.”

Since launching the CEPA program in September 2021, the UAE has signed 28 trade agreements with partners including India, Indonesia, Cambodia, Georgia, Costa Rica, Mauritius, Serbia, Jordan, Malaysia, New Zealand, and Australia. The initiative forms part of the UAE’s strategy to raise its total trade value to $1 trillion by 2031 and double the size of its economy to $800 billion.

Economic ties between Rwanda and the UAE have strengthened significantly in recent years. Bilateral trade is expected to reach $1.1 billion by 2023, driven by the growth of non-oil commerce.

According to the Rwanda Development Board’s 2024 report, the UAE remains the top destination for Rwandan exports. Goods exported to the UAE generated more than $1.4 billion in 2024, up from $951.2 million in 2023-an increase of 63.9%.

With CEPA negotiations now approaching the final stage, officials from both countries say the agreement is poised to unlock new opportunities in trade, logistics, manufacturing, and investment.

title: Senate Urges MINEDUC to Address Equivalence Delays for Foreign Qualifications
excerpt: KIGALI, RWANDA - The Rwandan Senate has called on the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) and the Higher Education Council (HEC) to find a sustainable solution to delays in granting equivalency certificates to students who…
title_en: Senate Urges MINEDUC to Address Equivalence Delays for Foreign Qualifications
excerpt_en: KIGALI, RWANDA - The Rwandan Senate has called on the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) and the Higher Education Council (HEC) to find a sustainable solution to delays in granting equivalency certificates to students who…
body_en:
KIGALI, RWANDA - The Rwandan Senate has called on the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) and the Higher Education Council (HEC) to find a sustainable solution to delays in granting equivalency certificates to students who studied abroad. The issue was raised during discussions on a report examining how institutions are implementing recommendations from the Auditor General of Rwanda.

Equivalence certificates validate foreign qualifications for use in Rwanda’s labor market. According to the Auditor General’s report, processing times have been excessively long, with applicants waiting between 20 and 405 days. Between 2021 and 2024, HEC received 28,043 applications but granted equivalence to only 21.4% of applicants.

Senators emphasized the need for clear guidelines to streamline the process and ensure timely issuance.

Edward Kadozi, Director General of HEC, explained that delays are often due to applicants failing to meet requirements or slow responses from foreign universities. “We are building a technological system so that an applicant cannot proceed if they have not met certain requirements, gradually reducing time-consuming processes,” Kadozi said.

He confirmed that the new system will be operational by June 2026, moving away from manual paper reviews to a digital process that allows quicker verification, approval, or rejection of applications. “The traditional way involved an employee reviewing and printing on paper. We are moving it to technology where the system ensures transparency and efficiency,” he added.

HEC noted that equivalence certificates continue to be issued weekly for applicants who meet all necessary requirements, and the upcoming system is expected to further expedite the process.

title: Bizimana Dominique Re-Elected President of NPC Rwanda After 13 Years
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Bizimana Dominique has been re-elected as President of the National Paralympic Committee of Rwanda (NPC Rwanda), marking his return to the helm after 13 years.
title_en: Bizimana Dominique Re-Elected President of NPC Rwanda After 13 Years
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Bizimana Dominique has been re-elected as President of the National Paralympic Committee of Rwanda (NPC Rwanda), marking his return to the helm after 13 years.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Bizimana Dominique has been re-elected as President of the National Paralympic Committee of Rwanda (NPC Rwanda), marking his return to the helm after 13 years. Bizimana, who previously led the organization from 2001 to 2012, succeeds Murema Jean Baptiste, whose term officially ended in June 2025.

The elections were held on Saturday, November 8, 2025, at the Classic Hotel in Kigali, with members of the committee casting their votes. Bizimana won by a narrow margin, securing 21 votes against his opponent Sekarema Jean Paul, who garnered 19 votes.

During his earlier tenure, Bizimana played a pivotal role in laying the foundations for Rwanda’s sports programs for persons with disabilities, championing inclusion and ensuring that Rwandan para-athletes gained greater recognition on the international stage.

Following his victory, Bizimana expressed gratitude for the renewed confidence placed in him. “It is an honor to be trusted again. With the new committee we have been elected, we are going to work transparently,” he said. He pledged to focus on expanding opportunities for athletes with disabilities, strengthening partnerships with both public and private institutions, and encouraging more youth with disabilities to engage in sports.

The elections also brought in a new leadership team to serve alongside him for the next four years:

Kanyange Espérance, First Vice President in charge of Competitions

Uwitonze Hesron, Second Vice President in charge of Publicity and Communications

Nzeyimana Célestin, Secretary General (returning to a role he held between 2001 and 2012 before serving as NPC Rwanda President from 2012 to 2017)

The Supervisory Committee includes Cyamenyerwa Solange, Ingabire Marthe, and Munyaneza Gratien, while Nkurayija Jean Pierre, Twizerimana David, and Byukusenge Elise will serve as Advisors.

The Arbitration Committee is composed of Uthama Solange and Ngendandumwe Augustin, with Mukanganizi Marie Claire representing women and Ndahiro Jean Claude representing the athletes.

Observers noted that the elections were long overdue, as the previous committee’s mandate expired on June 28, 2025. With a new team in place, stakeholders hope the NPC will renew its focus on strengthening Rwanda’s Paralympic movement and advancing inclusion in sports nationwide.

title: Rwandan Journalists Call for Expedited Media Policy Revision on African Press Day
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - As Rwanda marked African Press Day on November 7, 2025, journalists and media officials highlighted the urgent need for a revised media policy to address persistent challenges in the profession.
title_en: Rwandan Journalists Call for Expedited Media Policy Revision on African Press Day
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - As Rwanda marked African Press Day on November 7, 2025, journalists and media officials highlighted the urgent need for a revised media policy to address persistent challenges in the profession.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - As Rwanda marked African Press Day on November 7, 2025, journalists and media officials highlighted the urgent need for a revised media policy to address persistent challenges in the profession. They emphasized that the absence of an updated framework is at the root of ongoing issues in the media sector.

The Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) confirmed its commitment to supporting professional journalism, ensuring that media practitioners have the necessary knowledge and skills. However, journalists argued that the revision of the media policy must be prioritized to further strengthen the profession.

Jean Bosco Rushingabigwi, Director of Media at RGB, acknowledged progress but noted obstacles remain, particularly in journalism education and training.

“Journalism schools must keep up with the times. If you start a university that teaches journalism, how do you teach 80 students with only two cameras? How can a student reach the fourth year without hands-on experience?” he said.

Other challenges identified include gender equality, with women and girls in the media facing barriers and violence that limit their rights, and low salaries, which continue to affect journalists’ living conditions. Rushingabigwi stressed that the forthcoming media policy is expected to address these concerns.

The head of the Rwanda Media Regulatory Commission (RMC), Mutesi Scovia, echoed the call for urgency, noting that the revised policy will provide clarity on media operations, ethical standards, and professional principles.

“We are asking for it to be expedited so that no one applying for the right to work is left behind. A clear policy will determine what media practitioners can do, how they can do it, and what they must respect,” she said.

Other issues highlighted include the high costs media outlets face for broadcasting via RBA towers, which continue to strain operations.

Dr. Edward Kalisa, Secretary General of RGB, emphasized the broader African context, urging countries to ensure that news is truthful, evidence-based, and responsibly shared.

The head of the Rwanda Media Regulatory Commission (RMC), Mutesi Scovia, echoed the call for urgency, noting that the revised policy will provide clarity on media operations, ethical standards, and professional principles.

title: Supreme Court President Urges Judges to Reduce Backlogged Cases
excerpt: MUSANZE, RWANDA - Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, President of the Supreme Court, has called on judges to expedite the delivery of justice and reduce the backlog of cases in Rwandan courts.
title_en: Supreme Court President Urges Judges to Reduce Backlogged Cases
excerpt_en: MUSANZE, RWANDA - Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, President of the Supreme Court, has called on judges to expedite the delivery of justice and reduce the backlog of cases in Rwandan courts.
body_en:
MUSANZE, RWANDA - Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, President of the Supreme Court, has called on judges to expedite the delivery of justice and reduce the backlog of cases in Rwandan courts. She emphasized this during discussions on October 31 with judges and court staff at the Musanze High Court.

Mukantaganzwa highlighted that cases should generally be heard in the order they are filed, though postponements and other external factors may affect the schedule. At the Musanze High Court, 1,499 cases are currently recorded, with 1,096 identified as backlogged.

“Long-standing policies are in place to ensure that backlogged cases are addressed promptly,” Mukantaganzwa said. “In the reports submitted, you can see backlogs are being filed year after year, but there are very few old cases remaining, which are prioritized and completed.”

She clarified that any case not heard within six months is officially considered backlogged, explaining that this standard ensures timely justice for citizens. “Six months is not a long time, but it is necessary to provide fast service in the judiciary,” she said.

The Musanze High Court currently handles 1,214 cases, 95% of which are criminal and 5% civil. Of these, 585 cases dating back to 2022 remain backlogged, with criminal cases comprising 97% and civil cases 3%. Predominant offenses include drug-related crimes, child rape, theft, murder, and assault and battery.

Mukantaganzwa stressed that measures are being implemented to reduce these backlogs, ensuring that citizens receive timely judicial services and reinforcing the principle of prompt justice in Rwanda’s legal system.

title: Paris: Munyemana Sentenced to 24 Years in Prison Appeals to the Court of Cassation
excerpt: Paris, France - Dr. Sosthène Munyemana, a Rwandan gynecologist convicted in France for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, has appealed his 24-year prison sentence to the French Court of Cassation, seeking…
title_en: Paris: Munyemana Sentenced to 24 Years in Prison Appeals to the Court of Cassation
excerpt_en: Paris, France - Dr. Sosthène Munyemana, a Rwandan gynecologist convicted in France for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, has appealed his 24-year prison sentence to the French Court of Cassation, seeking…
body_en:
Paris, France - Dr. Sosthène Munyemana, a Rwandan gynecologist convicted in France for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, has appealed his 24-year prison sentence to the French Court of Cassation, seeking a new trial. The appeal, officially filed and served to the parties on November 4, was confirmed by lawyer Me Richard Gisagara, who represents the plaintiffs.

Dr. Munyemana was found guilty by the Paris Criminal Court in December 2023 of participating in genocide in Butare, particularly in the Tumba sector. His conviction and sentence were upheld by the Appeals Chamber on October 23, 2025. A separate compensation trial is set to begin on June 8, 2026.

The Court of Cassation, France’s highest judicial authority, does not retry cases on their facts but examines whether the law was properly applied. If procedural or legal errors are found, it can order a retrial before a different court.

“The appeal was filed and the notice served today,” Me Gisagara told reporters, confirming that the process is now in the hands of the Court of Cassation.

A Doctor Accused of Complicity in Genocide

Before and during the genocide, Dr. Munyemana worked as a gynecologist at Butare Hospital and taught at the former National University of Rwanda. He was a prominent member of the MDR party, serving as vice president of its intellectuals’ association (Cercle des Intellectuels) in Butare, and maintained close ties with figures such as Jean Kambanda, the former Prime Minister of the genocidal “Abatabazi” government.

The court found that Munyemana used his local influence to support the interim government that orchestrated the genocide. On April 16, 1994, he and other intellectuals in Butare signed a declaration endorsing the transitional government - fully aware, the court said, that mass killings of Tutsi had already begun nine days earlier.

“It is clear that the accused willingly supported, since April 16, 1994, the transitional government that planned and implemented the extermination of Tutsi,” the court wrote in its October 27, 2025 judgment.

Evidence presented in court showed that Dr. Munyemana attended an April 17, 1994 meeting at the Tumba Sector office, where local leaders decided to organize patrols and set up roadblocks. He was appointed to the security committee that oversaw these operations - measures later used to track, arrest, and execute Tutsi civilians.

Between April 23 and May 19, 1994, Munyemana reportedly held the keys to the Tumba Sector office, where dozens of Tutsi were detained under his supervision. Witnesses testified that many were later taken away and killed by the Interahamwe militia.

The court concluded that Munyemana knowingly facilitated their capture and imprisonment, contributing directly to their deaths. “He was fully aware that Tutsi would be arrested at roadblocks and executed, yet he continued to participate,” the judgment stated.

Dr. Munyemana claimed he detained Tutsi to protect them from attackers, but judges dismissed this argument as implausible. They noted that detainees were confined in inhumane conditions - without food, water, or protection - and that he made no effort to check their fate after they were taken away.

The court also rejected his assertion that he was “apolitical,” finding instead that he was deeply involved in local and national political networks that supported the genocide.

The conviction of Dr. Munyemana, who lived in France for decades before his arrest, was one of several landmark cases tried under France’s universal jurisdiction over crimes against humanity. His appeal now places the final decision in the hands of the Court of Cassation - the last legal avenue available to challenge his conviction.

If the appeal is rejected, the 24-year sentence handed down for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi will remain final.

title: Kigali Authorities Sound Alarm Over Rising Cases of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - The City of Kigali has raised alarm over the growing number of child sexual abuse cases, warning that many incidents remain unreported due to parental negligence and lack of awareness.
title_en: Kigali Authorities Sound Alarm Over Rising Cases of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - The City of Kigali has raised alarm over the growing number of child sexual abuse cases, warning that many incidents remain unreported due to parental negligence and lack of awareness.
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - The City of Kigali has raised alarm over the growing number of child sexual abuse cases, warning that many incidents remain unreported due to parental negligence and lack of awareness.

City spokesperson Ntirenganya Emma Claudine said the number of children suffering sexual violence is “not small,” adding that insufficient parental supervision continues to fuel the problem. “There are parents who do not monitor their children to ensure they do not encounter such a problem,” she said. “If a parent has other things to do, they should at least know who is with their child and where they are staying.”

According to the National Criminal Investigation Service (RIB), during the 2023/24 fiscal year, 4,901 people were prosecuted for sexual violence against children nationwide - including 4,767 men and 134 women. The victims included 4,849 children, among them 4,646 girls and 203 boys.

Ntirenganya noted that most of the reported cases are substantiated. “At the national level, more than 4,000 children were received by the Criminal Investigation Service with allegations of rape, and about 75 to 76 percent of those cases were proven,” she told Isango Star. “What concerns us most is that these figures represent only the complaints that reached the courts.”

She added that a significant number of cases go unreported, often because parents fail to notice the abuse or the children remain silent. “There are children who are raped without their parents knowing about it,” she said.

The City of Kigali is urging parents and guardians to take greater responsibility for their children’s safety by paying attention to their whereabouts and the people around them. Authorities also appealed to communities to show compassion toward victims rather than stigmatizing them.

“The girl who was raped and suffered a tragedy, even becoming pregnant - we must remember she is a victim of a heinous crime punishable by life imprisonment,” Ntirenganya emphasized. “We should not add another burden to her pain.”

Officials say continued public awareness and stronger parental involvement are crucial to protecting children and ensuring justice for survivors of sexual violence.

title: Rubavu Woman Arrested for Allegedly Concealing Information on Genocide Victims’ Whereabouts
excerpt: Rubavu, Rwanda - A 49-year-old woman from Cyanzarwe Sector in Rubavu District has been arrested on suspicion of withholding information about the location of bodies of victims allegedly killed by her father during the…
title_en: Rubavu Woman Arrested for Allegedly Concealing Information on Genocide Victims’ Whereabouts
excerpt_en: Rubavu, Rwanda - A 49-year-old woman from Cyanzarwe Sector in Rubavu District has been arrested on suspicion of withholding information about the location of bodies of victims allegedly killed by her father during the…
body_en:
Rubavu, Rwanda - A 49-year-old woman from Cyanzarwe Sector in Rubavu District has been arrested on suspicion of withholding information about the location of bodies of victims allegedly killed by her father during the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

According to local sources, the incident occurred on the night of November 6 to 7, 2025, in Mukingo Village, Makurizo Cell, after the woman, reportedly intoxicated, had an argument with her husband. During the quarrel, she allegedly told him that he would “end up like the 10 Tutsi children her father killed during the Genocide.” Alarmed by the statement, her husband immediately reported the matter to local authorities, leading to her arrest.

Investigators from the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) say the woman later provided partial information indicating that her father, who had worked in Mudende Sector during the Genocide, was involved in the killings of Tutsi civilians in the area. However, authorities noted inconsistencies in her account and a lack of full cooperation regarding the whereabouts of all the victims’ remains.

The President of Ibuka in Rubavu District, Gérard Mbarushimana, confirmed that during the investigation, the woman admitted to knowing the locations of some of the victims. “She identified three bodies, which have since been given a proper burial,” Mbarushimana told IGIHE. “However, she has not revealed where the remaining seven victims were buried. That information has now been handed over to justice for further investigation.”

Mbarushimana described the case as deeply troubling, particularly more than three decades after the Genocide. “It is regrettable that 31 years after the Genocide against the Tutsi was stopped, there is still a lack of information about the whereabouts of victims so they can be buried with dignity,” he said.

He added that the woman’s father, believed to have fled to the Democratic Republic of Congo after the killings, has since disappeared and is presumed dead.

Ibuka, the umbrella organization representing survivors of the Genocide, has urged residents who possess information about unlocated victims to come forward. “Anyone who provides information is free from blame,” Mbarushimana said. “But those who deliberately conceal such information will be held accountable.”

The suspect remains in custody at the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) station in Rubavu as investigations continue.

title: Government-Held Areas in DRC Need Urgent Aid, Analyst Says
excerpt: KINSHASA, DRC - Congolese political analyst Me Jean Baptiste Gasominari has argued that areas under government control in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are in greater need of humanitarian assistance than those…
title_en: Government-Held Areas in DRC Need Urgent Aid, Analyst Says
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DRC - Congolese political analyst Me Jean Baptiste Gasominari has argued that areas under government control in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are in greater need of humanitarian assistance than those…
body_en:
KINSHASA, DRC - Congolese political analyst Me Jean Baptiste Gasominari has argued that areas under government control in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are in greater need of humanitarian assistance than those administered by the rebel group AFC/M23. Speaking on national television following a recent conference on the Great Lakes Region’s security, he stated that territories held by M23 in the east are currently safer and more stable than those managed by Kinshasa.

The remarks came after a high-level meeting in France on October 30, 2025, where French President Emmanuel Macron announced plans to reopen Goma Airport within weeks to facilitate humanitarian flights twice a week. The move is aimed at boosting relief operations in eastern Congo amid ongoing conflict.

According to Me Gasominari, the M23 movement has restored order in the territories it controls, enabling displaced residents to return to their homes. “When AFC/M23 took over Goma and Bukavu in January, the population that had been forced into camps by government actions returned home almost immediately,” he said. “Today, visitors to these cities can see fields once again full of crops and communities rebuilding their lives.”

He accused the Congolese government of spreading misinformation about conditions in rebel-held areas to mislead the international community. “The DRC government used lies to convince people to move into camps, just to show the world that opponents had disrupted civilian life,” he said.

Gasominari acknowledged isolated tensions in M23-controlled zones, attributing them to government drone attacks and blockades that restrict access to markets and basic goods. However, he maintained that large-scale humanitarian needs are concentrated in government-held regions such as Beni, Butembo, Ituri, and Tshopo - areas plagued by violence from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and other armed groups.

“People there are being attacked, displaced, and killed,” he emphasized. “Those are the regions that truly need urgent humanitarian assistance.”

He concluded by criticizing the government’s narrative on aid distribution. “The claim that help is needed in M23-held areas is a deliberate lie,” Gasominari said. “Kinshasa no longer even has accurate information about those territories.”

title: Kamonyi Police Arrest Six Suspects for Theft and Armed Attacks
excerpt: KAMONYI, RWANDA - Rwandan police in Kamonyi District have arrested six individuals, including five men and one woman, for allegedly carrying traditional weapons and committing theft and other acts threatening public security.
title_en: Kamonyi Police Arrest Six Suspects for Theft and Armed Attacks
excerpt_en: KAMONYI, RWANDA - Rwandan police in Kamonyi District have arrested six individuals, including five men and one woman, for allegedly carrying traditional weapons and committing theft and other acts threatening public security.
body_en:
KAMONYI, RWANDA - Rwandan police in Kamonyi District have arrested six individuals, including five men and one woman, for allegedly carrying traditional weapons and committing theft and other acts threatening public security. The arrests took place during the night of November 1-2, 2025, in Gihinga Cell, Gacurabwenge Sector, with the assistance of local residents and authorities.

CIP Kamanzi Hassan, National Police Spokesperson for the Southern Province, told IGIHE that the suspects were primarily involved in livestock theft and housebreaking, armed with knives, machetes, axes, and other implements.

“Those arrested were found with some of the animals they had stolen, including 15 chickens and six rabbits,” CIP Kamanzi said. “They are now all detained at the Gacurabwenge Police Station, and the Criminal Investigation Department has begun tracking down others involved.”

CIP Kamanzi also urged residents to abandon criminal activities, warning that the police will prosecute and punish anyone involved in acts that threaten security and public peace.

He praised the community members who continue to cooperate with law enforcement by providing timely information and called on others to follow their example, emphasizing that maintaining security is a shared responsibility.

title_en: Kenyan Defence Chief Visits Rwanda to Strengthen Military Cooperation
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - The Chief of the Kenyan Defence Forces (KDF), General Charles Muriu Kahariri, is on a working visit to Rwanda from November 4 to 7, 2025, aimed at reinforcing bilateral military relations between the…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - The Chief of the Kenyan Defence Forces (KDF), General Charles Muriu Kahariri, is on a working visit to Rwanda from November 4 to 7, 2025, aimed at reinforcing bilateral military relations between the two East African nations.

On Wednesday, Gen. Kahariri met with Rwandan Minister of Defence Juvenal Marizamunda and Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Mubarakh Muganga, at the Ministry of Defence and RDF Headquarters in Kigali. Discussions focused on reviewing ongoing defence cooperation, identifying new areas of collaboration, and exchanging views on regional security challenges.

During his visit, the Kenyan military chief also toured the Kigali Genocide Memorial, where he received a briefing on Rwanda’s history and paid tribute to the victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

The visit underscores the continued commitment of Kenya and Rwanda to regional peace, security, and defence cooperation, building on their shared efforts within the East African Community (EAC) and broader continental security frameworks.

title: Rwanda Hosts 19th African Heads of Military Colleges Conference, Calls for Innovation and Unity in Security
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda’s Minister of Defence, Juvenal Marizamunda, has called for greater innovation, collaboration, and unity among African nations to effectively address the continent’s evolving security challenges.
title_en: Rwanda Hosts 19th African Heads of Military Colleges Conference, Calls for Innovation and Unity in Security
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda’s Minister of Defence, Juvenal Marizamunda, has called for greater innovation, collaboration, and unity among African nations to effectively address the continent’s evolving security challenges.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda’s Minister of Defence, Juvenal Marizamunda, has called for greater innovation, collaboration, and unity among African nations to effectively address the continent’s evolving security challenges.

Speaking at the opening of the 19th African Heads of Military Colleges Conference (ACoC) on Monday, November 10, 2025, in Kigali, Minister Marizamunda emphasized that Africa’s strength in defense and security depends on its capacity to innovate and work together.

“In today’s technologically advanced world, facing many security challenges, the capacity of our schools to innovate and collaborate is what determines our security strength as Africans,” he said. “We face many challenges including terrorism, cyber warfare, illicit trade, climate change, and migration. To overcome them, we need soldiers who are highly skilled, technologically literate, ethical, and forward-thinking.”

The three-day conference, which gathers delegates from 24 countries, is being held under the theme: “The Future of Military Training and Education in Africa: Bridging the Technology Gap.” Established to enhance knowledge-sharing and professional development across the continent’s defense institutions, ACoC serves as a vital platform for advancing military education and cooperation.

The meeting brought together heads of military colleges, representatives of the African Union Peace and Security Service, and regional defense experts.

Minister Marizamunda urged participants to ensure that their deliberations translate into tangible progress. “I urge all participants to ensure that your discussions are open and constructive, and that the decisions you make are practical and actionable. The future of military education in Africa will depend on what we agree on today and how we implement it,” he said.

He also praised the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) Military Academy for its leadership during Rwanda’s tenure as chair of ACoC, noting the institution’s role in fostering unity and advancing continental security education. Rwanda is expected to hand over the chairmanship to Tanzania at the close of the conference.

Brig. Gen. Andrew Nyamvumba, Commandant of the RDF Military Academy, highlighted that ACoC serves not only as a network of military training institutions but also as a hub for the exchange of knowledge and strategic insight. “This conference is a platform for pooling African military expertise and wisdom. It is where ideas are shared, traditions are refined, and partnerships are strengthened to build a secure, resilient, and self-reliant Africa,” he said.

Incoming chair Maj. Gen. Stephen Mnkande, Commandant of the Tanzanian Military Academy, stressed the importance of strengthening technology-driven institutions to respond to modern security threats.

Similarly, Air Commodore (Brig. Gen.) N. Maghidir, Commandant of the Libyan Military Academy, underscored that cooperation must remain the cornerstone of Africa’s collective security.

Delegates attending the conference represent countries including Cameroon, Egypt, Guinea, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Namibia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Malawi, Kenya, Ghana, Tanzania, Botswana, Burundi, Algeria, Zimbabwe, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, the Central African Republic, Somalia, and Rwanda.

The conference is expected to conclude with key resolutions on strengthening military education systems and enhancing regional defense collaboration to ensure a safer and more self-reliant Africa.

title: DRC and Burundi Accused of Increasing Troop Deployments in Fizi Highlands to Target Banyamulenge
excerpt: Fizi, South Kivu (DRC) - The Movement for the Defense of the People - Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho) has accused the governments of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Burundi of deploying additional troops to the…
title_en: DRC and Burundi Accused of Increasing Troop Deployments in Fizi Highlands to Target Banyamulenge
excerpt_en: Fizi, South Kivu (DRC) - The Movement for the Defense of the People - Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho) has accused the governments of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Burundi of deploying additional troops to the…
body_en:
Fizi, South Kivu (DRC) - The Movement for the Defense of the People - Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho) has accused the governments of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Burundi of deploying additional troops to the highlands of Fizi Territory with the alleged aim of targeting the Banyamulenge community.

In a statement released this week, the group claimed that more than 10 Burundian battalions are currently operating in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga, and that these forces have launched “serious attacks” against Banyamulenge civilians since early last week.

According to MRDP-Twirwaneho, the deployment includes two Burundian battalions and one Congolese battalion (the 3303rd), all reportedly led by Gen. Chivire. The units are said to be stationed at “Point-Zéro,” a key military position at the entrance to Minembwe, a town predominantly inhabited by the Banyamulenge.

Twirwaneho further alleged that the Burundian troops had crossed into DRC territory via Lake Tanganyika, using a military vessel. The group claimed the troops came from several Burundian army divisions commanded by senior officers, including Brig. Gen. Hakizimana Pontien (1st Division), Brig. Gen. Ndenzako Michel (2nd Division), Brig. Gen. Habarugira Jean-Luc (3rd Division), and Brig. Gen. Manirakiza Désiré, known as Gacanga (4th Division).

“The increase in Burundian troops in Fizi shows that the military cooperation between the DRC and Burundi governments paves the way for the continued deployment of Burundian troops in the highlands in order to commit genocide against the Banyamulenge,” the statement read.

Minembwe and the surrounding highlands have been the scene of repeated violence targeting the Banyamulenge community - a Tutsi-speaking minority - since 2017. The attacks have reportedly displaced more than 328,000 people, destroyed over 550 villages, and led to widespread looting of livestock and the destruction of infrastructure including schools and health centers.

MRDP-Twirwaneho accuses the Congolese and Burundian armies, along with local Wazalendo militias and members of the FDLR (Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda), of sharing what it describes as “an ideology of hatred against the Tutsi” and coordinating assaults on Banyamulenge communities.

Neither the DRC nor Burundian authorities have issued an official response to the allegations.

The situation in Fizi remains tense, as reports of military movements and renewed clashes continue to raise fears of further humanitarian crises in South Kivu’s highlands.

title: DRC Forces Accused of Launching Drone Strikes on Banyamulenge Communities in South Kivu
excerpt: South Kivu, DRC - Armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have been accused of launching drone attacks on Mikenke, a village in Mwenga Territory, South Kivu Province, in an alleged attempt to target…
title_en: DRC Forces Accused of Launching Drone Strikes on Banyamulenge Communities in South Kivu
excerpt_en: South Kivu, DRC - Armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have been accused of launching drone attacks on Mikenke, a village in Mwenga Territory, South Kivu Province, in an alleged attempt to target…
body_en:
South Kivu, DRC - Armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have been accused of launching drone attacks on Mikenke, a village in Mwenga Territory, South Kivu Province, in an alleged attempt to target Banyamulenge civilians and leaders in displacement camps.

The strikes were reported at 8:00 a.m. on November 15, 2025, according to Congolese politician Moïse Nyarugabo, himself a member of the Banyamulenge community.

“Tshisekedi’s drones targeted the village of Mikenke, which is inhabited by civilians, and also hosts a camp for Banyamulenge whose villages were burned,” Nyarugabo said.“The numbers are not yet known, but there is no doubt that civilians must have been there.”

Nyarugabo further claimed to have “reliable information” indicating that FARDC forces, along with Burundian troops, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR, are preparing new offensives in Minembwe and Mikenke, areas heavily populated by Banyamulenge communities.

He cited military movements in several locations - Point-Zéro, Mikalati, Kigazura, Marunde, Kipupu, Rugezi, and Mukoko - as evidence of imminent operations.

“Two generals, one Congolese and the other Burundian, are in that area preparing for the offensives. Unless the plan changes at the last minute, those who survived the Sukhoi and drone attacks may be bombed again,” he warned.

The Banyamulenge, a Tutsi-speaking minority community in South Kivu, have faced sustained attacks since 2017 from a coalition of armed groups that local activists say operates with government support.

According to the MRDP Twirwaneho movement, which advocates for Banyamulenge rights:

328,000+ people have been displaced

550 villages destroyed

41 health centres demolished

126+ churches attacked

Since October 16, residents of Minembwe have reportedly been cut off from market routes, accused by Burundian forces of “collaborating with enemies.”

Human rights observers warn that escalating military operations in South Kivu risk worsening an already dire humanitarian situation, while increasing the vulnerability of the Banyamulenge population, many of whom have been repeatedly displaced over the past decade.

title: Rwanda Receives Seven FDLR Fighters Repatriated by MONUSCO
excerpt: Rwanda has received seven former FDLR combatants and their family members repatriated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) by the UN peacekeeping mission, MONUSCO, on November 10, 2025.
title_en: Rwanda Receives Seven FDLR Fighters Repatriated by MONUSCO
excerpt_en: Rwanda has received seven former FDLR combatants and their family members repatriated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) by the UN peacekeeping mission, MONUSCO, on November 10, 2025.
body_en:
Rwanda has received seven former FDLR combatants and their family members repatriated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) by the UN peacekeeping mission, MONUSCO, on November 10, 2025.

The group had spent three days at a transit centre in Goma for ex-combatants wishing to lay down their arms before being returned to Rwanda.

According to MONUSCO, a total of 49 Rwandans were repatriated on the same day. Mission officials said the individuals expressed relief at returning home and urged others still in the bush to surrender.

From January to October 2025, MONUSCO repatriated 54 Rwandan fighters, mostly affiliated with the FDLR, along with 44 accompanying family members.

One of the returnees described life in the bush as “difficult,” appealing to remaining fighters to surrender so they too could return home safely.

Upon arrival in Rwanda, ex-combatants are transferred to the Rwanda Demobilisation and Reintegration Commission (RDRC) centre in Mutobo, Musanze District. There, they undergo several months of training to prepare them for reintegration into civilian life.

On October 30, the RDRC released 143 former FDLR members who had completed three to six months of reintegration training. Officials said efforts to support all who choose peaceful return will continue.

As Rwanda navigates the first half of November 2025, the country continues to balance complex regional tensions with steady diplomatic engagement and internal progress. While relations with the DRC remain strained amid accusations, stalled summits, and fragile peace negotiations, Rwanda has kept its focus on broader international partnerships - from defense cooperation and disaster-preparedness initiatives to expanding global trade and enhancing its presence in tourism markets. Domestically, advances in unity, energy access, education reform, and social protection underline a nation determined to strengthen its institutions and safeguard its social fabric. Yet challenges persist, particularly in labor enforcement, child protection, and lingering justice issues tied to the 1994 Genocide. Overall, the period reflects a Rwanda that is assertive on the diplomatic stage, vigilant on matters of security, and committed to long-term development, even as regional uncertainties continue to test its resilience.

title: Rwandan Community in France Accuses RFI of Giving Platform to FDLR
excerpt: The Rwandan Community in France (Communauté Rwandaise de France, CRF) has filed a formal complaint against Radio France Internationale (RFI), accusing the broadcaster of providing a platform to members of the FDLR - a…
title_en: Rwandan Community in France Accuses RFI of Giving Platform to FDLR
excerpt_en: The Rwandan Community in France (Communauté Rwandaise de France, CRF) has filed a formal complaint against Radio France Internationale (RFI), accusing the broadcaster of providing a platform to members of the FDLR - a…
body_en:
The Rwandan Community in France (Communauté Rwandaise de France, CRF) has filed a formal complaint against Radio France Internationale (RFI), accusing the broadcaster of providing a platform to members of the FDLR - a group responsible for the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi - and presenting them as a legitimate political movement.

The complaint, submitted on November 15, 2025, was addressed to ARCOM, France’s audiovisual and digital communications regulator.

According to the CRF, RFI crossed an ethical line after publishing an article on November 10, 2025, headlined: “We will continue to fight until Kigali accepts talks: FDLR said.” The community argues that the article, written by journalist Patient Ligodi, portrays the FDLR as a lightly armed faction operating in eastern DR Congo while downplaying its genocidal background and decades-long record of atrocities.

The complaint, signed by lawyer Me Richard Gisagara, notes that the FDLR has been widely condemned and sanctioned by the United Nations, the United States, and the European Union for crimes committed in both Rwanda and eastern DR Congo over the past three decades. Several of its leaders have been convicted in German courts for their role in genocide and mass violence.

The CRF argues that RFI’s reporting failed to provide essential contextual information, effectively granting respectability to a group internationally recognized as terrorist.

“CRF regrets that RFI, as a state media outlet expected to uphold democratic values, has not fulfilled its responsibility to provide accurate and balanced information,” the organization stated. “Instead, it repeats the group’s statements without verification, giving them a credibility they should not have.”

In its submission, the CRF cited the French law of September 30, 1986, as well as the editorial guidelines of France Médias Monde and RFI’s internal code of conduct, all of which require journalists to report truthful, balanced, and contextualized information. These rules specifically prohibit journalists from acting as mouthpieces for armed groups.

The CRF also linked the timing of the RFI article to political pressure in the Democratic Republic of Congo, recalling that in January 2025 the DRC government threatened foreign media with severe punishment - including the death penalty - for coverage deemed to oppose the state narrative. According to the CRF, this atmosphere has led some outlets to propagate unfiltered pro-government messaging, increasing the spread of anti-Rwandan rhetoric.

“This pressure has pushed some media to relay DRC propaganda without scrutiny,” the organization warned. “Such bias endangers Rwandan voices, who continue to be targeted by hate speech.”

The CRF is now urging ARCOM to investigate the incident and take appropriate action to ensure that RFI complies with professional standards and legal obligations.

In its concluding remarks, the community reaffirmed its commitment to defending historical truth and combating hatred and impunity: “We will continue to do whatever is necessary to preserve a truthful history and protect our community.”

title: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Rejects ICGLR Resolutions on Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt: Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has dismissed the latest resolutions adopted by the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR)…
title_en: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Rejects ICGLR Resolutions on Eastern DRC Conflict
excerpt_en: Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has dismissed the latest resolutions adopted by the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR)…
body_en:
Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, has dismissed the latest resolutions adopted by the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) concerning the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The ICGLR summit, held on 15 November 2025 in Kinshasa, saw member states grant President Félix Tshisekedi the mandate to lead the organization. According to DRC’s Minister for Regional Integration, Floribert Anzuluni, the heads of state condemned the M23 rebel group and urged “the aggressor state to completely withdraw its troops from the DRC.”

However, Minister Nduhungirehe said the resolutions were irrelevant and lacked legitimacy, arguing that Rwanda’s absence from the summit rendered the conclusions one-sided and detached from the realities of the conflict.

“The conclusions of the ICGLR meeting held in Kinshasa last week, in the absence of Rwanda - which elected Tshisekedi as the new President of this organization based in Bujumbura - are completely irrelevant to the issues related to the conflict in eastern DRC,” he said.

Nduhungirehe emphasized that the ongoing diplomatic efforts in Washington and Doha are the only meaningful pathways toward resolving the crisis. Talks between Rwanda and the DRC in the United States, along with negotiations between the DRC government and AFC/M23 in Qatar, he said, remain the most credible initiatives.

“For this reason, only the Washington and Doha peace processes, supported by the African Union, truly seek a lasting solution to the conflict in eastern DRC,” the minister noted.

His remarks came as both dialogue tracks reached promising stages. On November 7, Rwanda and the DRC signed a comprehensive economic cooperation agreement. One week later, on November 15, the DRC government and the AFC/M23 agreed on a set of basic principles aimed at paving the way for sustainable peace.

The progress made in Washington and Doha, Nduhungirehe added, offers renewed hope for stability in a region long plagued by cycles of violence.

title: Aliko Dangote and Ellen Sirleaf Lead Discussions at African Renaissance Retreat in Kigali
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf were among the high-profile leaders participating in the African Renaissance Retreat, an annual summit bringing…
title_en: Aliko Dangote and Ellen Sirleaf Lead Discussions at African Renaissance Retreat in Kigali
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf were among the high-profile leaders participating in the African Renaissance Retreat, an annual summit bringing…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote and former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf were among the high-profile leaders participating in the African Renaissance Retreat, an annual summit bringing together prominent investors, political leaders, policymakers, and experts to discuss Africa’s future. The retreat, held in partnership with President Paul Kagame and Aliko Dangote, took place from November 14-16, 2025, at The Pinnacle Kigali Hotel.

Now in its second edition, the forum explores how Africa can transform its past challenges through reflection, collaboration, and actionable solutions driven by Africans themselves. This year’s discussions focused on obstacles to sustainable development, investment, innovation, and long-term economic growth across the continent.

On the opening day, Aliko Dangote delivered a keynote address urging visionary leadership. “We need leaders with purpose. If we don’t have them, we will not build anything,” he said.

The program featured high-level panel discussions with current and former African leaders, including Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, former Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn, and former South African President Thabo Mbeki. On the second day, Jean-Guy Afrika, Director General of the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), briefed participants on Rwanda’s development progress, followed by sessions aimed at translating ideas into practical outcomes for the continent.

Through her X platform, Sirleaf expressed her gratitude for being part of the summit, thanking Aliko Dangote for initiating an event that unites the public and private sectors across Africa. “I am delighted to be part of the recent African Renaissance Group Summit in Kigali. This initiative brings together leaders to drive transformation on our continent,” she said.

Also attending were prominent figures from the private sector, including Tony Elumelu, Patrice Motsepe, Tidjane Thiam, Vera Songwe, Abdul Samad Rabiu, Mohammed Dewji, Naguib Sawiris, Femi Otedola, and James Mwangi. International leaders included Amina Mohammed, UN Under-Secretary-General, OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo, and IFC CEO Makhtar Diop.

The retreat concluded with a panel discussion between Hailemariam Desalegn and Thabo Mbeki, highlighting Africa’s governance, economic development, and growth strategies. Dr. James Mwangi, CEO of Equity Bank Group, emphasized the importance of strategic investment. “If we don’t invest in the unwritten to make it written, we will have problems. We need an Africa that understands where we have come from and where we are going,” he said.

Later this week, President Kagame and Aliko Dangote are expected to hold bilateral talks on Africa’s economic transformation, industrialization, and development priorities. The two leaders last met publicly in July 2025 during the inauguration of the Zaria Court sports and entertainment complex, where Kagame praised Dangote’s longstanding commitment to Africa’s progress.

“Some of us are proud to work with him and other leaders,” Kagame said. “There were meetings held here in Kigali, and many more are coming. Alhaji Aliko Dangote has done a lot for that.”

The retreat reinforced Dangote’s dedication to advancing the African Renaissance, a concept first articulated by Senegalese historian Cheikh Anta Diop and later popularized by Thabo Mbeki, envisioning a continent defined by prosperity, innovation, and progress rather than conflict, corruption, and poverty. Dangote reaffirmed his commitment to revitalizing this vision for Africa’s future.

title: Ambassador Innocent Muhizi Presents Credentials to Singaporean President
excerpt: Singapore - Innocent Muhizi, newly appointed Rwandan Ambassador to Singapore, presented his credentials to the President of Singapore, Tharman Shanmugaratnam, on November 17, 2025, marking the official start of his…
title_en: Ambassador Innocent Muhizi Presents Credentials to Singaporean President
excerpt_en: Singapore - Innocent Muhizi, newly appointed Rwandan Ambassador to Singapore, presented his credentials to the President of Singapore, Tharman Shanmugaratnam, on November 17, 2025, marking the official start of his…
body_en:
Singapore - Innocent Muhizi, newly appointed Rwandan Ambassador to Singapore, presented his credentials to the President of Singapore, Tharman Shanmugaratnam, on November 17, 2025, marking the official start of his diplomatic mission.

During the ceremony, Muhizi outlined his goals to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Rwanda and Singapore, particularly in trade, technology, innovation, and building partnerships that contribute to the development of both countries. “I am ready to increase cooperation in the fields of trade, technology, innovation and building partnerships that will develop both countries,” he said.

Muhizi, 49, brings over 20 years of experience in technology and trade. He holds a Master of Science in Information Technology from the University of Pretoria, South Africa, and two additional master’s degrees in Computer Information Systems and Business Management from La Roche University, United States.

He previously served as the Head of the Rwanda Information and Communication Technology Authority (RISA) and as Chief Information Officer and Head of Transactional Banking Services at I&M Bank Rwanda.

Rwanda and Singapore maintain a partnership focused on technology development, innovation, education, capacity building, and green technology, with Singapore playing a key role in supporting Rwanda’s ambition to become a Fintech hub.

title: AU Urges African Countries to Learn from Rwanda in Fighting Corruption
excerpt: Arusha, Tanzania - The Chairperson of the African Union (AU) Council on Corruption and Money Laundering, Kwami Edem Senanu, has called on African nations to take lessons from Rwanda and Botswana in combating corruption…
title_en: AU Urges African Countries to Learn from Rwanda in Fighting Corruption
excerpt_en: Arusha, Tanzania - The Chairperson of the African Union (AU) Council on Corruption and Money Laundering, Kwami Edem Senanu, has called on African nations to take lessons from Rwanda and Botswana in combating corruption…
body_en:
Arusha, Tanzania - The Chairperson of the African Union (AU) Council on Corruption and Money Laundering, Kwami Edem Senanu, has called on African nations to take lessons from Rwanda and Botswana in combating corruption and money laundering. His remarks came during the AU Council (AUABC) meeting held in Arusha on November 17, 2025.

The meeting reviewed measures adopted by African countries to fight corruption and money laundering and assessed the results achieved so far.

Senanu highlighted that Africa loses an estimated $125 billion annually to embezzlement, surpassing the combined GDP of many African countries.

Citing the Transparency International report on corruption and governance, he noted that in 2024, Rwanda ranked 43rd globally among countries making progress in tackling corruption. On the continental level, Rwanda was third in Africa, behind Seychelles and Cape Verde, tied with Botswana, both achieving a 57% score in anti-corruption efforts.

title: Rwanda Hosts OIF Executive Committee Meeting, Strengthens Ties with Cambodia
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda hosted a series of high-level diplomatic engagements on November 18, 2025, as the country prepared to welcome the 46th Council of Ministers of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF).
title_en: Rwanda Hosts OIF Executive Committee Meeting, Strengthens Ties with Cambodia
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda hosted a series of high-level diplomatic engagements on November 18, 2025, as the country prepared to welcome the 46th Council of Ministers of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF).
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Rwanda hosted a series of high-level diplomatic engagements on November 18, 2025, as the country prepared to welcome the 46th Council of Ministers of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF).

In Kigali, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva received Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Cambodia, Prak Sokhonn, to discuss expanding bilateral relations. The meeting focused on enhancing cooperation across several sectors and was highlighted by the signing of two new agreements: an Agreement on Consultative Relations and an Agreement on the abolition of visas for holders of diplomatic and service passports.

The leaders also discussed preparations for the upcoming 46th OIF Council of Ministers, which is scheduled to begin in Kigali the following day. Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn praised Rwanda for its warm reception of participants and the smooth organization of the event. Prime Minister Nsengiyumva expressed gratitude to Cambodia, which is set to assume the presidency of the Francophonie, wishing it success in hosting the 20th Francophonie Summit.

On the same day, the OIF Executive Committee convened in Kigali for its 132nd session, chaired by Secretary General Louise Mushikiwabo. The session reviewed progress on previous decisions and considered new initiatives for upcoming programs. The CPF Council, consisting of Permanent Representatives, Ambassadors, and Heads of Mission from member states, serves as one of the OIF’s primary decision-making bodies.

Hosting the meeting in Kigali reflects recognition of Rwanda’s growing role in advancing Francophone culture and language, following previous occasions when the country hosted major OIF events. The meeting also helped finalize the agenda for the 46th Council of Ministers, which will emphasize strengthening cooperation between member states, promoting technology, and enhancing the role of women, youth, and culture in development. This year’s conference coincides with the 30th anniversary of the Beijing Conference on the Advancement of Women, aligned with the theme: “30 Years After Beijing, the Role of Women in Francophonie.”

The OIF brings together 93 countries, including 56 full members, 5 associate members, and 32 observers, representing over 321 million French speakers worldwide. Rwanda has been a member for 55 years, joining shortly after the organization was established in 1970.

title: “The World Cannot Thrive Without Women,” Says OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary General of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF), emphasized the critical role of women in global development, stating that the world cannot progress without them.
title_en: “The World Cannot Thrive Without Women,” Says OIF Secretary-General Louise Mushikiwabo
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary General of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF), emphasized the critical role of women in global development, stating that the world cannot progress without them.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary General of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF), emphasized the critical role of women in global development, stating that the world cannot progress without them. She made the remarks on November 19, 2025, while opening the 46th Meeting of Foreign Ministers of OIF member states in Kigali.

The meeting focused on the role of women in development over the past 30 years, with Mushikiwabo highlighting persistent gender inequalities in many member countries. She stressed that women, who make up half of the world’s population, are essential for uniting families, fostering social cohesion, and driving national progress.

“Have we ever considered the role that women should play in uniting the family so that people can live well together? Rwanda knows this. […] I wonder how we are unable to see far ahead, don’t we often hear in public that the world cannot thrive while ignoring half of its population?” Mushikiwabo said.

Globally, out of 8.06 billion people, more than 4.05 billion are women, and in Rwanda, women constitute over 51.5% of the population, according to the 2022 census.

Mushikiwabo urged ministers from OIF member countries to ensure women are fully integrated into all aspects of social, economic, and political life. She said, “I urge ministers to create a new system of family functioning that fully understands the capabilities of women, including in preventing and resolving conflicts, and in promoting well-being in the extended family and at home. Make no mistake! For women to succeed, they need the cooperation of men. Without this, achievements will remain incomplete.”

The President of the Supreme Court of Rwanda, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, praised Rwanda’s progress in advancing women’s rights and inclusion, noting that post-genocide reconstruction prioritized empowering women. He highlighted programs promoting gender equality in government, justice, and other sectors, emphasizing the tangible impact of women in development.

“Thanks to these reforms, we have seen the benefits of women’s participation in every aspect of life. In politics, Rwanda leads the world with 63.7% of MPs being women, and in the justice sector, women make up nearly 50%,” Mukantaganzwa said.

He added that women have played a pivotal role in conflict resolution and reconciliation, particularly in post-genocide Rwanda, citing their contributions as mediators in communities across the country. Mukantaganzwa stressed that in many countries, initiatives for women exist only on paper and urged leaders to translate policies into tangible action.

The OIF Ministerial Meeting brought together participants from 65 countries and marks the first high-level OIF gathering hosted by Rwanda since the organization’s establishment.

title: Ambassador Dushimimana Presents Credentials as Rwanda’s Representative to Lithuania
excerpt: Vilnius, Lithuania - On November 19, 2025, Ambassador Lambert Dushimimana officially assumed his role as Rwanda’s Special Representative to Lithuania after presenting his credentials to President Gitanas Nausėda.
title_en: Ambassador Dushimimana Presents Credentials as Rwanda’s Representative to Lithuania
excerpt_en: Vilnius, Lithuania - On November 19, 2025, Ambassador Lambert Dushimimana officially assumed his role as Rwanda’s Special Representative to Lithuania after presenting his credentials to President Gitanas Nausėda.
body_en:
Vilnius, Lithuania - On November 19, 2025, Ambassador Lambert Dushimimana officially assumed his role as Rwanda’s Special Representative to Lithuania after presenting his credentials to President Gitanas Nausėda. Ambassador Dushimimana currently serves as Rwanda’s Ambassador to the Netherlands.

Following the credentialing ceremony, the two leaders held discussions aimed at strengthening bilateral relations, focusing on trade, investment, and technological cooperation. Ambassador Dushimimana emphasized Rwanda’s interest in collaborating with Lithuanian institutions to foster innovation and development.

The appointment reflects Rwanda’s ongoing efforts to expand its diplomatic presence in Europe and deepen partnerships in strategic sectors such as trade and technology.
