title: President Kagame Receives Gabonese Envoy
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - President Paul Kagame received François Ndong Obiang, Gabon’s Minister of Reforms and Institutional Cooperation, at Village Urugwiro.
title_en: President Kagame Receives Gabonese Envoy
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - President Paul Kagame received François Ndong Obiang, Gabon’s Minister of Reforms and Institutional Cooperation, at Village Urugwiro.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - President Paul Kagame received François Ndong Obiang, Gabon’s Minister of Reforms and Institutional Cooperation, at Village Urugwiro. Minister Obiang delivered a message from President Brice Oligui Nguema of Gabon to President Kagame.

Rwanda and Gabon have maintained diplomatic ties since their respective independences, cooperating through international organizations such as the African Union (AU) and the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF).

Bilateral relations have been strengthened in recent years. In October 2023, President Nguema visited Rwanda, discussing ways to enhance cooperation in education, trade, economy, agriculture, and technology, marking a new era in ties between the two countries.

In November 2024, Rwanda’s Office of the Ombudsman and Gabon’s Commission for the Fight Against Corruption and Financial Crimes signed a cooperation agreement to combat corruption. title_en: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva Commends Switzerland for Opening Embassy in Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva welcomed Ignazio Cassis, Swiss State Secretary for Foreign Affairs, to discuss bilateral relations and Switzerland’s decision to upgrade its…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva welcomed Ignazio Cassis, Swiss State Secretary for Foreign Affairs, to discuss bilateral relations and Switzerland’s decision to upgrade its liaison office in Kigali to a full-fledged embassy. The discussions coincided with Cassis’s attendance at the 46th Ministerial Meeting of the Organization of French-Speaking Countries (OIF).

Prime Minister Nsengiyumva commended Switzerland for attending the Francophonie Ministerial Meeting and praised the government’s decision to open a permanent embassy in Rwanda, calling it a significant milestone in deepening bilateral ties.

“The opening of a Swiss Embassy in Kigali strengthens our diplomatic relations and reflects Switzerland’s commitment to supporting Rwanda’s development. This is a major step in furthering cooperation between our two countries,” the Prime Minister said.

The Swiss Embassy in Kigali was officially inaugurated on 20 November 2025, marking a new chapter in diplomatic engagement. Minister Cassis emphasized that Switzerland will continue to support and promote economic relations, while expanding cooperation across multiple sectors.

Rwanda and Switzerland share a long-standing diplomatic relationship, dating back to the early 1960s, with development cooperation spanning health, education, housing, infrastructure, good governance, and culture. Both governments reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening ties and exploring new opportunities for partnership.

title: Belgian Foreign Minister Visits Kigali Genocide Memorial
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - Vice-Prime Minister and Belgian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, visited the Kigali Genocide Memorial at Gisozi, where he was briefed on the history, causes, and…
title_en: Belgian Foreign Minister Visits Kigali Genocide Memorial
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - Vice-Prime Minister and Belgian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, visited the Kigali Genocide Memorial at Gisozi, where he was briefed on the history, causes, and…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - 20 November 2025 - Vice-Prime Minister and Belgian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, visited the Kigali Genocide Memorial at Gisozi, where he was briefed on the history, causes, and consequences of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi, as well as Rwanda’s journey toward reconciliation and national reconstruction over the past 31 years.

During the visit, Minister Prévot and his delegation paid their respects at the memorial, standing before the remains of the Tutsi victims.

In a social media statement, the memorial emphasized that the delegation was informed about the historical context of the genocide, the truths uncovered, its consequences, and Rwanda’s progress in rebuilding unity and resilience.

Minister Prévot said he was deeply moved by the memorial and the stories of those who perished.

“On behalf of the Belgian Government and people, I once again pay my respects to the victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda. Visiting this memorial revives the memory of the profound and painful suffering that shook our humanity and courage. It is our duty to ensure that such tragedies never happen again, in this region or elsewhere in the world,” he stated.

He reaffirmed Belgium’s commitment to combating genocide denial and ensuring justice for those responsible.

“Belgium will continue this mission with utmost determination. Fighting genocide denial and the trivialization of these crimes is a priority, just as holding the perpetrators accountable in Belgian courts is essential, because impunity is unacceptable. I commend the resilience of the Rwandan people who have overcome this tragic history and built a present and future based on unity, dignity, and progress,” he added.

Minister Prévot is in Rwanda to participate in the 46th Ministerial Meeting of the Organization of Francophone Countries (OIF), hosted in Kigali.

title: Qatar Warns of Deep Mistrust Hindering DRC-AFC/M23 Reconciliation Efforts
excerpt: Doha - November 2025. Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al-Khulaifi, has highlighted the serious challenges facing the reconciliation process between the Democratic Republic of…
title_en: Qatar Warns of Deep Mistrust Hindering DRC-AFC/M23 Reconciliation Efforts
excerpt_en: Doha - November 2025. Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al-Khulaifi, has highlighted the serious challenges facing the reconciliation process between the Democratic Republic of…
body_en:
Doha - November 2025. Qatar’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al-Khulaifi, has highlighted the serious challenges facing the reconciliation process between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebel movement, stressing that the talks remain heavily burdened by deep mistrust between the parties.His remarks follow the November 15, 2025, signing of eight basic principles by representatives of the DRC government and the AFC/M23-an agreement reached after months of talks mediated by Qatar and the United States.

In an exclusive interview with Breitbart, Minister Al-Khulaifi described the signing as “a crucial moment” in efforts to restore peace in the Great Lakes region, but warned that progress remains fragile.

“It is a very difficult task… there is a great deal of mistrust between them,” he said. “The word ‘trust’ is not in the vocabulary of the opposing parties.”

Talks Marked by Tension and Ongoing Fighting

According to the minister, negotiations in Doha, which began in March 2025 after discussions between the Emir of Qatar, President Paul Kagame, and President Félix Tshisekedi, often required mediators to separate the delegations to prevent confrontation.

“Sometimes we abandon direct talks and put them in separate rooms,” he noted, underscoring the volatility of the discussions.

He stressed that the biggest challenge is the continuation of fighting in eastern DRC even as negotiations take place:

“This is not only a political conflict. It is an armed conflict… with civilians being killed.”

The minister described intense last-minute negotiations before the November signing, recalling working “until 8:00 a.m.” to refine key lines of the draft text.

Al-Khulaifi cautioned that implementing the principles will be a “100% difficult” task, given the ongoing hostility and the absence of mutual confidence.

He emphasized the step-by-step approach adopted by Qatar and the U.S., noting that six of the eight principles still require detailed negotiations. Two-prisoner releases and cessation of hostilities-were signed earlier in September and October 2025.

Unlike previous mediation attempts, the Doha talks integrate economic measures as a pillar for long-term stability-an approach the minister called “unique and essential.”

The process has received strong backing from the United States, the African Union, and other international partners-support that Minister Al-Khulaifi says enhances the credibility of the initiative. Still, he cautioned:

“Will it be difficult to implement? Absolutely. Will we face challenges? 100%. But we remain committed, step by step, toward lasting peace.”

Initially, Qatar expected a comprehensive peace agreement in early August, following the July 19 adoption of the principles framework. The deal did not materialize. Under the new timeline agreed on November 15, a final agreement will be signed once both sides negotiate and validate the implementation details of the remaining six principles.

title: Rwanda’s Deputies Launch Nationwide Inspection on Urban Development and Housing
excerpt: The Chamber of Deputies has announced a nationwide tour to assess Government programs related to urban development, housing, and land use planning.
title_en: Rwanda’s Deputies Launch Nationwide Inspection on Urban Development and Housing
excerpt_en: The Chamber of Deputies has announced a nationwide tour to assess Government programs related to urban development, housing, and land use planning.
body_en:
The Chamber of Deputies has announced a nationwide tour to assess Government programs related to urban development, housing, and land use planning. The inspections will take place from 24-29 November 2025 across all provinces and from 5-6 December 2025 in Kigali City, according to a statement released by Parliament.

Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, Kazarwa Gertrude, underscored the importance of direct engagement with citizens to strengthen Government initiatives.“The Parliament supports efforts to improve urban development, housing and land use programs based on the needs of the population. Visiting citizens and speaking to them face-to-face helps us enhance our monitoring and support for programs that contribute to sustainable development,” she said.

Parliament indicated that Deputies will visit 237 Sectors, observing both successful projects-such as urban expansion, housing initiatives, and efficient energy use-and areas where development remains limited. The goal is to work with district and sector leaders to identify solutions and accelerate progress.

During the tour, Deputies will also hold community meetings to encourage residents to settle in designated safe zones, avoid risky locations, and participate actively in maintaining public infrastructure designed to improve their quality of life.

In addition, the Deputies will take part in community work (Umuganda) at the end of November 2025, joining residents in activities aimed at enhancing local development, sanitation, and security within their communities.

title: USA: Banyamulenge Community Urges Washington to Intervene in Ongoing Attacks in Eastern DRC
excerpt: The Banyamulenge community in the United States is appealing to American authorities to intervene and protect their relatives who remain under attack in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
title_en: USA: Banyamulenge Community Urges Washington to Intervene in Ongoing Attacks in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: The Banyamulenge community in the United States is appealing to American authorities to intervene and protect their relatives who remain under attack in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
body_en:
The Banyamulenge community in the United States is appealing to American authorities to intervene and protect their relatives who remain under attack in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The request was published in an open letter by the Mahoro Peace Association, addressed to top U.S. officials including the Secretary of State and members of Congress such as Marco Rubio.

According to the organization’s leader, Douglas Kabunda, the Banyamulenge living in the mountainous areas of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga have faced continuous attacks since 2017, reportedly carried out by the DRC national army (FARDC).

Kabunda stated that Banyamulenge-populated areas in South Kivu are encircled by more than 58 military bases, where soldiers allegedly prevent civilians from accessing markets, healthcare, and humanitarian assistance.

He added that houses and crops have been burned, and drone strikes by FARDC and Burundian forces continue to hit civilian zones as of November 2025, despite the Doha ceasefire agreement.

Kabunda also recalled that on November 12, the spokesperson of the Burundian military, Brig. Gen. Gaspard Baratuza, publicly admitted the blockade of Minembwe, accusing its inhabitants of collaborating with armed groups. Kabunda warned that failing to distinguish civilians from combatants constitutes serious violations of international law, including war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide, given that the Banyamulenge are a targeted ethnic group.

The Mahoro Peace Association is urging the U.S. government to pressure for an end to the blockade, the reopening of supply routes, and the withdrawal of Burundian forces from eastern DRC. The organization is also calling for an independent international commission to investigate alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity, and acts of genocide in the region.

Kabunda noted that military officers from Burundi and the DRC involved in the siege and starvation of Banyamulenge communities could face sanctions, including asset freezes and travel bans to the United States.

From November 23 to 28, members of the Banyamulenge diaspora in the United States are expected to hold protests to amplify their appeal to U.S. leaders.

title: Rwanda Signs Cross-Border Agreement to Protect Migratory Cranes
excerpt: The Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Association (RWCA) has signed cooperation agreements with four conservation organizations in Burundi, Tanzania, and Uganda to strengthen the protection of migratory cranes that regularly…
title_en: Rwanda Signs Cross-Border Agreement to Protect Migratory Cranes
excerpt_en: The Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Association (RWCA) has signed cooperation agreements with four conservation organizations in Burundi, Tanzania, and Uganda to strengthen the protection of migratory cranes that regularly…
body_en:
The Rwanda Wildlife Conservation Association (RWCA) has signed cooperation agreements with four conservation organizations in Burundi, Tanzania, and Uganda to strengthen the protection of migratory cranes that regularly cross into these countries. The agreements were concluded in Kigali on November 21, 2025, during RWCA’s celebration of its 10th anniversary.

Representatives from partner organizations-including Nature Uganda, the International Crane Foundation (Uganda), Nature Tanzania, and the Association Burundaise pour la Protection de la Nature-joined RWCA in formalizing a regional conservation framework. The collaboration will focus on safeguarding 24,904 square kilometers of shared wetland ecosystems.

A joint survey conducted this year revealed the scale of wetlands requiring protection:

1,030 wetlands in Rwanda (82% of the national total),

787 wetlands in Uganda,

266 in Tanzania,

19 in Burundi,

all forming part of interconnected ecosystems frequented by migratory cranes and other wetland species.

RWCA Director General and founder Dr. Olivier Nsengimana noted that cranes and other species are increasingly crossing borders, particularly from wetlands near Akagera, Akanyaru, and Kagitumba. Many do not return, raising concerns about their safety on the other side, especially in wetlands affected by agriculture.

“Some of the cranes equipped with GPS trackers move into neighboring countries, which is why cooperation with local institutions is essential,”Dr. Nsengimana explained, adding that the agreements will facilitate information sharing, community awareness, and joint monitoring.

He emphasized that tracking wildlife across borders comes with logistical barriers-including permits and travel restrictions-making regional collaboration the most practical solution.

Reflecting on RWCA’s first decade, Dr. Nsengimana highlighted significant progress: Rwanda’s wild crane population has risen from fewer than 300 in 2015 to 1,245 today, supported by a conservation team that has grown from five volunteers to 300 permanent staff.

Fidèle Bingwa, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Environment, commended RWCA’s impact, noting that its consistent results have encouraged the government to deepen its commitment to wildlife protection.

title: Peace Talks in Doha, Prisons in Kinshasa: AFC/M23 Challenges the DRC’s Security Leadership
excerpt: The AFC/M23 coalition, which is battling the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has questioned what it calls a glaring contradiction in the country’s leadership-pursuing peace talks in Doha while…
title_en: Peace Talks in Doha, Prisons in Kinshasa: AFC/M23 Challenges the DRC’s Security Leadership
excerpt_en: The AFC/M23 coalition, which is battling the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has questioned what it calls a glaring contradiction in the country’s leadership-pursuing peace talks in Doha while…
body_en:
The AFC/M23 coalition, which is battling the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has questioned what it calls a glaring contradiction in the country’s leadership-pursuing peace talks in Doha while expanding prisons and detaining senior officers in Kinshasa under opaque circumstances.

In recent weeks, several high-ranking FARDC officers - including generals and colonels - have been held for alleged collaboration with the enemy, treason, embezzlement, and attempting to harm the Head of State. The arrests, made without public judicial proceedings, have intensified concerns about due process and political instability.

Among those detained are Gen Christian Tshiwewe, former Chief of Staff of the army and security advisor to President Félix Tshisekedi; Gen Franck Ntumba, former head of military operations at the Presidential Palace; and Brig Gen Benjamin Katende Batubadila, former intelligence chief of the General Staff Guard. Others include John Tshibangu, Commander of the Fourth Military Region, Lt Gen Pacifique Masunzu, and Eric Ruhorimbere Ruhanga.

FARDC spokesperson Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa confirmed on November 22 that several officers have been detained for months, insisting investigations into “serious crimes” were still ongoing.

But AFC/M23 says the explanation is insufficient. In its statement, the group described it as “incomprehensible” that while the government is negotiating peace abroad, it is “building prisons in Kinshasa to detain people illegally.”

The movement accused the government of using these arrests as a political smokescreen, arguing that the generals are victims of injustice and that the official FARDC communication aims to divert public attention.

The detentions have sparked widespread outrage and prompted the Chairman of the AFC/M23 Forum, Corneille Nangaa, to publicly question what he calls the “death of leadership” in Kinshasa.

“How can a civilian detain generals in Kinshasa,” he asked, “while other generals wait their turn for arrest?”

In a message shared via X, Nangaa added:

“In Kinshasa, we are no longer led by leadership. We are led by prison and fear. Twenty FARDC generals are held in Ndolo Military Prison, in inhumane conditions. Two have died, and their bodies have not been recovered. Others have disappeared.”

He accused the government of continuing to add names to an “illegal detention list,” calling it a strategy of intimidation rather than governance.

According to AFC/M23, while the Doha discussions focused on Congolese unity, justice, military cohesion, forgiveness, and transparent governance, the situation in Kinshasa reflects the opposite - marked by arbitrary arrests, military distrust, and a politics of fear.

The group asserts that the Doha process cannot be effective while people “are being arrested without reason” in the DRC.

The movement further warns that the persistent arrests have weakened the army:

“When a regime routinely arrests generals without transparent trials or clear reasons, trust collapses. Generals begin to suspect one another; soldiers begin to doubt. Respect is replaced by fear, and the military becomes fragile.”

A divided and intimidated army, they argue, risks becoming “weak, manipulable, and a source of internal and regional conflict.”

AFC/M23 also raised alarms over what it describes as the targeting of Swahili-speaking officers, a claim the government denies. The group argues that such discrimination, if proven, could have dangerous consequences, recalling the DRC’s long history of division driven by language and identity.

They warned that bringing these divisions into the army is “reckless and short-sighted,” adding that “no regime survives long while mistreating its own army.”

AFC/M23 concluded by saying that unless the government becomes transparent, ends secret detentions, and rebuilds trust within the military, the DRC will continue to project a false image - “looking good in front of the cameras while the army weakens behind the scenes.”
body_fr:
The AFC/M23 coalition, which is battling the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has questioned what it calls a glaring contradiction in the country’s leadership-pursuing peace talks in Doha while expanding prisons and detaining senior officers in Kinshasa under opaque circumstances.

In recent weeks, several high-ranking FARDC officers - including generals and colonels - have been held for alleged collaboration with the enemy, treason, embezzlement, and attempting to harm the Head of State. The arrests, made without public judicial proceedings, have intensified concerns about due process and political instability.

Among those detained are Gen Christian Tshiwewe, former Chief of Staff of the army and security advisor to President Félix Tshisekedi; Gen Franck Ntumba, former head of military operations at the Presidential Palace; and Brig Gen Benjamin Katende Batubadila, former intelligence chief of the General Staff Guard. Others include John Tshibangu, Commander of the Fourth Military Region, Lt Gen Pacifique Masunzu, and Eric Ruhorimbere Ruhanga.

FARDC spokesperson Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa confirmed on November 22 that several officers have been detained for months, insisting investigations into “serious crimes” were still ongoing.

But AFC/M23 says the explanation is insufficient. In its statement, the group described it as “incomprehensible” that while the government is negotiating peace abroad, it is “building prisons in Kinshasa to detain people illegally.”

The movement accused the government of using these arrests as a political smokescreen, arguing that the generals are victims of injustice and that the official FARDC communication aims to divert public attention.

The detentions have sparked widespread outrage and prompted the Chairman of the AFC/M23 Forum, Corneille Nangaa, to publicly question what he calls the “death of leadership” in Kinshasa.

“How can a civilian detain generals in Kinshasa,” he asked, “while other generals wait their turn for arrest?”

In a message shared via X, Nangaa added:

“In Kinshasa, we are no longer led by leadership. We are led by prison and fear. Twenty FARDC generals are held in Ndolo Military Prison, in inhumane conditions. Two have died, and their bodies have not been recovered. Others have disappeared.”

He accused the government of continuing to add names to an “illegal detention list,” calling it a strategy of intimidation rather than governance.

According to AFC/M23, while the Doha discussions focused on Congolese unity, justice, military cohesion, forgiveness, and transparent governance, the situation in Kinshasa reflects the opposite - marked by arbitrary arrests, military distrust, and a politics of fear.

The group asserts that the Doha process cannot be effective while people “are being arrested without reason” in the DRC.

The movement further warns that the persistent arrests have weakened the army:

“When a regime routinely arrests generals without transparent trials or clear reasons, trust collapses. Generals begin to suspect one another; soldiers begin to doubt. Respect is replaced by fear, and the military becomes fragile.”

A divided and intimidated army, they argue, risks becoming “weak, manipulable, and a source of internal and regional conflict.”

AFC/M23 also raised alarms over what it describes as the targeting of Swahili-speaking officers, a claim the government denies. The group argues that such discrimination, if proven, could have dangerous consequences, recalling the DRC’s long history of division driven by language and identity.

They warned that bringing these divisions into the army is “reckless and short-sighted,” adding that “no regime survives long while mistreating its own army.”

AFC/M23 concluded by saying that unless the government becomes transparent, ends secret detentions, and rebuilds trust within the military, the DRC will continue to project a false image - “looking good in front of the cameras while the army weakens behind the scenes.”

title: President Faustin-Archange Touadéra of the Central African Republic Arrives in Kigali
excerpt: Kigali, November 23, 2025 - The President of the Central African Republic (CAR), Faustin-Archange Touadéra, arrived in Kigali on a working visit, announced the Rwandan Ministry of Foreign Affairs via X.
title_en: President Faustin-Archange Touadéra of the Central African Republic Arrives in Kigali
excerpt_en: Kigali, November 23, 2025 - The President of the Central African Republic (CAR), Faustin-Archange Touadéra, arrived in Kigali on a working visit, announced the Rwandan Ministry of Foreign Affairs via X.
body_en:
Kigali, November 23, 2025 - The President of the Central African Republic (CAR), Faustin-Archange Touadéra, arrived in Kigali on a working visit, announced the Rwandan Ministry of Foreign Affairs via X. The two-day visit aims to strengthen the longstanding bilateral relations between the two countries, particularly in the security sector.

President Touadéra was received by Dr. Vincent Biruta, Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security, highlighting the strategic importance of the visit.

Rwanda has been a major security partner of the CAR for over a decade. In 2014, the Rwandan Armed Forces were deployed to the CAR under the African Union mission (MISCA) to restore peace after the outbreak of conflicts in 2012, especially against armed groups that later formed the Séléka coalition, which had attempted a coup d’état.

Rwandan troops later joined the UN mission (MINUSCA), protecting civilians, UN equipment, and the Head of State and his family. Rwanda also contributed to the training of Central African soldiers, with the third batch of 438 soldiers completing training in March 2025. The program included enemy reconnaissance, military tactics, map usage, and field exercises.

Beyond security, Rwanda has supported the health and well-being of the CAR population. In February 2025, both countries signed a security cooperation agreement to further strengthen bilateral defense collaboration.

President Touadéra’s visit comes just weeks before the CAR presidential elections, scheduled for December 2025, in which he has announced he will seek re-election.

title: President Kagame and Touadéra Discuss Security for December 2025 Elections
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - November 24, 2025 - President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and Central African Republic (CAR) President Faustin-Archange Touadéra held high-level talks focused on security for the December 28, 2025…
title_en: President Kagame and Touadéra Discuss Security for December 2025 Elections
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - November 24, 2025 - President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and Central African Republic (CAR) President Faustin-Archange Touadéra held high-level talks focused on security for the December 28, 2025…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - November 24, 2025 - President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and Central African Republic (CAR) President Faustin-Archange Touadéra held high-level talks focused on security for the December 28, 2025 presidential elections and on strengthening bilateral relations.

President Touadéra, on a working visit to Rwanda, announced on social media, particularly X, that the discussions included electoral security and ways to reinforce friendship and cooperation between the two countries.

He stated, “Yesterday in Kigali, I met with President Paul Kagame to discuss security for the elections scheduled for December 28 and to strengthen friendship and cooperation between our countries. Rwanda’s assistance and increased investment in the CAR strengthen our strong partnership.”

Rwanda has been deeply involved in the Central African Republic since 2014, deploying troops as part of UN peacekeeping missions (MINUSCA) and to counter rebels led by François Bozizé. In 2020, Rwandan troops were sent to ensure election security, monitoring the polls held on December 27, 2020, which resulted in Touadéra’s second-term election.

Through bilateral agreements, Rwanda has also trained Central African soldiers, with the third batch of 438 graduates completing their training in March 2025. The Rwandan Armed Forces have since been a key presence in peacekeeping, protecting the Head of State, and contributing to stability and security.

In 2023, the CAR constitution was amended via referendum, extending the presidential term from five to seven years, allowing Touadéra to seek re-election after nine years in power. He first assumed office in 2006 following a five-year tenure as Prime Minister.

For the 2025 elections, Touadéra is expected to face Anicet-Georges Dologuélé, a former Prime Minister (1999-2001) and ex-President of the Central African Development Bank (BDEAC) (2001-2010), recognized for his expertise in economics, development projects, and financial management in the region.

title: DRC Government Spokesperson Says Eastern Conflict Represents Only a ‘Small Portion’ of National Territory
excerpt: KINSHASA - Democratic Republic of Congo Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya Katembwe has described the ongoing conflict in the eastern part of the country as a “minor issue” when viewed in relation to the nation’s…
title_en: DRC Government Spokesperson Says Eastern Conflict Represents Only a ‘Small Portion’ of National Territory
excerpt_en: KINSHASA - Democratic Republic of Congo Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya Katembwe has described the ongoing conflict in the eastern part of the country as a “minor issue” when viewed in relation to the nation’s…
body_en:
KINSHASA - Democratic Republic of Congo Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya Katembwe has described the ongoing conflict in the eastern part of the country as a “minor issue” when viewed in relation to the nation’s vast territory.

Eastern DRC has endured decades of insecurity fueled by the presence of hundreds of armed groups, with violence intensifying in November 2021 when M23 rebels resumed fighting, accusing President Félix Tshisekedi of failing to implement commitments made during earlier peace negotiations.

Speaking to reporters on November 26, 2025, Muyaya said the scale of the conflict is often misunderstood.

He argued that although the situation is serious, it affects only a limited portion of the country:“I don’t want to downplay the crisis because it concerns us all, but what percentage does it represent out of 2,345,410 square kilometers?”

Muyaya added that many people mistakenly believe the entire country is engulfed in conflict, whereas the violence is concentrated in a specific region.

His comments echo earlier remarks by Jules Alingete, the former Auditor General, who in April 2022 stated that the fighting in the east had not significantly impacted the rest of the country because it was taking place nearly 2,000 kilometers from Kinshasa.

Alingete made those comments at a time when heavy clashes were ongoing in Rutshuru Territory, North Kivu, where government forces were struggling to hold their positions.

title: Kagame Accuses Europe of Longstanding Exploitation of DRC Minerals: “They Looted More Than Anyone Else”
excerpt: KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has sharply criticized European countries for what he described as centuries-long exploitation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mineral wealth, arguing that Europe should not be quick…
title_en: Kagame Accuses Europe of Longstanding Exploitation of DRC Minerals: “They Looted More Than Anyone Else”
excerpt_en: KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has sharply criticized European countries for what he described as centuries-long exploitation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mineral wealth, arguing that Europe should not be quick…
body_en:
KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has sharply criticized European countries for what he described as centuries-long exploitation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mineral wealth, arguing that Europe should not be quick to accuse Rwanda of smuggling precious minerals from its neighbor.

Speaking during a press conference on November 27, 2025, Kagame said that European powers-historically and even today-have profited extensively from resources originating in the DRC, despite lacking any significant mineral deposits of their own.

“They Have Looted More Than Anyone Else”

Responding to renewed accusations that Rwanda benefits from smuggled minerals originating in the eastern DRC, Kagame said: “They have looted them more than anyone else I have ever known in the world. They trade precious stones in Antwerp. Diamonds-do they mine diamonds? Do they have gold mines?”

He argued that Europe’s legacy of exploitation remains visible today, pointing to the Antwerp Diamond District, one of the world’s biggest trading hubs, built on stones sourced largely from Africa, particularly Congo.

European involvement in Congo’s mineral exploitation dates back to the colonial era. Between 1885 and 1960, Belgium extracted enormous quantities of diamonds, gold, copper, ivory, and other valuable resources during its rule over what was then known as the Congo Free State and later the Belgian Congo.

Kagame said this history undermines the credibility of European states when they point fingers at Rwanda today.

Rwanda Says It Has Followed Transparency Measures

Kagame revealed that Rwanda had engaged in extensive verification processes, in collaboration with European partners, to certify the origin of minerals exported from Rwanda.

According to him, Rwanda “went through all the steps” required for transparency in mineral trade but faced political interference: “There were cooperation agreements we were ready to sign with Europe. A lot was done regarding verification. Surprisingly, the DRC came and said: ‘Don’t sign anything with them.’”

The president maintained that Rwanda’s mineral exports follow legal channels and do not originate from conflict zones.

Kagame criticized what he sees as a pattern of repeated accusations that eventually shape international opinion.

He said: “Some Congolese sell minerals through Rwanda, Burundi, Uganda or other neighbors. But when it comes to precious stones, they always speak about Rwanda because they have heard these accusations many times.”

Figures for 2024/2025 show that Rwanda earned $1.7 billion from mineral exports, driven largely by the expansion of professional mining and value-addition industries.Kagame said these reforms aim to shift Rwanda from raw exports toward processing and refining.

Kagame Questions International Silence on FDLR’s Role in Mineral Smuggling

The president also criticized what he described as the international community’s lack of attention to the role of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR)-a militia operating in eastern DRC since the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

“Why Is the FDLR Being Acquitted?”

Kagame said that for years, the FDLR has controlled parts of Goma and surrounding areas-regions central to today’s conflict-but has not been scrutinized regarding mineral trafficking.

He asked: “Why is the FDLR being acquitted when we report on it every day? They say it is small. If they think it is small, they should come and speak with those recently repatriated from the DRC. They will give you information.”

It is estimated that between 7,000 and 10,000 FDLR fighters remain active, including those integrated within FARDC units, those working with local militias supported by the government, and independent cells.

Kagame stated that some of these fighters are involved in mining activities in eastern Congo:“Where do they sell the minerals? It seems they end up in Europe, and then Rwanda is blamed.”

The president suggested that European narratives often shape global opinion, regardless of facts: “Sometimes they exaggerate. People think what they say is the truth, yet they are the ones who have played a major role in this issue.”

title: Kagame Questions Legitimacy of Guinea-Bissau Coup: “I Don’t Believe It”
excerpt: KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has expressed doubts about the reported overthrow of Guinea-Bissau’s President Umaro Sissoco Embaló, saying he still does not fully believe the coup took place as presented.
title_en: Kagame Questions Legitimacy of Guinea-Bissau Coup: “I Don’t Believe It”
excerpt_en: KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has expressed doubts about the reported overthrow of Guinea-Bissau’s President Umaro Sissoco Embaló, saying he still does not fully believe the coup took place as presented.
body_en:
KIGALI - President Paul Kagame has expressed doubts about the reported overthrow of Guinea-Bissau’s President Umaro Sissoco Embaló, saying he still does not fully believe the coup took place as presented. Speaking during a press briefing on November 27, 2025, Kagame said the circumstances surrounding the event remain unclear to him.

Responding to a question from The New Times journalist James Munyaneza, Kagame reflected on the rise of coups d’État across Africa in recent years, warning that they often reveal deeper, unresolved political or governance problems.

“I Still Don’t Know What Happened”

Kagame said his first reaction to reports of the Guinea-Bissau coup was skepticism.

“When I heard about the coup in Guinea-Bissau, I still don’t know what happened,” he said.“When I heard it, I thought someone carried out the coup himself. I didn’t think it was a real coup. I still need more time to confirm it.”

The president added that the increasing number of coups on the continent suggests widespread structural issues that have long been ignored.

Coups as a Symptom of Deeper Problems

Kagame argued that in most cases, coups do not occur spontaneously. “Where coups are happening, there is something wrong,” he said. According to him, at least 90% of coups emerge from grievances that leaders or their international partners have refused to acknowledge.

He criticized what he described as a pattern in which Western countries publicly praise certain leaders for years, only to shift positions when crises erupt. “These coups happen by telling these people that you have been lying to us for some time,” he said.

“Good Coups” vs “Bad Coups”

In one of the more striking parts of his remarks, Kagame distinguished between what he called “good” and “bad” coups.

He defined a bad coup as one driven by opportunism or military arrogance: “Someone who thinks that because he has a gun he can overthrow the government-that is bad.”

However, he said there are situations where a coup may be a response to entrenched corruption or abuse: “If a person or a group says: enough is enough, this person has lied to us, has stolen from us, has exploited us-and they act-then I think I have no problem with it.”

For a coup to be considered “good,” Kagame said, the new leadership must govern differently from the regime it removed and show meaningful change.

Youth Protests Across Africa: “Give Them Space”

Kagame also commented on recent waves of youth-led protests in Kenya, Madagascar, Tanzania and other regions, where demonstrators have taken to the streets against corruption, mismanagement, or social inequality.

While acknowledging that some methods used by protesters may be misguided, he said leaders must not ignore the underlying grievances.“Before they do that, it is our responsibility to do something so that they have no reason to do so,” he emphasized.

Kagame stressed the importance of opening channels of dialogue with young people and ensuring that governance is transparent and responsive. “Every country has problems, and citizens may not get what they want when they want it,” he said, adding that it is the responsibility of leaders to explain decisions clearly and build trust.

title: AFC/M23 Leader Advocates for Federalism and Renaming of the DRC
excerpt: Goma, 27 November 2025 - Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government, has called for a major overhaul of the country’s governance, including a…
title_en: AFC/M23 Leader Advocates for Federalism and Renaming of the DRC
excerpt_en: Goma, 27 November 2025 - Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government, has called for a major overhaul of the country’s governance, including a…
body_en:
Goma, 27 November 2025 - Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, leader of the AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government, has called for a major overhaul of the country’s governance, including a proposal to rename it the Federal Republic of Congo (RFC).

Speaking at a seminar in Goma, Nangaa emphasized that the DRC, which has undergone five name changes since colonial times, requires a governance system that empowers provinces and respects local autonomy. The current name, Democratic Republic of Congo, was adopted by Laurent-Désiré Kabila in 1997 after he overthrew Mobutu Sese Seko.

Nangaa outlined the coalition’s vision of a federal system, where provinces would have substantial independence, including control over mining, agriculture, livestock, tourism, culture, forestry, infrastructure, and energy. title: Mozambique President Visits Rwandan Security Forces in Cabo Delgado
excerpt: Ancuabe District, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique ; November 29, 2025 - President Daniel Francisco Chapo of Mozambique paid an official visit to the Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province, emphasizing…
title_en: Mozambique President Visits Rwandan Security Forces in Cabo Delgado
excerpt_en: Ancuabe District, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique ; November 29, 2025 - President Daniel Francisco Chapo of Mozambique paid an official visit to the Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province, emphasizing…
body_en:
Ancuabe District, Cabo Delgado, Mozambique ; November 29, 2025 - President Daniel Francisco Chapo of Mozambique paid an official visit to the Rwandan Security Forces (RSF) deployed in Cabo Delgado Province, emphasizing the critical role of international cooperation in combating terrorism.

President Chapo was accompanied by senior Mozambican officials, including Minister of Defense Maj Gen Cristovão Artur Chume, Commander-in-Chief of the FADM Gen Julio dos Santos Jane, Commander-in-Chief of the Land Forces Maj Gen André Rafael Mahunguane, and the Cabo Delgado Provincial Administration led by Valige Tauabo. The delegation was received by Maj Gen Vincent Gatama, Head of Rwandan Security Forces.

During the visit, Chapo received a detailed briefing on the security situation in the areas where Rwandan forces operate. The discussions highlighted the ongoing collaboration between the Rwandan and Mozambican security forces in counter-terrorism operations across the Ancuabe District.

“I am very grateful to the Rwandan Armed Forces for the excellent work they are doing in Mozambique, which has brought peace and security to this region,” President Chapo said. “Continue to work with your brothers and sisters here, because no progress can be achieved without peace and security.”

The Mozambican President stressed that terrorism is a global challenge, not confined to Mozambique, and highlighted the importance of unity, strong cooperation, and seamless collaboration between the Rwandan and Mozambican forces. He also noted that long-term development projects in the province depend on maintaining peace and security.

The visit underscores Rwanda’s growing role in regional security operations, particularly in supporting countries facing extremist threats, and reflects the close military cooperation between the two nations in Cabo Delgado.

title: President Kagame Issues Strong Statement on Goma Amid Escalating Regional Tensions
excerpt: Kigali, November 27, 2025 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame made pointed remarks from the capital, Kigali, regarding the city of Goma in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in a statement that has…
title_en: President Kagame Issues Strong Statement on Goma Amid Escalating Regional Tensions
excerpt_en: Kigali, November 27, 2025 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame made pointed remarks from the capital, Kigali, regarding the city of Goma in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in a statement that has…
body_en:
Kigali, November 27, 2025 - Rwandan President Paul Kagame made pointed remarks from the capital, Kigali, regarding the city of Goma in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in a statement that has stirred tensions and provoked strong reactions in Kinshasa.

“If I were in charge of Goma and you came to me and said you wanted to take control, I would tell you: no problem. But Goma is in my hands. I will not hand it over to you until you show me how you intend to solve my problems,” Kagame declared. He further emphasized, “I cannot ask anyone to do me a favor to ensure Rwanda's safety or that my rights are respected… If you don't give me my rights, then we will fight, that's clear.”

These statements, both provocative and strategic, come amid the resurgence of clashes in eastern DRC between the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) and the M23 rebels, whom Kinshasa accuses Kigali of supporting-a charge the Rwandan government denies. By referring to a form of “guardianship” over Goma, a border city and major economic hub, Kagame appeared to link the stability of eastern Congo directly to Rwanda’s national security concerns.

The remarks have triggered strong criticism in the DRC, where officials and citizens view them as an infringement on national sovereignty. Many questions have arisen over what Kagame meant by Rwanda’s “rights” in Goma and the surrounding region. Critics argue that, under international law, no country has a claim over the territory, resources, or sovereignty of another state, and that security concerns should never justify threats or the imposition of armed force on a neighboring nation.

Does Kagame’s reference to “rights” imply a claim over Congolese mineral resources?

Does it signal approval or protection of armed groups operating in eastern DRC under the guise of security?

Could it suggest an effort to redraw borders or influence the political future of millions of Congolese?

Kinshasa has reiterated that the DRC owes Rwanda nothing-not land, resources, or sovereignty-and that the Congolese people retain their right to peace, territorial integrity, and national dignity. Observers note that while regional diplomacy seeks de-escalation, statements like Kagame’s risk reigniting tensions between the two nations, already strained by decades of cross-border conflicts, mutual accusations, and allegations of interference.

As the situation unfolds, the international community continues to call for calm and dialogue, emphasizing that sovereignty and security must be respected for lasting peace in the Great Lakes region.

Economy and Tech.

title: Rehabilitation and Widening of Rubengera-Nyange Road Completed
excerpt: Rubengera, Rwanda - The Rwanda Transport Development Authority (RTDA) has announced the full completion of the 37.15-kilometer Rubengera-Rambura-Nyange road, marking a major milestone in the rehabilitation and widening…
title_en: Rehabilitation and Widening of Rubengera-Nyange Road Completed
excerpt_en: Rubengera, Rwanda - The Rwanda Transport Development Authority (RTDA) has announced the full completion of the 37.15-kilometer Rubengera-Rambura-Nyange road, marking a major milestone in the rehabilitation and widening…
body_en:
Rubengera, Rwanda - The Rwanda Transport Development Authority (RTDA) has announced the full completion of the 37.15-kilometer Rubengera-Rambura-Nyange road, marking a major milestone in the rehabilitation and widening of the Karongi-Muhanga road corridor.

The project, which addressed years of damage to the road since its original construction, aims to improve connectivity across the region. According to RTDA, the remaining Nyange-Muhanga section is progressing well, and once completed, the road will link seamlessly with other major arteries, including the Kivu-Belt and Kigali-Huye roads.

The expansion and rehabilitation works have also revitalized the commercial centers of Rubengera, Rugabano, and Nyange, enabling easier movement of vehicles, including public transport, cargo, and private cars, which has helped local traders attract more customers.

The Muhanga-Karongi road, spanning 128 kilometers, was originally completed in two phases, with the first section finished in 2000 and the second in 2002. Roads constructed in Rwanda are designed to last at least 20 years, and with proper maintenance, some can remain in service for up to 30 years.

RTDA noted that the road plays a critical role in Rwanda’s economy, facilitating trade between the Western and Southern provinces and Kigali City, while also serving tourists traveling to destinations such as Rutsiro, Karongi, and Nyamasheke.

title: Rwandan Entrepreneurs Receive 175 Million Frw to Expand Innovative Projects
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - In a move to support innovation and entrepreneurship, 35 Rwandan projects were awarded a total of 175 million Frw under the Ongera Igishoro program, organized by the Ministry of Public Works and Labor…
title_en: Rwandan Entrepreneurs Receive 175 Million Frw to Expand Innovative Projects
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - In a move to support innovation and entrepreneurship, 35 Rwandan projects were awarded a total of 175 million Frw under the Ongera Igishoro program, organized by the Ministry of Public Works and Labor…
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - In a move to support innovation and entrepreneurship, 35 Rwandan projects were awarded a total of 175 million Frw under the Ongera Igishoro program, organized by the Ministry of Public Works and Labor (MIFOTRA) in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and other partners. The awards ceremony took place on November 18, 2025, in Kigali.

The selected projects, which include ventures such as producing beef jerky and flour from potatoes and cassava, were implemented by Rwandans who had received training abroad. Each of the 35 winners received 5 million Frw to expand their activities and increase operational capital.

Before the awards, a short-term business training course was conducted for 100 participants, of whom the 35 most promising projects were chosen. In 2024, the program trained 60 participants and awarded 33 projects, which have since created jobs for over 100 people.

The awards primarily focused on projects aimed at adding value to agricultural products (80%), as well as initiatives leveraging technology, tourism, and hospitality.

Mugwaneza Fina, who received training in food processing in Russia, will use her award to produce a flour combining cassava and potatoes, designed to replicate wheat flour but without gluten. She explained, “The cassava flour available in our market cannot be made into flour. Adding potatoes creates a good flour that works like normal. This will benefit people with health restrictions and can be used to make bread, mandazi, and other products.”

Ingabire Rwibutso Denys Clément, trained in Israel, plans to produce cow salt locally, reducing reliance on imported salt. “Imported packages cost 6,500 Rwf for five kilos, which many farmers cannot afford. My project will produce smaller one-kilo packages for around 1,000 Rwf. Ingredients are already available locally, including maize residues, bone meal, regular salt, cow dung, and sugarcane waste,” he said. The plan is to produce at least 3,000 packets per month.

Kabiligi Clément, Permanent Secretary of MIFOTRA, emphasized that supporting such initiatives aligns with Rwanda’s vision of economic and social development, leveraging the skills Rwandans acquire abroad. “These projects improve livelihoods and contribute to job creation, especially for youth,” he said.

Erika De Bona Fofana, Deputy Director of IOM in Rwanda, praised the recipients, saying, “These youth are not waiting for opportunities-they are creating them and leading the way in employment generation.”

The Ongera Igishoro program continues to provide both financial and technical support to foster innovation and entrepreneurship, particularly among Rwandans who have gained knowledge and skills abroad.

title: Residents of Akagera National Park to Benefit from 1.2 Billion Rwf in Tourism Revenue
excerpt: Kayonza, Rwanda - 19 November 2025 - Residents living around Akagera National Park are set to receive 1.285 billion Rwf in revenue from tourism during the 2025/2026 financial year, the Park administration announced.
title_en: Residents of Akagera National Park to Benefit from 1.2 Billion Rwf in Tourism Revenue
excerpt_en: Kayonza, Rwanda - 19 November 2025 - Residents living around Akagera National Park are set to receive 1.285 billion Rwf in revenue from tourism during the 2025/2026 financial year, the Park administration announced.
body_en:
Kayonza, Rwanda - 19 November 2025 - Residents living around Akagera National Park are set to receive 1.285 billion Rwf in revenue from tourism during the 2025/2026 financial year, the Park administration announced. This initiative is being carried out in collaboration with the three Eastern Province districts that share the park: Kayonza, Gatsibo, and Nyagatare.

The revenue distribution will see Kayonza District receive 857 million Rwf, Gatsibo 142 million Rwf, and Nyagatare 285 million Rwf. To ensure that the funds are used effectively, the Park administration and district authorities have launched a campaign to engage residents, seeking their input on potential projects to be funded.

During meetings in Rwinkwavu, Kabare, and Ndego sectors, Kayonza District Mayor Nyemazi John Bosco praised residents for offering ideas focused on community development. He assured participants that their suggestions would guide project implementation.

Some of the proposed projects include the construction of a youth center with health services, improvements in access to clean water, and the renovation and expansion of local health centers. Residents emphasized that these initiatives would help address issues such as teenage pregnancies, HIV prevention, and general health accessibility.

Mayor Nyemazi also reminded residents of the importance of protecting the park from poachers, noting that sustainable conservation directly contributes to their income from tourism.

Last year, Akagera National Park generated $4.7 million in revenue, highlighting its critical role in supporting local development across Nyagatare, Gatsibo, and Kayonza districts.

title: Rwandan Traders Hit by Delays as Tanzanian Post-Election Unrest Disrupts Dar es Salaam Port
excerpt: Rwandan traders and manufacturers are counting losses after post-election unrest in Tanzania disrupted operations at the Dar es Salaam port, blocking cargo routes and delaying shipments.
title_en: Rwandan Traders Hit by Delays as Tanzanian Post-Election Unrest Disrupts Dar es Salaam Port
excerpt_en: Rwandan traders and manufacturers are counting losses after post-election unrest in Tanzania disrupted operations at the Dar es Salaam port, blocking cargo routes and delaying shipments.
body_en:
Rwandan traders and manufacturers are counting losses after post-election unrest in Tanzania disrupted operations at the Dar es Salaam port, blocking cargo routes and delaying shipments. The disturbances followed the October 29, 2025 presidential elections, which sparked protests - largely driven by youth - over allegations of unfairness after opposition figures, including CHADEMA’s Tundu Lissu, were jailed and barred from running.

Manufacturers relying on raw materials routed through Dar es Salaam say the delays have slowed production and strained supply chains.

Nteziyaremye Bercar, Production Manager at Multiple Packaging Rwanda Ltd, told RBA that several consignments stalled at the port, forcing temporary shutdowns.

“The unrest caused some of our materials to remain stuck in Dar es Salaam, which forced us to stop. Some shipments are only arriving now, while others are still held back,” he said on November 23, 2025. “This has affected our production and our customers, because there are items we should have delivered but couldn’t.”

The impact has been equally severe for Amaco Paints, where production has reportedly dropped by half. Sales manager Ndayisenga Emmanuel said shortages of imported inputs left factories unable to operate normally.

“If the materials do not arrive, we cannot produce. Without them, we cannot supply our customers as required. The numbers have dropped so much that our production has been heavily affected,” he said.

Regional trade institutions say they are assessing the situation and seeking solutions to the transport disruptions.

Dr. John Deng Diar Ding, Executive Secretary of the Northern Corridor, confirmed that cargo destined for Rwanda was rerouted.

“After the post-election violence in Tanzania, goods meant for Rwanda were immediately diverted to Mombasa. We are closely monitoring these obstacles,” he noted.

Despite the delays, the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) says the situation is under surveillance and does not expect significant pressure on domestic prices of imported goods.

The port of Dar es Salaam is a vital gateway for Rwanda and other landlocked countries in the region, handling a substantial volume of regional imports and exports. Any disruption, analysts warn, has immediate ripple effects across supply chains and national production lines.

title: Rwanda Wins 10 Medals at 2025 African Cycling Championships
excerpt: Ukunda, Kenya, November 23, 2025 - Rwanda concluded the four-day 2025 African Cycling Championships with a strong performance, finishing third overall with 10 medals, including two golds.
title_en: Rwanda Wins 10 Medals at 2025 African Cycling Championships
excerpt_en: Ukunda, Kenya, November 23, 2025 - Rwanda concluded the four-day 2025 African Cycling Championships with a strong performance, finishing third overall with 10 medals, including two golds.
body_en:
Ukunda, Kenya, November 23, 2025 - Rwanda concluded the four-day 2025 African Cycling Championships with a strong performance, finishing third overall with 10 medals, including two golds. The 19th edition of the Championships saw 30 countries compete across men's, women's, under-23, under-19, and under-17 categories.

The final day featured road races in the men's and boys' under-23 and under-19 categories, where Eritrea dominated. In the men's 163.8km race, Merhawi Kudus took gold, followed by his compatriot Aman Awet, clocking three hours, 53 minutes, and six seconds, just five seconds behind Algeria’s Mimouni Oussama Abdellah.

title: Rusizi: Two Killed in Gold Mine Collapse
excerpt: RUSIZI - Two miners died on November 26, 2025, after being trapped in a collapsed gold mine in Byimana Village, Rwambogo Cell, in the Butare Sector of Rusizi District.
title_en: Rusizi: Two Killed in Gold Mine Collapse
excerpt_en: RUSIZI - Two miners died on November 26, 2025, after being trapped in a collapsed gold mine in Byimana Village, Rwambogo Cell, in the Butare Sector of Rusizi District.
body_en:
RUSIZI - Two miners died on November 26, 2025, after being trapped in a collapsed gold mine in Byimana Village, Rwambogo Cell, in the Butare Sector of Rusizi District.

The victims were identified as Tuyishime Wilson, 24, and Habumukiza Alexis, 45, both residents of the sector. The mine was being operated legally under New Kush Rwanda Ltd, which immediately alerted local authorities when the incident occurred.

According to the Executive Secretary of the Butare Sector, Ntibizera Jean Pierre, rescue efforts began as soon as the alarm was raised.

“We instructed the team to extract them as quickly as possible. By 9:00 a.m., they had been pulled out, but unfortunately both were already deceased,” he said.

Initial findings indicate that the collapse was triggered by unstable, rain-soaked soil following several days of heavy rainfall.

Local officials have urged mining operators to strengthen safety precautions, especially during the rainy season.

The bodies of the two men were transferred to Mibilizi Hospital for post-mortem examination before burial.

title: UAE and DRC Lead Rwanda’s Export Destinations in 2024/25
excerpt: Kigali, November 27, 2025 - The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) emerged as Rwanda’s top export destinations in the 2024/25 fiscal year, according to a recent report by the Rwanda…
title_en: UAE and DRC Lead Rwanda’s Export Destinations in 2024/25
excerpt_en: Kigali, November 27, 2025 - The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) emerged as Rwanda’s top export destinations in the 2024/25 fiscal year, according to a recent report by the Rwanda…
body_en:
Kigali, November 27, 2025 - The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) emerged as Rwanda’s top export destinations in the 2024/25 fiscal year, according to a recent report by the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA).

Rwanda earned a total of Rwf 3,955.5 billion from various exports during this period. Of this, exports to the UAE accounted for Rwf 2,205.8 billion, representing 60.1% of total export earnings. The DRC followed with exports valued at Rwf 375.4 billion.

Other notable export destinations included the Netherlands (Rwf 218.8 billion), Belgium (Rwf 195 billion), Sweden (Rwf 194.9 billion), China (Rwf 144.3 billion), Luxembourg (Rwf 72.5 billion), Kenya (Rwf 59.1 billion), the United States (Rwf 53.4 billion), and Switzerland (Rwf 49.7 billion).

The RRA report highlighted the diversity of Rwanda’s exports:

Processed goods sent directly to consumers: Rwf 1,907.8 billion

Capital and raw materials: Rwf 862 billion

Processed goods requiring additional processing abroad: Rwf 33 billion

The export mix demonstrates Rwanda’s progress in industrialization and agricultural reform, with a focus on adding value to goods before export.

Rwanda’s precious metals sector, including Gasegereti, Coltan, Wolfram, and Gold, generated $1.6 billion in export earnings for 2024/25. Coffee and tea exports to countries such as Belgium, the Netherlands, and Japan also saw significant growth.

The National Agricultural Export Board (NAEB) reported that Rwanda exported 4,200 tons of avocados in 2024/25, compared to just 1,000 tons in 2019. Avocado exports reach Europe, China, India, and Arab countries, where 80% of raw avocados are consumed. Rwanda recently signed an agreement allowing exports of avocados to China, further expanding its market.

Other notable export products include industrial cooking oil, processed agricultural products such as cereal, wheat, and maize flour, and manufactured goods from household appliance and construction equipment industries. By 2024, Rwanda had:

85 large-scale agro-processing industries and 608 medium-scale industries

91 large-scale and 398 medium-scale factories producing household appliances

38 large-scale and 82 medium-scale manufacturers producing construction equipment

Rwanda aims to increase its exports by 13% annually until 2029, as part of its five-year development plan. The report shows that Rwanda’s export markets have expanded, allowing total exports to grow by 16% in 2024/25.

The government’s focus on industrialization, value addition, and diversification of agricultural products is positioning Rwanda as a competitive player in global markets.

title: Rwanda Police Report Over 300 Road Accidents in Kigali in Three Months
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda-The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has revealed that more than 300 road accidents were recorded in Kigali City between August and October 2025, with several resulting in fatalities.
title_en: Rwanda Police Report Over 300 Road Accidents in Kigali in Three Months
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda-The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has revealed that more than 300 road accidents were recorded in Kigali City between August and October 2025, with several resulting in fatalities.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda-The Rwanda National Police (RNP) has revealed that more than 300 road accidents were recorded in Kigali City between August and October 2025, with several resulting in fatalities. The figures were announced on November 17, 2025, by RNP Spokesperson ACP Boniface Rutikanga during the ongoing Turindane-Tugereyo Amahoro road safety campaign.

The latest phase of the campaign was held in Magerwa, Gikondo, where truck drivers, public transport operators, cyclists, and pedestrians gathered for safety sensitization activities.

ACP Rutikanga noted that the majority of recent accidents in Kigali involve motorcyclists.“In the past three months, we have had about 300 accidents here in Kigali City, though most of them were not very serious,” he said. He added that no passenger buses were involved in accidents during the same period.

During the event, DCG Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, the Deputy Commissioner General of Police in charge of Administration and Personnel, urged road users to avoid behaviors that increase the risk of accidents. “Drivers should avoid distractions,” she said. “Prepare properly before leaving home, avoid overspeeding, and respect traffic signs.”

She further warned against using mobile phones while driving and emphasized that drinking and driving remains a major cause of fatal crashes.

Kigali City Mayor Samuel Dusengiyumva commended the police for their continued commitment to reducing road accidents through countrywide awareness campaigns.“We thank the police leadership for this initiative. The Turindane Tugereyo Amahoro program reflects strong collaboration between government institutions, local authorities, and security agencies to ensure safety for all,” he said.

National data shows a fluctuating but persistent rise in road accidents over the years. Rwanda recorded 621 accidents in 2021, 676 in 2022, 761 in 2023, 751 in 2024, and 719 accidents in the first nine months of 2025, underscoring the urgency of ongoing safety efforts.

title: Rwanda Sees 20% Surge in Flu Cases as Health Ministry Urges Parental Vigilance
excerpt: Kigali-Rwanda is experiencing a 20% increase in flu cases, prompting the Ministry of Health to urge parents and schools to take extra precautions. Minister of Health Dr.
title_en: Rwanda Sees 20% Surge in Flu Cases as Health Ministry Urges Parental Vigilance
excerpt_en: Kigali-Rwanda is experiencing a 20% increase in flu cases, prompting the Ministry of Health to urge parents and schools to take extra precautions. Minister of Health Dr.
body_en:
Kigali-Rwanda is experiencing a 20% increase in flu cases, prompting the Ministry of Health to urge parents and schools to take extra precautions. Minister of Health Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana issued the warning during an interview with RBA on 17 November in Kigali, following a noticeable rise in infections across the country in recent days. The situation has already turned tragic in Rubavu District, where three children died from flu-related complications.

Dr. Nsanzimana reassured the public that the country is not facing an epidemic, but stressed that heightened vigilance is essential as cases are likely to continue rising.

“The message we would like to give to people is that they should not be afraid of another epidemic,” he said. “We encourage them to avoid infecting others because a person with flu can infect those with low immunity and they will fall ill.”

The minister noted that hospitals have recorded a 20% rise in flu patients, and authorities anticipate a further surge in December. Seasonal patterns indicate that flu cases typically climb during the rainy season.

Schools remain a particular concern, as children often play in close proximity, increasing the risk of transmission. Dr. Nsanzimana called on parents to keep sick children at home until they fully recover, stressing that sending them to school could worsen the spread and endanger other children.

During this rainy period, the Ministry of Health is encouraging citizens to take preventive measures including frequent handwashing, regular physical exercise, wearing masks when sick, and seeking medical attention if they develop symptoms such as high fever, chest pain, persistent cough, shortness of breath, or fatigue.

title: Mild 4.8-Magnitude Earthquake Shakes Parts of Rwanda
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - A 4.8-magnitude earthquake was felt across several parts of the country on November 17, 2025, according to the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB).
title_en: Mild 4.8-Magnitude Earthquake Shakes Parts of Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - A 4.8-magnitude earthquake was felt across several parts of the country on November 17, 2025, according to the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB).
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - A 4.8-magnitude earthquake was felt across several parts of the country on November 17, 2025, according to the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (RMB). The tremor, recorded at 3:12 p.m., had its epicenter in Gatare Sector, Nyamagabe District, but was also experienced in Kigali City and surrounding areas.

In its statement, the RMB noted that the quake was strong enough to cause noticeable shaking. “This earthquake may cause windows to shake, furniture to shake or slight shaking of poorly constructed houses,” the agency reported.

Earthquakes with magnitudes between 4.0 and 5.0 are classified as mild, but they can still cause localized damage - particularly near the source. Such tremors may rattle buildings, shake windows and small objects, and in some cases, cause walls of weakly built homes to collapse. They may also trigger landslides on steep slopes and damage fragile items like plates and glassware.

Residents indoors often perceive this intensity as similar to a heavy truck passing nearby. Despite the shaking, experts say the quake was not considered highly destructive.

Geologists emphasize that the impact of an earthquake depends on multiple factors, including its intensity, location, frequency, and the resilience of local infrastructure.

This latest tremor follows a series of seismic events recorded in Rwanda this year. On November 11, 2025, a 4.2-magnitude quake was felt in western Rwanda. Earlier on July 28, a stronger 6.1-magnitude earthquake struck the Lake Tanganyika region. Another quake occurred on May 4 near Lake Albert, registering 5.4 in magnitude and followed minutes later by a 4.1 aftershock.

Historically, Rwanda’s strongest recorded earthquake occurred on March 20, 1966, with a magnitude of 6.6 - the most powerful in over a century. The region also witnessed significant seismic activity in 2021 during the Nyiragongo volcanic eruption, which forced thousands to flee.

Authorities have not reported any major damage or casualties from the latest incident.

title: Prof. Pastor Egide Kayitare Elected President of Rwandan Association of Pharmacists
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - Prof. Pastor Egide Kayitare, a pharmaceutical sciences lecturer at the University of Rwanda for 26 years, has been elected President of the Rwandan Association of Pharmacists (RAP).
title_en: Prof. Pastor Egide Kayitare Elected President of Rwandan Association of Pharmacists
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - Prof. Pastor Egide Kayitare, a pharmaceutical sciences lecturer at the University of Rwanda for 26 years, has been elected President of the Rwandan Association of Pharmacists (RAP).
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - Prof. Pastor Egide Kayitare, a pharmaceutical sciences lecturer at the University of Rwanda for 26 years, has been elected President of the Rwandan Association of Pharmacists (RAP). The announcement was made during the association’s 13th annual general meeting on November 14, 2025, attended by over 700 members.

Prof. Kayitare pledged to work collaboratively with members to address challenges such as drug-resistant pathogens and to safeguard the integrity and prestige of the pharmaceutical profession.

During the meeting, a five-year study aligned with Rwanda’s National Vision 2050 was presented, outlining strategies to accelerate development across sectors, including the pharmaceutical industry. The study emphasized professionalism, adherence to laws, and delivering quality healthcare services.

Outgoing President DCG (Rtd) Stanley Nsabimana highlighted the importance of continuous professional development. “Today we meet not to fulfill legal obligations, but to celebrate our achievements, reaffirm our values, and continue our commitment to protecting public health through a profession of medicine carried out with integrity and solid competence,” he said.

Dr. Ntihumbya Jean Baptiste, Director of Quality Assurance at the Ministry of Health, commended the role of pharmacists in improving healthcare and combating antimicrobial resistance. He urged members to prioritize patient safety, noting that antibiotics should not be prescribed without a doctor’s approval. Dr. Ntihumbya reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to supporting pharmacists through training, financial assistance, and capacity-building initiatives.

The government has implemented an integrated health program known as ‘One Health’, covering human, animal, and environmental health, to curb the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Launched in 2024, the initiative involves collaboration between the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Environment, and Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock.

Other newly elected leaders include Ntirenganya Remy Pacifique as Vice President, Uwase Marie Ange as Secretary, and Byomuhangi Evariste as Treasurer, all serving three-year terms.

The Rwandan Association of Pharmacists remains responsible for upholding professional ethics, ensuring compliance with laws and regulations, and fostering excellence within the pharmaceutical sector.

title: Rwanda Launches 30 Billion Rwf Laboratory to Test for Zoonotic Diseases
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda - The Government of Rwanda has launched a major project to build a state-of-the-art laboratory aimed at testing zoonotic diseases, with an estimated cost of over Rwf 34 billion ($24 million).
title_en: Rwanda Launches 30 Billion Rwf Laboratory to Test for Zoonotic Diseases
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda - The Government of Rwanda has launched a major project to build a state-of-the-art laboratory aimed at testing zoonotic diseases, with an estimated cost of over Rwf 34 billion ($24 million).
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda - The Government of Rwanda has launched a major project to build a state-of-the-art laboratory aimed at testing zoonotic diseases, with an estimated cost of over Rwf 34 billion ($24 million). The initiative is being implemented in collaboration with the Pandemic Fund and other international partners. The launch took place on Tuesday, November 18, 2025, with top officials including Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Dr. Mark Cyubahiro and Minister of Health Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana in attendance.

The new laboratory will operate at the third level of biosecurity, a significant upgrade from the previous facility, which was only at the second level. This advancement allows the laboratory to safely test for diseases originating from animals that could affect humans, including high-risk pathogens such as rabies.

For a laboratory to achieve third-level certification, it must be accredited, approved, and meet strict quality standards, with qualified personnel and specialized equipment to handle dangerous pathogens.
