body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Even as President Tiani toured the regions, the government continued to advance its diplomatic agenda in the capital. On Wednesday, November 12, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad, Bakary Yaou Sangaré, received copies of credentials from newly appointed representatives of Germany, the World Health Organization (WHO), and the African Development Bank (AfDB). The ceremony signaled Niger’s intent to maintain-though on its own terms-a calibrated engagement with both traditional allies and multilateral institutions.

On the same day, Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine held talks with an AfDB delegation led by Country Representative Mamadou Tangara. Discussions centered on development financing and the continuation of key programs, reflecting the government’s efforts to balance domestic restructuring with sustained international cooperation.

title: ZINDER (November 15-16, 2025): Reclaiming the Eastern Heartland
excerpt: ZINDER, Niger - President Abdourahamane Tiani’s arrival in Zinder on Saturday, November 15, 2025, marked a strategic assertion of state presence in Niger’s eastern territories.
title_en: ZINDER (November 15-16, 2025): Reclaiming the Eastern Heartland
excerpt_en: ZINDER, Niger - President Abdourahamane Tiani’s arrival in Zinder on Saturday, November 15, 2025, marked a strategic assertion of state presence in Niger’s eastern territories.
body_en:
ZINDER, Niger - President Abdourahamane Tiani’s arrival in Zinder on Saturday, November 15, 2025, marked a strategic assertion of state presence in Niger’s eastern territories. The 700-kilometer overland journey from Arlit, undertaken despite significant security concerns, symbolized the government’s commitment to territorial integration and citizen engagement. Residents illuminated the route with mobile phones and traditional torches, creating a striking visual metaphor of guidance and unity through adversity.

On Sunday, November 16, the program highlighted the administration’s sophisticated regional planning. At Stade Lawan Idrissa Manzo, President Tiani announced a historic African Development Bank (AfDB) investment of 98.7 billion CFA Francs for the Zinder region. This project addresses the long-standing “calvaire hydrique”, or water scarcity crisis, affecting nearly 700,000 residents. The initiative includes 12 drilled boreholes and three modern water towers, reflecting a detailed technical approach beyond mere political symbolism.

The Regional Security Council meeting offered insights into the government’s evolving security doctrine, with President Tiani analyzing disinformation and psychological operations aimed at military morale. His visit to Defense Zone No. 3 included private discussions with junior officers, demonstrating a hands-on approach to understanding operational realities on the ground and reinforcing the importance of security leadership at all levels.

MARADI (November 17, 2025): Agricultural Revolution Manifesto

President Tiani’s visit to Maradi underscored the economic core of his national tour, translating Niger’s agricultural potential into a tangible development blueprint. The events of Monday, November 17, positioned Maradi as a prototype for the country’s economic future.

The inspection of the Jirataoua irrigation perimeter involved two hours of detailed technical engagement with local farmers and processors, reflecting the President’s deep understanding of agricultural operations and value chains.

In a landmark announcement, the President unveiled a 60 billion CFA Franc agro-industrial center, complemented by a dry port and the near-completion (87%) of the Kano-Maradi railway. Together, these initiatives establish Maradi as a pivotal hub in the emerging Trans-Sahelian Economic Corridor, demonstrating the government’s commitment to regional integration and cross-border economic development. Notably, Nigerian investors were explicitly invited to participate, signaling a pragmatic approach to economic diplomacy despite ongoing political tensions.

During his visit to Defense Zone No. 6, President Tiani engaged in substantive discussions regarding the intersection of economic and security priorities. He addressed repeated pipeline sabotage attempts and committed to the deployment of advanced monitoring technologies, including drone surveillance and ground-penetrating radar, ensuring the protection of critical infrastructure and safeguarding strategic investments.

title: DIFFA (November 18-20, 2025): Sovereignty Frontier
excerpt: The Diffa segment represented the most politically sensitive phase of President Tiani’s national tour, emphasizing sovereignty, security, and regional integration.
title_en: DIFFA (November 18-20, 2025): Sovereignty Frontier
excerpt_en: The Diffa segment represented the most politically sensitive phase of President Tiani’s national tour, emphasizing sovereignty, security, and regional integration.
body_en:
The Diffa segment represented the most politically sensitive phase of President Tiani’s national tour, emphasizing sovereignty, security, and regional integration.

Upon his arrival in Goudoumaria on Tuesday, November 18, the President was greeted with ceremonial Kanuri cavalry displays, combining cultural homage with a clear demonstration of security presence. During an extended stay in Mainé Soroa, the President conducted a symbolic visit to the grave of former President Mamadou Tandja, framing a narrative of historical continuity and political evolution.

On Wednesday, November 19, the President inspected the CDA hydro-agricultural perimeter, highlighting the transformative potential of the FSSP program. A 1.3 billion CFA Franc investment achieved 85% utilization rates on previously marginal land, showcasing the administration’s focus on optimizing agricultural productivity. Presidential engagement included detailed questions on crop rotation and water management practices, reflecting a high level of technical policy involvement.

The Thursday, November 20 stadium address underscored explicit geopolitical framing, characterizing regional security challenges as resistance against "neocolonial powers" rather than purely religious conflict. Infrastructure announcements-including critical road networks linking N’guingmi to N’gourti and Yawoura to Gouré-strategically enhanced both economic connectivity and military mobility, reinforcing the dual objectives of development and sovereignty consolidation.

title: NIAMEY (November 20, 2025): Triumphal Apotheosis
excerpt: The return to Niamey marked the historic culmination of President Tiani’s national tour, transcending routine political ceremony to become a genuine popular phenomenon.
title_en: NIAMEY (November 20, 2025): Triumphal Apotheosis
excerpt_en: The return to Niamey marked the historic culmination of President Tiani’s national tour, transcending routine political ceremony to become a genuine popular phenomenon.
body_en:
The return to Niamey marked the historic culmination of President Tiani’s national tour, transcending routine political ceremony to become a genuine popular phenomenon. The three-hour, nine-kilometer procession drew over 150,000 participants, reflecting remarkable demographic diversity and widespread civic engagement. Elderly citizens, some waiting since the early afternoon with personal provisions, symbolized the depth and authenticity of popular support.

A coordinated strategic communications operation amplified the event across traditional media and social platforms, reinforcing a narrative of national renewal and direct citizen-state connection. The terrestrial travel modality, covering 2,500 kilometers throughout the tour, intentionally contrasted with the aerial preferences of previous administrations, embodying a new ethos of accessibility, proximity, and participatory governance.

NIAMEY, Niger-The government advanced sophisticated foreign policy diversification while managing an intensive domestic political campaign.

On Friday, November 21, meetings with a Belarusian delegation led by Vice Minister of Industry Bakey Denis accelerated the “Look East” policy. The delegation, including specialists in agricultural machinery, mining technology, and security equipment, signaled comprehensive partnership ambitions. Separate meetings with Prime Minister Zeine (focusing on economic cooperation) and Minister Toumba (focusing on security collaboration) reflected calibrated bilateral relationship management.

Industry analysis highlights Belarusian interest in uranium sector technology transfer, potentially filling technical gaps following the French withdrawal. Discussions on agricultural machinery aligned with Maradi development ambitions, including attractive financing mechanisms with extended terms and local assembly provisions.

On Tuesday, November 18, a meeting with the Chadian delegation led by Minister of Petroleum Mme NDOLONOGIE Naimbaye Alixe strengthened the AES eastern pillar cooperation. Topics included joint Lake Chad basin patrols, petroleum infrastructure protection, and mining regulation harmonization. The presence of petroleum and interior ministers emphasized a comprehensive cross-border resource management approach.

Intelligence assessments indicate that the Niger-Chad axis demonstrates enhanced effectiveness against Boko Haram splinter groups through improved coordination. Petroleum cooperation encompasses advanced pipeline feasibility studies and product exchange agreements, potentially reducing lucrative smuggling trade.

The Friday, November 21 Moroccan National Day celebrations served as a strategic messaging platform, highlighting the Atlantic access initiative for Sahelian global trade integration. Technical teams have initiated preliminary route surveys, offering potential reduction of landlocked AES dependency on traditional coastal outlets.

body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger-The November 20 implementation of Message-Radio n°002393 revealed a sophisticated regulatory approach balancing sovereignty assertion with continued engagement. Authorization for compliant organizations created a deliberate distinction between “responsible” and “non-compliant” entities, affecting approximately 23% of international NGOs and 35% of national associations.

title: Frontline Visits and Assertion of Sovereign Control Over Strategic Resources
excerpt: The final leg of President Tiani’s regional mission included high-stakes visits to some of Niger’s most sensitive security zones and economically strategic sites.
title_en: Frontline Visits and Assertion of Sovereign Control Over Strategic Resources
excerpt_en: The final leg of President Tiani’s regional mission included high-stakes visits to some of Niger’s most sensitive security zones and economically strategic sites.
body_en:
The final leg of President Tiani’s regional mission included high-stakes visits to some of Niger’s most sensitive security zones and economically strategic sites. At dawn on Friday, November 14, the Head of State traveled to Assamaka, the northern border town in Agadez Region that has suffered three attacks in less than a year. Arriving just one day after FDS units repelled another attempted incursion, President Tiani praised the courage and resilience of the troops stationed in this remote desert post and pledged reinforced logistical and operational support to secure the frontier.

Later that day, the President moved to Arlit for a landmark visit to the Société des Mines de l’Aïr (SOMAÏR). Standing at the heart of Niger’s uranium basin, he reaffirmed the irreversible nationalization of the mining site-a move he described as a cornerstone of Niger’s economic sovereignty. President Tiani declared that Niger would henceforth sell its uranium directly on the international market through “partners who respect the nation’s sovereignty,” underscoring a decisive shift toward state-controlled management of strategic natural resources.

title: Niger Secures Historic AfDB Funding to Overhaul Water Access in Zinder
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - In a major stride toward addressing chronic water shortages in the country’s southeast, the African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a landmark financing package worth 120.9 million Units of Account…
title_en: Niger Secures Historic AfDB Funding to Overhaul Water Access in Zinder
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - In a major stride toward addressing chronic water shortages in the country’s southeast, the African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a landmark financing package worth 120.9 million Units of Account…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - In a major stride toward addressing chronic water shortages in the country’s southeast, the African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a landmark financing package worth 120.9 million Units of Account - roughly 98.7 billion CFA francs - to transform water and sanitation infrastructure in the Zinder region.

Announced on Friday, November 14, the project marks one of the most significant water-sector investments in Niger’s recent history. It will overhaul drinking water systems in Zinder city, Mirriah, and 14 surrounding villages, ultimately benefiting nearly 700,000 residents who have long endured severe shortages that hinder health, economic activity, and daily living.

Authorities say the initiative aims to put a definitive end to a decades-long crisis in one of the nation’s most densely populated regions, where unreliable supply and aging infrastructure have repeatedly compounded public-health risks.

The AfDB’s support is expected to fund new water production and distribution facilities, expand sanitation services, and reinforce the resilience of communities facing rising demand and climate-related pressures.

Officials hailed the financing as a turning point - one that could reshape the socio-economic landscape of Zinder and provide a model for long-term water security across the country.

excerpt: TILLABÉRI, Niger - In a decisive push to address critical infrastructure gaps, the Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, launched rehabilitation works on the 112-kilometer…
title_en: Infrastructure Development and Public Service Management Strengthened in Tillabéri and Tahoua
excerpt_en: TILLABÉRI, Niger - In a decisive push to address critical infrastructure gaps, the Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, launched rehabilitation works on the 112-kilometer…
body_en:
TILLABÉRI, Niger - In a decisive push to address critical infrastructure gaps, the Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, launched rehabilitation works on the 112-kilometer Farié-Téra section of the RN4 national road on Thursday, November 13. This strategic project is expected to significantly enhance regional mobility, trade flow, security operations, and access to essential services across the Tillabéri region, which has long struggled with deteriorated transport infrastructure amid persistent security challenges.

In parallel, efforts to reinforce municipal governance and public service coordination advanced in the Tahoua region. On the same day, Thursday, November 13, Governor Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa presided over the opening of a technical workshop aimed at strengthening local administrative capacity, public service performance, and collaborative management between Development Associations and Secretary-Generals of partner communes.

The workshop underscored the government’s broader commitment to improving local governance, service delivery, and decentralized development, aligning with national priorities highlighted throughout President Tiani’s ongoing reform agenda.

title: Major Social Policy: SMIG Increase Formalized
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger-The November 21 SMIG announcement marked a calculated social investment, addressing both immediate economic pressures and long-term political economy considerations.
title_en: Major Social Policy: SMIG Increase Formalized
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger-The November 21 SMIG announcement marked a calculated social investment, addressing both immediate economic pressures and long-term political economy considerations.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger-The November 21 SMIG announcement marked a calculated social investment, addressing both immediate economic pressures and long-term political economy considerations. The 39.78% increase follows six months of technical analysis and extensive consultations with social partners.

Ministry impact assessments project a direct effect on approximately 127,000 formal sector workers, with significant ripple effects for an additional 85,000 workers. The January 1, 2026 implementation date provides a critical enterprise adjustment period while aligning with fiscal cycles.

The government implemented mitigation measures including targeted tax adjustments for SMEs, streamlined regulations, and enhanced credit access to offset labor costs. The policy explicitly links purchasing power improvement to economic sovereignty through enhanced domestic consumption and reduced import dependency.

The government implemented mitigation measures including targeted tax adjustments for SMEs, streamlined regulations, and enhanced credit access to offset labor costs. The policy explicitly links purchasing power improvement to economic sovereignty through enhanced domestic consumption and reduced import dependency.

NIAMEY, Niger - In a move aimed at reinforcing the country’s public water management system, Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine and the Director-General of the Société des Patrimoines des Eaux du Niger (SPEN), Niandou Mounkaila, signed a subsidiary agreement on Friday, November 14.

The agreement retrocedes the financing of the PASEPA Niamey-Tillabéri water supply project to SPEN, marking a significant step in strengthening the institution's operational and financial capacity.

This measure is expected to improve the efficiency of water infrastructure management, enhance the sustainability of ongoing reforms, and contribute to expanding access to potable water in the Niamey-Tillabéri corridor-an area facing rapid population growth and increasing demand for reliable water services.

excerpt_en: DIFFA, Niger - The Regional Directorate of the National Agency for Employment Promotion (ANPE) launched a vocational training program for 60 women in the Diffa region on Tuesday, November 11, 2025.

DIFFA, Niger - The Regional Directorate of the National Agency for Employment Promotion (ANPE) launched a vocational training program for 60 women in the Diffa region on Tuesday, November 11, 2025. The initiative aims to promote economic empowerment, skills development, and livelihood diversification among women, providing practical skills in the cosmetics sector.

On the same day, a separate training session for investigators was opened for the national household food security survey, “Sites Sentinelles 2025.” This training is essential for ensuring accurate data collection, which will support the government in anticipating and responding to food crises, a persistent challenge in Diffa and the wider region.

These parallel initiatives demonstrate Niger’s commitment to strengthening human capital and resilience, linking economic empowerment with critical monitoring of food security.

NIAMEY, Niger - In a major step toward strengthening the academic foundations of child protection and public policy, UNICEF and Abdou Moumouni University of Niamey signed a new memorandum of understanding on Friday, November 14.

The agreement, which builds on three years of collaboration, formalizes a strategic partnership centered on research, training, and policy support related to children’s rights. Officials say the initiative is designed to generate sustainable, evidence-based impact by integrating child-focused studies into university programs and supporting national efforts to improve child welfare.

The partnership is expected to enhance expertise within Niger’s academic institutions, bolster policymaking with reliable research, and strengthen the country’s long-term capacity to protect and promote the rights of every child.

TAHOUA, Niger - In a significant crackdown on organized narcotics operations, the Central Office for the Repression of Illicit Drug Trafficking (OCRTIS) successfully dismantled major trafficking networks in the Tahoua region.

Concluding on Friday, November 14, operations in the Konni department led to the seizure of over 57 kg of cannabis and tens of thousands of psychotropic tablets, with two high-profile suspects arrested.

Earlier, on Thursday, November 13, a separate operation in Baga, near Tahoua, intercepted 9,380 Diazepam tablets and five bricks of cannabis, targeting a Nigerian cross-border trafficking network.

Authorities emphasized that these operations demonstrate the increasing sophistication and effectiveness of Niger’s specialized counter-narcotics units, reinforcing the government’s commitment to curbing drug-related crime and protecting public health and security.

Between November 5 and 12, authorities arrested six individuals involved in fuel trafficking networks that supplied armed groups, cutting off a critical financial and logistical support chain for criminal actors.

The suspects were publicly presented to the press in Niamey, highlighting the government’s intensified intelligence-driven efforts to target organized crime and reinforce national security.

title: Major Incident Analysis: Garbougna Attack
excerpt: GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri Region-The November 19 attack revealed persistent terrorist capabilities despite overall security improvements.
title_en: Major Incident Analysis: Garbougna Attack
excerpt_en: GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri Region-The November 19 attack revealed persistent terrorist capabilities despite overall security improvements.
body_en:
GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri Region-The November 19 attack revealed persistent terrorist capabilities despite overall security improvements. Preliminary investigations indicate roughly 80 attackers employing coordinated vehicle-borne IEDs, direct assault, and supporting fires, pointing to professional training and multi-week planning.

The gendarmerie position on the Téra-Niamey axis demonstrated the attackers’ ability to strike near the capital while disrupting vital supply routes. The toll-17 killed, 34 injured-marks the largest security force loss since the transition began.

Captured equipment, including night vision and communications gear, underscores both the tactical success of the attackers and concerning potential for intelligence gathering in future operations. The complex methodology suggests possible external training support.

The security response followed standard procedures executed professionally, but prompted a comprehensive review of isolated position protocols and accelerated AES joint patrols.

title: President Tiani Intensifies National Tour With High-Stakes Regional Engagements
excerpt: DOSSO / TAHOUA / AGADEZ, Niger - President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani has intensified his national tour with a series of high-profile engagements across three strategic regions, reinforcing the transitional…
title_en: President Tiani Intensifies National Tour With High-Stakes Regional Engagements
excerpt_en: DOSSO / TAHOUA / AGADEZ, Niger - President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani has intensified his national tour with a series of high-profile engagements across three strategic regions, reinforcing the transitional…
body_en:
DOSSO / TAHOUA / AGADEZ, Niger - President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani has intensified his national tour with a series of high-profile engagements across three strategic regions, reinforcing the transitional government’s dual agenda of security consolidation and regional development. The tour, which has rapidly evolved into a cornerstone of the regime’s political strategy, showcased a deliberate effort to strengthen ties with local populations while addressing urgent security and governance challenges.

DOSSO REGION - Border Security and Traditional Endorsement (November 8-9)

President Tiani concluded his visit to southwestern Niger with a decisive security review. On November 9, he presided over the Dosso Regional Security Council, where he assessed border dynamics with Benin, focusing on cross-border criminality and the operational readiness of security forces deployed in this key corridor.

During a major address in Gaya on November 8, delivered in the Djerma language, the Head of State explained the rationale behind the Benin border closure, emphasizing national security concerns while acknowledging the economic impact on border communities. His visit received notable cultural resonance when the Canton Chief of Gaya presented him with two symbolic crocodiles, a gesture signaling strong traditional endorsement within the Dendi cultural sphere.

TAHOUA REGION - Mass Mobilization and Military Morale (November 9-10)

The President’s arrival in Tahoua was marked by unprecedented crowds, stretching from Koujack to the regional capital, where cultural delegations celebrated the visit with elaborate traditional performances.

On November 10, President Tiani visited the 42nd Combined Arms Battalion, where he delivered a morale-boosting speech, declaring:

“The Defense and Security Forces, as the nation’s first bastion and pillar, have not and will never kneel before the enemy.”

He later chaired the Tahoua Regional Security Council, receiving operational updates on counter-terrorist efforts in Tillia and Tchintabaraden, before addressing a packed stadium. He denounced internal actors accused of collusion with jihadists or bandit groups, asserting that such elements "will not triumph over the united and determined Nigerien people."

AGADEZ REGION - Security Consolidation and Landmark Economic Declarations (November 11-15)

President Tiani’s extended mission in Agadez, Niger’s northern geopolitical crossroads, was met with vibrant traditional ceremonies, including youyous and biyanou chants, with thousands lining the route from Tamaya onward.

A crucial Regional Security Council was held on November 12 at the Governorate, bringing together Niger’s top security leadership - including Minister of State for National Defense General Salifou Modi and Armed Forces Chief of Staff General Moussa Salaou Barmou. Discussions centered on the evolving threats in the uranium-rich north, a region pivotal for both national security and economic sovereignty.

During a major public rally at the Aboubacar Djibo Traditional Wrestling Arena, the President made some of his most consequential policy declarations to date:

“Niger’s wealth will now belong to Niger.”“The era of exploitation without adequate national benefit has definitively ended.”

He confirmed the nationalization of several mining companies, particularly in the uranium and gold sectors - a move poised to reshape the country’s economic landscape.

excerpt: DIFFA / MARADI / ZINDER / NIAMEY, Niger - November 16-20 - The final week of President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani’s nationwide tour demonstrated unprecedented popular mobilization, highlighting strong public…
title_en: President Tiani's National Tour Culminates in Historic Mobilizations Across Niger
excerpt_en: DIFFA / MARADI / ZINDER / NIAMEY, Niger - November 16-20 - The final week of President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani’s nationwide tour demonstrated unprecedented popular mobilization, highlighting strong public…
body_en:
DIFFA / MARADI / ZINDER / NIAMEY, Niger - November 16-20 - The final week of President Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani’s nationwide tour demonstrated unprecedented popular mobilization, highlighting strong public support for the transition government and underscoring the administration’s commitment to security, economic development, and infrastructure expansion. The tour combined high-level security consultations, policy announcements, and direct engagement with local populations, reflecting a multi-faceted approach to governance and state consolidation.

DIFFA (November 18-20): The President’s entry into Diffa was marked by vibrant Kanuri cultural ceremonies in Goudoumaria on November 18, featuring spectacular camel and horse fantasia displays, traditional drumming, and colorful attire that reflected local heritage. On November 19, he chaired the Regional Security Council, attended by Minister of State for National Defense General Salifou Modi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces General Moussa Salaou Barmou, and other senior security officials. The council conducted an in-depth review of regional counter-terrorism operations and cross-border security challenges, particularly along Diffa’s volatile eastern frontier. The President also inspected the 204-hectare CDA hydro-agricultural perimeter, a cornerstone of the Great Irrigation Program, rehabilitated at over 1.3 billion CFA francs, emphasizing the government’s focus on agricultural self-sufficiency and rural employment. On November 20, a massive Regional Concord Stadium rally drew thousands of Manga people. President Tiani connected the state’s present vision to the historical legacy of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, stating, “This war we are waging is a total war, wanted by France and its leader Emmanuel Macron... Our determination is unlimited.” He announced key infrastructure projects, including the N’guigmi-N’gourti and Yawoura-Diffa roads, and a new hospital in N’gourti, demonstrating a commitment to regional connectivity and health services expansion.

MARADI (November 17): The President’s arrival in Maradi was greeted by packed crowds at the traditional wrestling arena, reflecting the region’s enthusiasm for national initiatives. He announced a 60 billion CFA franc agro-industrial center, strategically integrated with the planned dry port and Kano-Maradi railway, designed to enhance regional trade and agro-industrial output. The Djirataoua irrigated perimeter was praised for producing 25,035 tons of crops, valued at approximately 2 billion CFA francs in 2025. During his visit to Defense Zone No. 6 Military Camp, he paid homage to fallen soldiers, highlighting the sacrifices of the FDS and affirming the government’s enduring support for national defense and security operations.

ZINDER (November 16): The President addressed the chronic water crisis affecting the region for decades, confirming the signing of a 98.7 billion CFA franc financing agreement with the African Development Bank for comprehensive water and sanitation infrastructure. He encouraged youth to “work the land” and called on economic operators to invest in local processing factories, aiming to generate value-added employment and strengthen the agricultural economy. The visit included a Regional Security Council meeting and inspection of Defense Zone No. 3, where President Tiani emphasized the ongoing need for vigilance against security threats and the importance of coordination between military and civil authorities.

NIAMEY (November 20): The national tour concluded with a historic nine-kilometer human corridor from Diori Hamani International Airport to the Presidential Palace, with citizens waiting for up to six hours to welcome the President. The three-hour procession symbolized the culmination of a strategic political outreach across all eight regions of Niger, highlighting massive public endorsement of the government’s Refoundation agenda, which emphasizes national sovereignty, infrastructure development, and social cohesion.

The final phase of the tour demonstrated the government’s capacity to combine security oversight, developmental policy, and direct citizen engagement, reinforcing the message that Niger’s transition authorities are focused on stability, prosperity, and inclusive governance in all corners of the country.

title: Strategic Partnerships Expand with Belarus and Chad
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - November 18-21 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs strengthened Niger’s multi-vector diplomacy through a series of high-level engagements aimed at deepening economic, technical, and security cooperation.
title_en: Strategic Partnerships Expand with Belarus and Chad
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 18-21 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs strengthened Niger’s multi-vector diplomacy through a series of high-level engagements aimed at deepening economic, technical, and security cooperation.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 18-21 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs strengthened Niger’s multi-vector diplomacy through a series of high-level engagements aimed at deepening economic, technical, and security cooperation.

CHAD (November 18): General Mohamed Toumba received Chadian Minister of Petroleum, Mines and Geology Mrs. NDOLONOGIE Naimbaye Alixe, accompanied by her Nigerien counterpart. The discussions focused on bilateral cooperation in the petroleum and mining sectors, including harmonization of sector policies and the strengthening of cross-border security coordination, reflecting a proactive approach to regional stability and economic integration.

BELARUS (November 21): Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine and Minister of State for Interior, General of Division Mohamed Toumba, met with a Belarusian delegation led by Vice-Minister of Industry Bakey Denis. The meetings established concrete frameworks for enhanced economic and technical cooperation, with a particular focus on industrial development and technology transfer, signaling Niger’s commitment to diversifying its strategic partnerships.

These engagements highlight Niger’s continued efforts to consolidate diplomatic relations while aligning economic development priorities with regional security imperatives.

title: Strategic Mine Site Inspections Reinforce Resource Nationalization Policy
excerpt: ARLIT/ASSAMAKA, Agadez - President Tiani intensified his northern tour on November 14 with high-stakes inspections of two strategic locations, underscoring the administration’s determination to secure border regions and…
title_en: Strategic Mine Site Inspections Reinforce Resource Nationalization Policy
excerpt_en: ARLIT/ASSAMAKA, Agadez - President Tiani intensified his northern tour on November 14 with high-stakes inspections of two strategic locations, underscoring the administration’s determination to secure border regions and…
body_en:
ARLIT/ASSAMAKA, Agadez - President Tiani intensified his northern tour on November 14 with high-stakes inspections of two strategic locations, underscoring the administration’s determination to secure border regions and advance its flagship resource-nationalization agenda. At the SOMAÏR uranium mine-now fully state-owned after post-transition restructuring-the Head of State reiterated that the nationalization process is “irreversible,” announcing that Niger will henceforth market its uranium to “respectful partners under clear terms guaranteeing fair returns for the Nigerien people.” The technical inspection revealed production exceeding 1,000 tons of yellowcake since the July 26, 2023 transition, with the President engaging directly with engineers, technicians, and workers to assess operational constraints and ongoing modernization efforts.

Earlier in Assamaka, at the edge of the Algerian border, President Tiani visited frontline positions less than a day after security forces repelled a coordinated attack carried out by four armed vehicles. He praised the “exceptional courage” of Defense and Security Forces stationed in isolated desert posts, emphasizing that their resilience “embodies the highest form of patriotism and national service” and remains essential to securing major transit corridors and preventing infiltration along one of the country’s most volatile frontiers.

title: Historic Water Infrastructure Investment for Zinder Region
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - November 14 - A transformative 98.7 billion CFA franc financing agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) has been formally confirmed to support a sweeping overhaul of water and sanitation…
title_en: Historic Water Infrastructure Investment for Zinder Region
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 14 - A transformative 98.7 billion CFA franc financing agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) has been formally confirmed to support a sweeping overhaul of water and sanitation…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 14 - A transformative 98.7 billion CFA franc financing agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) has been formally confirmed to support a sweeping overhaul of water and sanitation infrastructure in the Zinder region. The landmark project-covering Zinder city, Mirriah, and 14 surrounding villages-aims to put an end to the chronic water shortages that have affected nearly 700,000 residents for generations, a crisis local authorities have described as “seven decades of rationing, temporary solutions, and perpetual water anxiety.”

The initiative involves the construction of new water treatment plants, the expansion of distribution networks, and the deployment of modern management systems designed to boost daily water production capacity by 45,000 cubic meters. Once completed, the project is expected to fundamentally improve living conditions and strengthen economic opportunities in Niger’s second-largest urban center.

title_en: Strategic Infrastructure Development Accelerates Across Multiple Sectors
excerpt_en: TILLABÉRI/TAHOUA, Niger - November 13 - A series of major infrastructure initiatives advanced this week, underscoring the government's determination to close long-standing development gaps and strengthen critical…
body_en:
TILLABÉRI/TAHOUA, Niger - November 13 - A series of major infrastructure initiatives advanced this week, underscoring the government's determination to close long-standing development gaps and strengthen critical services across multiple regions.

The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, officially launched rehabilitation works on the 112-kilometer Farié-Téra road segment (RN4) on Thursday, November 13. The project is expected to significantly improve transportation links between the Tillabéri region and Niamey, while boosting economic activity in one of Niger’s most productive agricultural zones.

The government finalized the transfer of drinking water supply financing to the Niger Water Heritage Company through a subsidiary agreement signed on Friday, November 14, facilitating the implementation of the PASEPA Niamey-Tillabéri water project, which will serve more than 500,000 residents in western regions.

In the Tahoua region, authorities launched specialized training sessions for Municipal Directors and Secretaries-General focused on public service delivery and municipal coordination under the ProDEC project. The program aims to strengthen local governance across 25 pilot communes.

title_en: Employment Promotion and Economic Diversification Initiatives Expand
excerpt_en: DIFFA, Niger - November 11 - The National Employment Promotion Agency (ANPE) has launched an ambitious cosmetic production training program for 60 women in the Diffa region, marking a new step in national efforts to…
body_en:
DIFFA, Niger - November 11 - The National Employment Promotion Agency (ANPE) has launched an ambitious cosmetic production training program for 60 women in the Diffa region, marking a new step in national efforts to strengthen economic resilience in areas affected by the Boko Haram insurgency.

The six-week initiative provides technical training, business management skills, and market access support, with participants set to receive starter kits enabling them to establish their own micro-enterprises upon completion.

Authorities describe the program as a key component of the government's broader strategy to combat youth vulnerability and reduce susceptibility to extremist recruitment through practical economic empowerment and diversification of local income sources.

title_en: Government Announces Historic 40% Minimum Wage Increase
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 21 - In a landmark social policy decision with far-reaching economic implications, the Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Employment announced a major adjustment to the Guaranteed…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 21 - In a landmark social policy decision with far-reaching economic implications, the Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Employment announced a major adjustment to the Guaranteed Interprofessional Minimum Wage (SMIG).

During a press briefing, Secretary General Abdou Dounama detailed the increase from 30,047 CFA francs to 42,000 CFA francs, effective January 1, 2026. The measure addresses a long-standing union demand and represents a strategic effort to strengthen household purchasing power amid inflationary pressures, while reinforcing the government’s social contract with workers nationwide.

title_en: Regulatory Framework for Civil Society Strengthened Through Compliance Measures
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 19 - The Ministry of Interior implemented a measured approach to civil society regulation through Radio Message No. 002393, issued on Wednesday, November 19.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Wednesday, November 19 - The Ministry of Interior implemented a measured approach to civil society regulation through Radio Message No. 002393, issued on Wednesday, November 19. The directive lifted suspensions for national NGOs and associations that submitted their 2024 financial statements to the Official Journal by March 31, 2025.

This initiative regularizes hundreds of organizations while maintaining suspensions for non-compliant entities, demonstrating the government’s strategy of combining enforcement with incentives to encourage transparency. Reports indicate that approximately 140 organizations (including 60 international and 75 national NGOs) were compliant, while several hundred others remain suspended pending regularization.

body_en:
DIFFA / NATIONWIDE, Niger - November 11 - A series of major social development programs advanced across the country, underscoring the government's focus on human security, public health, and sustainable development:

· National Community Relay Day was marked on November 9, with Interior Minister General Mohamed Toumba commending community health relays for their “exemplary engagement” in extending state services to remote areas and serving as essential links between local populations and public institutions.

· The National Household Food Security Survey (Sites Sentinelles 2025) launched intensive investigator training in Diffa on November 11. The initiative establishes a nationwide data collection system monitoring food security across 125 sentinel sites, enabling rapid response to emerging vulnerabilities.

· Ahead of upcoming presidential visits, regional governments intensified sanitation and beautification campaigns, particularly in Maradi and Diffa, where municipal authorities mobilized substantial resources to showcase development progress and demonstrate public support for the transition authorities.

title: Historic Liberation of Abducted State Officials After 17-Month Captivity
excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - November 09 - In a major security breakthrough with wide implications for national morale and administrative continuity, Bilma Prefect Commandant Amadou Torda and four collaborators abducted in June 2024…
title_en: Historic Liberation of Abducted State Officials After 17-Month Captivity
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - November 09 - In a major security breakthrough with wide implications for national morale and administrative continuity, Bilma Prefect Commandant Amadou Torda and four collaborators abducted in June 2024…
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - November 09 - In a major security breakthrough with wide implications for national morale and administrative continuity, Bilma Prefect Commandant Amadou Torda and four collaborators abducted in June 2024 in the Dirkou area were successfully freed and returned to Niamey on Sunday, November 9.

The officials - all in remarkably good health despite their 17-month captivity - were received at the capital’s military airport by Interior Minister General Mohamed Toumba, in an emotional ceremony marking the end of an extended rescue effort.

According to authorities, the liberation resulted from a sustained, multi-track strategy combining diplomatic pressure, local mediation, and targeted security operations. The successful outcome is viewed as a significant validation of the government’s evolving approach to handling kidnappings and reflects enhanced national capabilities in managing complex negotiation environments.

body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 21 - In a major development for the judicial sector, the constitutive general assembly of the Nigerien Association of Young Judicial Officers convened under the theme "UNITE TRAIN ACT: young judicial officers at the service of justice and the rule of law."

The assembly brought together judicial officers from all eight regions of Niger to establish a unified professional body aimed at enhancing the efficiency and integrity of judicial processes. The association’s mandate emphasizes capacity building, professional standardization, and improving the execution of court decisions, a crucial step toward strengthening public confidence in the justice system.

title_en: IOM and Government Collaborate to Strengthen Legal Protection for Migrant Children

body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Friday, November 21 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) Niger, in collaboration with the Ministry in charge of child protection, is undertaking a comprehensive compilation of legislative texts and frameworks applicable to children in mobility situations.

Announced during World Children's Day commemorations on November 21, the initiative seeks to identify legal gaps and harmonize national legislation with international standards. The project represents a proactive approach to addressing the vulnerabilities of migrant children, particularly those separated from their families, by strengthening legal protection mechanisms rather than relying on ad-hoc interventions.

excerpt: NIAMEY, Niger - Despite ongoing judicial reforms, the judicial system continues to face significant challenges in processing terrorism- and organized crime-related cases.
title_en: Judicial System Faces Backlog Amid Security Challenges
excerpt_en: NIAMEY, Niger - Despite ongoing judicial reforms, the judicial system continues to face significant challenges in processing terrorism- and organized crime-related cases.
body_en:
NIAMEY, Niger - Despite ongoing judicial reforms, the judicial system continues to face significant challenges in processing terrorism- and organized crime-related cases. Reliable sources indicate that approximately 347 terrorism-related cases remain pending before specialized courts, with the High Court of Niamey accounting for nearly 42% of the backlog.

The delays are attributed to logistical constraints, security concerns for judicial personnel, and the complexity of gathering admissible evidence in conflict-affected regions. Analysts warn that this backlog could undermine the government’s security gains by delaying the prosecution of apprehended suspects, highlighting the need for accelerated judicial capacity building and operational support.

body_en:
ZINDER, Niger - During the presidential visit to Zinder on November 16, traditional leaders signed a framework agreement with the Ministry of Justice, formalizing their role in resolving civil disputes and minor criminal cases.

The agreement establishes protocols for case referral between traditional and formal justice systems and provides for training on fundamental legal principles. While the initiative aims to improve access to justice in remote areas, some legal experts have raised concerns about potential conflicts with statutory law and the protection of women's and children's rights within traditional proceedings.

body_en:
TAHOUA/KONNI, Niger - November 14 - A series of high-impact counter-narcotics operations has dealt a significant blow to transnational drug trafficking networks, underscoring Niger's strengthened interdiction and intelligence capabilities.

• In Konni department, the Central Office for the Repression of Illicit Drug Trafficking (OCRTIS) dismantled a major international trafficking network, seizing 57 kg of high-grade cannabis and thousands of psychotropic tablets on Friday, November 14. Two high-profile suspects were arrested. Investigators uncovered advanced concealment techniques and distribution routes extending across borders into neighboring states.

• In a separate intelligence-led operation in Baga, near Tahoua, on Thursday, November 13, security forces intercepted 9,380 Diazepam tablets and five bricks of cannabis, successfully disrupting a Nigerian cross-border trafficking ring that had been exploiting remote desert corridors to evade authorities.

excerpt: NATIONWIDE, Niger - November 5-12 - The National Guard carried out a series of coordinated operations targeting fuel trafficking networks that finance armed groups in the Tillabéri and Tahoua regions.
title_en: National Guard Intensifies Anti-Trafficking Operations with Focus on Terrorist Financing
excerpt_en: NATIONWIDE, Niger - November 5-12 - The National Guard carried out a series of coordinated operations targeting fuel trafficking networks that finance armed groups in the Tillabéri and Tahoua regions.
body_en:
NATIONWIDE, Niger - November 5-12 - The National Guard carried out a series of coordinated operations targeting fuel trafficking networks that finance armed groups in the Tillabéri and Tahoua regions. During the week-long campaign, authorities arrested six individuals involved in sophisticated smuggling schemes, as well as a fake non-commissioned officer who had been operating undetected for several years using forged documentation.

The suspects were publicly presented in Niamey, highlighting the government’s enhanced intelligence capabilities and inter-agency coordination in dismantling the complex financial networks that sustain terrorist activity. Investigations revealed increasingly sophisticated trafficking methods, including the use of legitimate business fronts and the corruption of security personnel.

NIAMEY, Niger - November 21 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) Niger joined the Government of Niger and UNICEF in commemorating World Children's Day, highlighting the particular vulnerabilities of children in mobility situations.

The IOM emphasized its ongoing work in facilitating the return and socio-economic reintegration of vulnerable migrant children into their families. title: Major Terrorist Attack Inflicts Heavy Losses on Security Forces in Tillabéri
excerpt: GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri - Wednesday, November 19 - The National Gendarmerie position in Garbougna came under a complex attack by Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (EIGS) militants on Wednesday, November 19, marking the…
title_en: Major Terrorist Attack Inflicts Heavy Losses on Security Forces in Tillabéri
excerpt_en: GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri - Wednesday, November 19 - The National Gendarmerie position in Garbougna came under a complex attack by Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (EIGS) militants on Wednesday, November 19, marking the…
body_en:
GARBOUGNA, Tillabéri - Wednesday, November 19 - The National Gendarmerie position in Garbougna came under a complex attack by Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (EIGS) militants on Wednesday, November 19, marking the most severe security incident of the week.

Preliminary reports indicate 17 soldiers killed, including the mission commander (a captain), 34 seriously wounded, and several reported missing. The attackers also destroyed multiple vehicles and seized significant military equipment before withdrawing.

Security analysts describe the assault as a substantial tactical setback in the Tillabéri region, where previous security gains had been recorded, underscoring the persistent threat posed by organized terrorist networks in Niger’s border areas.

title: Nationwide Security Operations Disrupt Criminal Networks Across Multiple Regions
excerpt: NIGER - November 17-20, 2025 - Nigerien security forces conducted a series of coordinated operations across multiple regions, targeting criminal networks involved in fuel smuggling, drug trafficking, and other illicit…
title_en: Nationwide Security Operations Disrupt Criminal Networks Across Multiple Regions
excerpt_en: NIGER - November 17-20, 2025 - Nigerien security forces conducted a series of coordinated operations across multiple regions, targeting criminal networks involved in fuel smuggling, drug trafficking, and other illicit…
body_en:
NIGER - November 17-20, 2025 - Nigerien security forces conducted a series of coordinated operations across multiple regions, targeting criminal networks involved in fuel smuggling, drug trafficking, and other illicit activities, signaling improved intelligence capabilities and inter-agency coordination.

GOURÉ, Zinder (November 19): The Departmental Directorate of the National Police (DDPN) successfully dismantled a sophisticated fuel fraud network, arresting one suspect and seizing 338 jerricans of gasoline smuggled from Nigeria via the Guidguir border crossing. Investigators noted that the smugglers had bypassed multiple official security checkpoints, highlighting the network’s adaptive operational methods and its potential to supply armed groups in conflict-affected areas.

TANOUT, Zinder (November 20): Police intercepted a drug courier in the Kara-kara district, recovering 06 cannabis balls and 2,500 Hexol tablets. Preliminary investigations traced the trafficking route from Tessaoua to Agadez, with criminals exploiting motorcycles to traverse remote areas and evade detection. The operation revealed the growing sophistication of transregional narcotics networks.

ARLIT, Agadez (November 17): The Central Office for the Repression of Illicit Traffic in Stupéfiants (OCRTIS) executed two major anti-drug operations, seizing 16 kg of cannabis and a handgun with obliterated serial numbers. Alarmingly, three of the four arrested individuals were members of the FDS, underscoring serious internal corruption risks that could compromise counter-insurgency efforts and the integrity of security operations in northern regions.

SAY, Tillabéri (November 17): The DDPN dismantled a complex fuel smuggling network using passenger vehicles to transport fuel from Niamey to terrorist groups operating in Doguel-Kaina village. Simultaneous investigations uncovered pharmaceutical narcotics trafficking, with seizures including Tramadol, Eskazepam, and cannabis, illustrating the interconnected nature of criminal enterprises and the convergence of terrorist financing and illicit trade.

Officials highlighted that these operations demonstrate the increasingly proactive posture of Nigerien security forces, the growing use of intelligence-led interventions, and enhanced coordination between police, gendarmerie, and national anti-drug agencies. Analysts warned, however, that networks remain adaptive and heavily reliant on regional smuggling routes, requiring sustained surveillance and continuous operational reinforcement.

Conclusion: Consolidating Sovereignty and Development Amidst Persistent Challenges

The period from November 10 to 24, 2025, was defined by a strategic dual focus from the transitional government: intensified internal political consolidation and decisive policy shifts aimed at national sovereignty and socio-economic development, all while confronting persistent security threats.

Political Consolidation and Popular Endorsement: President Tiani's national tour across all eight regions culminated in "historic mobilizations," underscoring strong public support for the government's Refoundation agenda. The tour combined high-level security reviews with policy announcements and direct citizen engagement, reinforcing the administration's commitment to stability and inclusive governance.

Economic Sovereignty and Development: The government executed a landmark resource nationalization policy, particularly in the uranium and gold sectors, affirming that "Niger’s wealth will now belong to Niger". This was coupled with significant social policy wins, including a historic 40% increase in the minimum wage and major infrastructure agreements, such as the 98.7 billion CFA franc deal with the AfDB to end chronic water shortages in Zinder.

Diplomatic and Security Realignment: Niger pursued a "multi-vector diplomacy," strengthening strategic partnerships with countries like Belarus and Chad while maintaining pragmatic engagement with multilateral institutions like the African Development Bank (AfDB) and the World Health Organization (WHO). On the security front, the successful liberation of abducted state officials validated the government's complex negotiation strategies.

Persistent Security and Judicial Challenges: Despite successful, coordinated anti-trafficking and anti-narcotics operations across multiple regions, the security environment remains volatile. The complex attack on the National Gendarmerie in Garbougna, Tillabéri, resulting in significant casualties, served as a stark reminder of the persistent threat posed by organized terrorist networks. Furthermore, the judicial system continues to face a significant backlog of approximately 347 terrorism-related cases, which analysts warn could undermine security gains.

In summary, the transition government successfully leveraged its domestic outreach to solidify popular legitimacy and drive forward its ambitious agenda of resource control and structural development. However, the period’s successes were tempered by the deadly realities of the security crisis and the imperative to accelerate judicial and institutional reforms to match the pace of its security and economic policies. The ultimate success of the Refoundation agenda hinges on the government's ability to swiftly translate policy declarations into tangible, sustainable improvements in security, justice, and the socio-economic well-being of the Nigerien people.

title: Ouagadougou and Novosibirsk Seal Twinning Agreement to Boost Cultural and Educational Exchanges
excerpt: Novosibirsk, November 17, 2025 - The President of the Special Delegation of Ouagadougou, Maurice Konaté, and the Mayor of Novosibirsk, Maksim Kudryavtsev, have signed a twinning agreement formalizing decentralized…
title_en: Ouagadougou and Novosibirsk Seal Twinning Agreement to Boost Cultural and Educational Exchanges
excerpt_en: Novosibirsk, November 17, 2025 - The President of the Special Delegation of Ouagadougou, Maurice Konaté, and the Mayor of Novosibirsk, Maksim Kudryavtsev, have signed a twinning agreement formalizing decentralized…
body_en:
Novosibirsk, November 17, 2025 - The President of the Special Delegation of Ouagadougou, Maurice Konaté, and the Mayor of Novosibirsk, Maksim Kudryavtsev, have signed a twinning agreement formalizing decentralized cooperation between the capitals of Burkina Faso and Siberia.

Signed on November 11, the agreement marks the culmination of a process initiated several months ago and covers multiple sectors, including education, arts, culture, sports, and tourism. The partnership aims to strengthen exchanges of expertise and deepen ties between the Burkinabè and Russian communities.

Coinciding with the ceremony, a delegation from Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Trade inaugurated a cultural exhibition titled "The Grandeur of Bronze: Traditional Culture of Burkina Faso" at the Novosibirsk Regional Museum. The exposition, which will run for three months, highlights the artistic heritage of Burkina Faso, offering Russian visitors the opportunity to discover bronze works and traditional craftsmanship. A dedicated Burkinabè booth showcasing souvenirs and cultural items has also been set up at the Novosibirsk Regional Library.

Novosibirsk, the third-largest city in Russia with a population of about 1.63 million, serves as the administrative capital of Siberia and a major cultural and economic hub - offering what officials describe as “significant potential” for this new cooperation framework.

title: Burkina Faso-Belgium Cooperation: Foreign Minister Traoré and Ambassador De Wandel Review Priority Issues
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, granted an audience on Monday to the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Belgium, Erwin…
title_en: Burkina Faso-Belgium Cooperation: Foreign Minister Traoré and Ambassador De Wandel Review Priority Issues
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, granted an audience on Monday to the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Belgium, Erwin…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, granted an audience on Monday to the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Belgium, Erwin De Wandel, to review several key areas of bilateral cooperation.

The meeting focused on the adjustment of the budgetary program, the continuation of Belgium’s humanitarian support, and the need to strengthen economic and commercial cooperation between Belgian and Burkinabè companies.

On this last point, Minister Traoré stressed the importance of providing accurate and updated information on the national context to Belgian business leaders. He noted that many stakeholders continue to rely on sources spreading inaccurate information about Burkina Faso, which undermines their willingness to establish partnerships with local companies.

Ambassador De Wandel also informed the Ministry of Brussels’ ongoing review of its diplomatic network, a process currently under assessment by the Belgian authorities.

title: Burkina Faso-Belarus Economic Cooperation: Belarusian Investors Present Projects to Foreign Minister Traoré
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received on Monday, November 17, a delegation of Belarusian investors seeking to…
title_en: Burkina Faso-Belarus Economic Cooperation: Belarusian Investors Present Projects to Foreign Minister Traoré
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received on Monday, November 17, a delegation of Belarusian investors seeking to…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received on Monday, November 17, a delegation of Belarusian investors seeking to implement development projects in Burkina Faso.

Led by Vitaly Gmyrak, the delegation expressed its intention to establish a mutually beneficial partnership in several strategic sectors, including agricultural production, fertilizer manufacturing, agricultural mechanization, mining, and electrical engineering.

According to Mr. Gmyrak, this first meeting with Minister Traoré marks “the starting point for building economic relations” between Belarus and Burkina Faso.

Minister Traoré welcomed what he described as the “pragmatic approach” of the Belarusian investors, noting that their proposals align with the government’s priority areas. He encouraged them to use their stay in Burkina Faso to develop win-win partnerships with local entrepreneurs.

During the audience, an envoy of the Belarusian Minister of Foreign Affairs also delivered a letter to Minister Traoré, reaffirming Minsk’s commitment to strengthening friendship and cooperation with Ouagadougou.

title_en: Bilateral Cooperation: Ambassador Appolinaire SAWADOGO Presents Credentials to Tunisian President
excerpt_en: Tunis, November 24, 2025 - His Excellency Appolinaire SAWADOGO, the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to Tunisia, presented his credentials to the President of the Tunisian Republic, Kaïs…
body_en:
Tunis, November 24, 2025 - His Excellency Appolinaire SAWADOGO, the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to Tunisia, presented his credentials to the President of the Tunisian Republic, Kaïs Saïed, on Friday, November 21, 2025.

The ceremony, held at the Carthage Presidential Palace, allowed Ambassador Sawadogo to convey the fraternal greetings of Burkina Faso’s President, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, to his Tunisian counterpart. The two leaders discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in the economy, higher education, vocational training, and health sectors.

Ambassador Sawadogo also emphasized cooperation in the fight against terrorism and violent extremism, highlighting Tunisia's expertise in this field. He expressed Burkina Faso’s intention to hold the 9th session of the Joint Cooperation Commission in Tunis in 2026, following the agreement reached by both countries in July 2024.

President Kaïs Saïed, while reaffirming Tunisia’s commitment to enhanced relations with Burkina Faso, commended the historic measures taken by the Burkinabe authorities under President Traoré in defense of national and African sovereignty.

title: Confederation of Sahel States (AES): Senior Officials Meet in Ouagadougou Ahead of Foreign Ministers' Meeting
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - Senior officials from the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) are convening in Ouagadougou on November 24-25, 2025, to prepare for the Confederation's Foreign Ministers' Meeting…
title_en: Confederation of Sahel States (AES): Senior Officials Meet in Ouagadougou Ahead of Foreign Ministers' Meeting
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - Senior officials from the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) are convening in Ouagadougou on November 24-25, 2025, to prepare for the Confederation's Foreign Ministers' Meeting…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - Senior officials from the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) are convening in Ouagadougou on November 24-25, 2025, to prepare for the Confederation's Foreign Ministers' Meeting, scheduled for November 26 in the Burkinabe capital. The meeting opened this morning with delegations of experts from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. These senior officials, specializing in the AES’s three pillars - diplomacy, defense and security, and development - are tasked with establishing the technical, political, and diplomatic groundwork for the confederation. Their findings will be submitted to the Foreign Ministers for review ahead of the second session of the AES College of Heads of State. The head of the Burkinabe delegation, Ambassador Secretary-General Yirigouin Hermann Toe, emphasized that the preparatory meeting aims to harmonize diplomatic positions so that the AES can speak with one coherent and strong voice on regional and international matters.

During the meeting, experts are reviewing achievements since the first session of the College of Heads of State and assessing the implementation of the roadmap under the Malian presidency.

For Ambassador Mahamane Amadou Maïga, head of the Malian delegation, the objective is to identify ways to consolidate peace and fraternity among the three peoples and strengthen the Confederation’s sovereignty internationally.

According to Ambassador Ousmane Alhassane, head of the Nigerien delegation, several reports and draft documents will be examined and finalized, including:

The draft additional protocol regarding the Confederation's pillars and the confederal sessions of parliaments;

The draft rules of procedure for the confederal sessions of the Council of Ministers;

The draft working document for the upcoming session of Foreign Ministers.

The outcomes of this 48-hour preparatory meeting will be presented to the Foreign Ministers of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger on November 26, ahead of the second session of the AES College of Heads of State, planned for December 2025.

body_en:
Bratislava, November 24, 2025 - Her Excellency Maïmounata OUATTARA, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Burkina Faso to the Slovak Republic, officially presented her credentials to President Peter PELLEGRINI on November 18, 2025, in accordance with established diplomatic protocol.

This formal and courteous ceremony provided the Ambassador an opportunity to convey the fraternal greetings of His Excellency Captain Ibrahim TRAORÉ, President of Burkina Faso, to her Slovak counterpart. She also reaffirmed Burkina Faso’s commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two nations.

In response, President PELLEGRINI expressed his desire to intensify diplomatic relations with Burkina Faso, as well as with other countries represented in Slovakia. He further shared Slovakia’s new strategic vision, aimed at diversifying partnerships, with particular emphasis on collaborations with Africa and Southeast Asia.

title: Strengthening the Ouagadougou-Tehran Axis: Visit of a Special Envoy from the Islamic Republic of Iran to Burkina Faso
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad, His Excellency Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received a special envoy from the Islamic Republic of Iran, Mr.
title_en: Strengthening the Ouagadougou-Tehran Axis: Visit of a Special Envoy from the Islamic Republic of Iran to Burkina Faso
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad, His Excellency Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received a special envoy from the Islamic Republic of Iran, Mr.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabe Abroad, His Excellency Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, received a special envoy from the Islamic Republic of Iran, Mr. Akbar Khosravinejad, on the evening of Tuesday, November 25, 2025.

The Iranian envoy conveyed an important message from the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, His Excellency Dr. Abbas Araghchi, to his Burkinabe counterpart. He also extended an official invitation to Minister Traoré for a visit to Iran, aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

Mr. Khosravinejad highlighted the satisfaction of Iranian authorities with the quality of cooperation between Iran and Burkina Faso, and praised the excellent relations between Iran and the three member states of the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA).

He expressed hope that these relations would be further reinforced through a consultation framework between the CSA and Iran, fostering greater support and solidarity between the parties.

Minister Traoré welcomed the initiative and acknowledged the invitation as a strong sign of friendship between Burkina Faso and the Islamic Republic of Iran. He also emphasized his appreciation for Iran’s ambition to engage in active cooperation with the CSA within a shared vision.

title: Second Summit of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES): Preparatory Meeting of Foreign Ministers
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - Bamako is set to host the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025.
title_en: Second Summit of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES): Preparatory Meeting of Foreign Ministers
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - Bamako is set to host the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - Bamako is set to host the second session of the College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) on December 22 and 23, 2025.

In preparation for this major summit, the Foreign Ministers of Burkina Faso, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, of Mali, H.E. Abdoulaye Diop, and of Niger, H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangaré, are meeting on November 26, 2025, in Ouagadougou. During this session, they will examine the various reports prepared by experts during the 48 hours of work held in Ouagadougou, with a view to submitting them in December to the Council of Ministers, and subsequently to Their Excellencies Captain Ibrahim Traoré, General Assimi Goïta, and General Abdourahamane Tiani during the summit.

Welcoming his counterparts, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré stated that this meeting is “an opportunity to review all the important measures taken since the first summit of July 2024, with a view to consolidating the confederation’s momentum.”

The ministers will present the progress achieved since the creation of the Confederation, as well as the implementation of the roadmap under the Malian presidency, structured around the three pillars of the AES: defense and security, diplomacy, and development.

They commended the achievements recorded so far, particularly:

Significant gains made by the defense and security forces,

The establishment of the Unified AES Force,

The imminent opening of the Confederal Investment and Development Bank (BCID-AES),

Enhanced coordination among member states at all levels.

According to H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangaré, the meeting in Ouagadougou is a “decisive step” toward consolidating these accomplishments and implementing the Confederation’s structural framework, notably through the examination and validation of key legal instruments and protocols.

Expressing gratitude for the support provided by Burkina Faso and Niger during Mali’s recent fuel crisis, H.E. Abdoulaye Diop, who chaired the opening ceremony, emphasized:“These advances, although not exhaustive, demonstrate that with political vision and consistent commitment, we are capable of achieving the noble objectives set by our Heads of State.”

title: Strengthening the Confederation of Sahel States: Foreign Ministers Report Significant Progress
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 27, 2025 - The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States concluded on Wednesday evening, November 26, 2025, in Ouagadougou with the signing of the session minutes, a press…
title_en: Strengthening the Confederation of Sahel States: Foreign Ministers Report Significant Progress
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 27, 2025 - The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States concluded on Wednesday evening, November 26, 2025, in Ouagadougou with the signing of the session minutes, a press…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 27, 2025 - The meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States concluded on Wednesday evening, November 26, 2025, in Ouagadougou with the signing of the session minutes, a press release, and a motion of thanks addressed to the Confederation’s leaders.

During this preparatory session ahead of the second meeting of the College of Heads of State-scheduled for December 22 and 23, 2025, in Bamako-Their Excellencies Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré (Burkina Faso), Abdoulaye Diop (Mali), and Bakary Yaou Sangaré (Niger) reviewed the actions taken since the creation of the Confederation to advance its establishment and strengthen its presence at regional and international levels.

According to the three ministers, the Ouagadougou meeting is fully aligned with the vision of the Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA), which seeks to build a sovereign, secure, and prosperous space for the benefit of the peoples of the Sahel.

The ministers examined in detail the implementation of the Confederation’s roadmap, under Mali’s presidency, developed during the first Summit of Heads of State held on July 6, 2024, in Niamey, Niger.

A year and a half after the CSA’s creation, the ministers noted substantial progress in consolidating the bloc.

They highlighted achievements by the three member states in addressing security challenges, strengthening diplomatic coordination, and promoting socio-economic development for the populations of the Confederation.

The ministers also denounced what they described as “media terrorism” waged by segments of the international press seeking to tarnish the image of CSA member states and undermine the development efforts led by their presidents. Applauding the resilience of Sahelian populations and their confidence in national leadership, they reaffirmed their determination to continue building the Confederation in the same spirit, consistent with the vision of the Heads of State.

At the close of the session, the ministers extended special appreciation to the President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, for his commitment-alongside his Malian and Nigerien counterparts-to consolidating the achievements of the CSA and upholding the dignity of the region within Africa and beyond, in keeping with its pan-African orientation.
