title_en: 8th National Integration Forum: Official Launch of Activities in the Border Town of Pô
excerpt_en: The border town of Pô, November 29, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, accompanied by the Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms.
body_en:
The border town of Pô, November 29, 2025 - The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation, and Burkinabè Abroad, H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, accompanied by the Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation, Ms. Stella Bêbgnansgna Eldine Kabre/Kaboré, officially inaugurated the 8th edition of the National Integration Forum on Friday, November 28, in the border town of Pô.

The patron of this edition, Mr. Jacques Sosthène Dingara, Minister of Basic Education, members of the African diplomatic corps accredited to Burkina Faso, and numerous administrative, traditional, military, and paramilitary authorities from the Nazinon region attended the ceremony.

Before the African diaspora living in Burkina Faso and the traditional authorities of Nahouri and Ghana, Minister Traoré launched three days of activities aimed at strengthening cohesion and peaceful coexistence between Burkinabè citizens and diaspora communities.

Placed under the theme “African Integration: Historical Landmarks and Contemporary Imperatives,” the forum serves as a space for dialogue, exchange, and promotion of African values of solidarity and brotherhood.

In his opening address, Minister Traoré praised the local and diaspora communities of the border town of Pô, highlighting the natural integration and cohesion that define this strategic crossing point.

“Here, in this border town, we witness perfect integration-people move freely, exchange, and unite. Every action reminds us that it is the administration that is lagging behind. We must accelerate legislation to match the lived reality of our people,” he said.

The Minister commended efforts in the Nazinon region and Nahouri province to promote harmonious coexistence, helping build strong integration.

He urged African communities to embrace unity, dialogue, and collective strength, stressing that Africa is a mosaic in which each state plays a vital role.

“This is how, in centuries to come, our children will inherit a space of pride and dignity-where integration is not discussed but lived,” he added.

The patron of the edition, Minister Jacques Sosthène Dingara, commended the government for its initiative to reinforce integration and unity in everyday life.

He encouraged continued efforts to strengthen integration in this border area and stressed the need to combat anything that could weaken social cohesion.

Speaking for the foreign communities, Anane James Amedeker expressed pride in the harmony enjoyed by African nationals living in Burkina Faso. He praised government initiatives, especially the visa exemption, and urged African states to collaborate in fighting border harassment.

During the opening ceremony, ten foreign nationals received their naturalization decrees. The Ministry also awarded certificates of recognition to four individuals whose work supports integration and social cohesion.

The Directorate General for African Integration planned varied activities for this major gathering, including brainstorming sessions, dialogues with ministry officials, cultural exchanges, sports activities, and tourist excursions.

title: Burkina Faso: Future Police Officers Trained on International Protection and Refugee Management
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Permanent Secretariat of the National Commission for Refugees (CONAREF) organized a training workshop on November 14 for trainees of the 55th class of the National Police School (ENP).
title_en: Burkina Faso: Future Police Officers Trained on International Protection and Refugee Management
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Permanent Secretariat of the National Commission for Refugees (CONAREF) organized a training workshop on November 14 for trainees of the 55th class of the National Police School (ENP).
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Permanent Secretariat of the National Commission for Refugees (CONAREF) organized a training workshop on November 14 for trainees of the 55th class of the National Police School (ENP). The session aimed to strengthen their understanding of refugee protection mechanisms and the responsibilities of security forces in managing displaced populations.

Ambassador Vlé Flubert Traoré, Permanent Secretary of CONAREF, reaffirmed that these efforts demonstrate Burkina Faso’s commitment to honoring its international obligations in matters of refugee protection. He emphasized the importance of solidarity toward individuals forced to flee their countries, while stressing the need to reconcile this commitment with national security priorities.

He underscored that state security remains paramount and that authorities must prevent the entry or settlement of individuals who may pose risks. He encouraged the future police officers to fully engage in this training, which he described as essential to their professional development.

Representing the Director General of the ENP, Principal Commissioner Djibril Hié praised the initiative, noting that the workshop would equip trainees with specialized skills in international protection. CONAREF also presented the legal instruments governing the protection of refugees and asylum seekers in Burkina Faso.

title_en: Burkina Faso: DGIA Reviews Implementation of Budget Program 137 on African Integration
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 20, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate-General for African Integration (DGIA), held on Thursday its third review session of…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 20, 2025 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad, through the Directorate-General for African Integration (DGIA), held on Thursday its third review session of Budget Program 137: “African Integration.” The meeting was chaired by the Director-General for African Integration, Ambassador Marie Bernadette Conrad Nikiema/Tapsoba.

This framework for dialogue aimed primarily at assessing the implementation of Program 137 since the previous review session in October 2024, and at identifying the main challenges that hindered its execution on the ground.

According to Ambassador Nikiema/Tapsoba, the session also sought to harmonize the interventions of various sectoral ministries involved in promoting African integration, in order to improve coordination and ensure greater coherence in national actions.

In light of recent geopolitical developments-particularly the creation of the Confederation of Sahel States (CES)-the Director-General stressed the need to align all regional and subregional integration initiatives with the current strategic dynamics. “It is essential that every action promoting regional and subregional integration be coordinated and consistent with the evolving context,” she stated.

Program 137 is one of the six budget programs managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and is specifically dedicated to advancing regional integration efforts within Burkina Faso.

title: Burkina Faso Moves Forward with Nuclear Project: Lawmakers Approve Ratification of Agreement on the Peaceful Use of Nucl
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT) unanimously adopted, on Friday, the bill authorizing the ratification of the cooperation agreement between Burkina Faso and the Russian…
title_en: Burkina Faso Moves Forward with Nuclear Project: Lawmakers Approve Ratification of Agreement on the Peaceful Use of Nucl
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT) unanimously adopted, on Friday, the bill authorizing the ratification of the cooperation agreement between Burkina Faso and the Russian…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT) unanimously adopted, on Friday, the bill authorizing the ratification of the cooperation agreement between Burkina Faso and the Russian Federation on the peaceful use of nuclear energy. This marks a major step in the country’s ambition to develop electro-nuclear capacity and strengthen its energy sovereignty.

The plenary session of November 21 was highlighted by the presentation of the bill by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, who once again defended the initiative introduced by the government. The bill builds on the cooperation agreement signed with Russia on June 19, 2025, laying the foundation for a strategic partnership in the civilian nuclear sector.

During discussions, lawmakers expressed several important concerns, particularly regarding:

The overall cost of building and operating a nuclear facility;

Safety and security guarantees, especially in relation to technological risks;

The availability of domestic expertise to manage, operate, and maintain nuclear installations;

Modalities of regional cooperation, especially with other members of the AES Confederation, within a framework of integrated energy planning.

Several speakers stressed the need for a long-term vision, a strong regulatory framework, and significant capacity building for national technical personnel.

A Government Defense Focused on Energy Sovereignty

Minister Traoré responded in detail, emphasizing the strategic relevance of civilian nuclear energy for Burkina Faso.

According to him, nuclear technology represents one of the most reliable and effective solutions today to meet:

the growing demand for electricity,

the country’s industrial ambitions,

the need for economic competitiveness,

and the challenge of energy autonomy.

“If we want to live up to our industrial promises, enhance the competitiveness of our economy, and consolidate our energy sovereignty, this option becomes necessary,” the minister declared, stressing that nuclear energy will allow the country to reach a competitive level in the long term.

He also reaffirmed the unwavering determination of the President of Faso to see this initiative through, highlighting its structural and historic significance for the nation.

Unanimous Vote Gives Government the Green Light for the Nuclear Program

Convinced by the minister’s arguments, lawmakers cast a unanimous vote in favor of the bill, thereby granting the government the official mandate to begin the operational implementation of the national nuclear program.

Following the vote, the Minister of Energy, Mines, and Quarries, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, welcomed what he described as a “decisive milestone” for Burkina Faso. He stated that this adoption represents a major advancement, clearing the way for the development of a sovereign, diversified, and resilient energy capacity.

The adoption of this law marks the beginning of a structuring process for the future of Burkina Faso’s energy landscape. It opens the door to:

the technical planning of the nuclear project,

the training of a national specialized engineering corps,

the development of international partnerships,

and the establishment of a nuclear safety framework aligned with international standards.

This strategic decision, rooted in a desire for energy independence, positions Burkina Faso among the African nations turning to civilian nuclear power as a driver of economic transformation.

title_en: Confederation of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES): Minister Pindgwendé Gilbert Ouedraogo Present at the Signing of the
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts, and Tourism, Pindgwendé Gilbert Ouedraogo, took part in a major step toward strengthening communication within the Confederation of the…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Minister of Communication, Culture, Arts, and Tourism, Pindgwendé Gilbert Ouedraogo, took part in a major step toward strengthening communication within the Confederation of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). On Wednesday, November 26, 2025, he attended the official signing of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) that establishes the Confederation’s first joint radio broadcasting platform.

The MoU was signed by the Foreign Ministers of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger, the three member states of the AES, marking a significant advance in the Confederation’s strategy to unify its information ecosystem, counter hostile media narratives, and enhance sovereign communication capacity.

The new station, named “Daandè Liptako”-Fulfulde for “The Voice of Liptako”-symbolizes the shared heritage, identity, and geopolitical importance of the Liptako-Gourma region, a territory historically linked to the three nations.

According to officials, the creation of Daandè Liptako is a direct response to the growing challenges posed by disinformation campaigns, perception warfare, and external attempts to influence public opinion in the Sahel. The station will function as a central pillar of the Confederation’s communication architecture, ensuring:

the production and dissemination of verified, credible, and timely information,

the countering of false narratives,

and the promotion of the Confederation’s vision, reforms, and achievements.

The memorandum outlines several core missions assigned to the radio station:

Strengthen communication mechanisms within the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA) in the face of security, political, and informational threats;

Raise awareness among populations and encourage positive behavioral change, particularly in matters of unity, security cooperation, and civic responsibility;

Serve as a centralized communication hub for the three member countries, enabling harmonized public messaging;

Promote dialogue, cultural exchange, and mutual understanding across the confederation territory.

The station’s headquarters will be based in Ouagadougou, reflecting Burkina Faso’s central role in the AES communication initiatives. To ensure broad coverage across the Sahel:

a relay antenna will be installed in Bamako,

another in Niamey,

allowing the station to broadcast continuously throughout the Confederation area and reach remote communities.

Programming is expected to include news bulletins, educational content, cultural programming, public service announcements, and special features promoting the values and goals of the AES.

Launch Expected at the Next Heads of State Summit

The radio station will be officially launched during the upcoming AES Heads of State Summit, scheduled for December 22-23, 2025, in Bamako, Mali. The launch will be one of the flagship achievements presented at the summit, alongside other initiatives aimed at strengthening the Confederation’s institutional framework and sovereign communication tools.

By attending this ceremony, Minister Pindgwendé Gilbert Ouedraogo reaffirmed Burkina Faso’s commitment to building a strong, coordinated, and resilient Sahel communication space, capable of defending the interests and image of its peoples on the regional and international scenes.

title_en: Burkina Faso: Correction Issued on Admission Results for Early Childhood Educator Recruitment Exam
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection has issued a correction notice regarding the results of the recruitment examination for the 910 trainees admitted to the 2025…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 17, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection has issued a correction notice regarding the results of the recruitment examination for the 910 trainees admitted to the 2025 session for early childhood educator training. The clarification comes following a review of the list of candidates previously placed on the waiting list.

According to the ministry, the case of candidate Sankara Karim, initially listed as inadmissible and ranked 52nd on the waiting list, has been formally rectified after a re-examination of his application file.

Following this review, the “inadmissible” status attributed to him was lifted.

The ministry’s updated statement confirms that Sankara Karim is now officially admitted and has been added to the list of successful candidates. The institution stresses that no other modifications have been made to the original results.

The Ministry of Public Service reiterates that, aside from this single correction, all provisions and information contained in the initial press release remain fully valid and unchanged.

title: Burkina Faso Advances Toward a Legal Framework for Occupational Health and Safety in Public Administration
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through the Directorate General of Social Protection (DGPS), has launched a two-day pre-validation workshop…
title_en: Burkina Faso Advances Toward a Legal Framework for Occupational Health and Safety in Public Administration
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through the Directorate General of Social Protection (DGPS), has launched a two-day pre-validation workshop…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through the Directorate General of Social Protection (DGPS), has launched a two-day pre-validation workshop dedicated to the draft decree on occupational health and safety (OHS) within the Burkinabe public administration.

The opening session was presided over by the Ministry’s Secretary-General, Suanyaba Rodrigue Oboulbiga, who emphasized the government’s determination to strengthen the protection of workers across public institutions.

In his remarks, Mr. Oboulbiga recalled that the initiative reflects the State's commitment to preserving human capital, which he described as essential to productivity, institutional efficiency, and sustainable development. He noted that the future decree aims not only to clarify and unify the legal framework governing workplace safety but also to reinforce prevention mechanisms across all public bodies.

“Work can be a source of fulfillment, but it also exposes men and women to risks that can affect their physical and mental well-being,” he warned.

The Secretary-General pointed out a significant imbalance between the public and private sectors: while the private sector already operates under a clear legal framework ensuring safe working conditions, public administration remains far behind, with fragmented and insufficient legislative provisions in place.

To illustrate the urgency of reform, Mr. Oboulbiga cited data from the Autonomous Pension Fund for Civil Servants (CARFO). In 2023 alone, 608 workplace accidents and occupational illnesses were recorded among civil servants.

“While compensation mechanisms are well-established, prevention remains the weak link of our system,” he acknowledged, urging participants to contribute constructively and propose actionable improvements.

Throughout the workshop-held on November 18 and 19-participants will examine several key areas, including:

Universal norms related to specific workplace risk factors

Accident prevention requirements tailored to public administration

This pre-validation marks a decisive step toward establishing a comprehensive and coherent OHS framework, with the potential to significantly improve working conditions for thousands of civil servants nationwide.

body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 19, 2025 - The Secretary General of the Ministry of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Suanyaba Rodrigue Oboulbiga, officially opened the 2nd Ordinary Session of the Labor Advisory Commission (CCT) on Wednesday in Ouagadougou. The three-day session, held from November 19 to 21, 2025, will focus on reviewing four major draft regulatory texts aimed at strengthening the national labor framework.

Among the documents submitted for examination is a draft decree establishing working conditions for domestic employees-a sector often marked by informality and limited legal protection. Another key text concerns the procedures for filing, publishing, translating, adhering to, and withdrawing from collective bargaining agreements, a move intended to modernize social dialogue mechanisms.

The commission will also review two additional draft decrees:

one regulating the functioning of employment placement agencies and temporary work agencies, and

another defining and sanctioning violations of the Labor Code and its implementing provisions.

In his opening address, Secretary-General Oboulbiga praised the commission members for their unwavering dedication to promoting constructive social dialogue and maintaining stability in the world of work.

“I would like to emphasize the quality of the work you accomplished during the first session of this year. Your contribution to the review of the draft texts relating to staff representatives and the procedures for communicating internal regulations was remarkable,” he said.

Turning to the four draft decrees under review, Mr. Oboulbiga encouraged participants to pursue their deliberations in a climate of serenity, mutual respect, and consensus-building.

“I sincerely hope that your reflections and recommendations will lead to clear and operational texts that promote sustainable social progress,” he added before formally declaring the session open.

This second ordinary session marks another step toward reinforcing the legal and institutional environment governing labor relations in Burkina Faso, with outcomes expected to shape policy implementation in key segments of the country’s workforce.

“I would like to highlight the quality of the work you accomplished during the first session of this year. Your contribution to the review of draft texts related to staff representatives and procedures for communicating internal regulations was remarkable. I am sincerely grateful,” he said.

Regarding the four draft decrees on the agenda for this second session, Mr. Oboulbiga urged participants to conduct their work with serenity, mutual respect, and a search for consensus.

“I sincerely hope that your reflections and recommendations will result in clear and operational texts that promote sustainable social progress,” he added, before officially declaring the second ordinary session of the CCT for 2025 open.

excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 20, 2025 - The enrollment campaign for the Universal Health Insurance Scheme (RAMU) continues to gain strong momentum in the Nahouri region. A supervisory mission, led by the Deputy Director General, Mr.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 20, 2025 - The enrollment campaign for the Universal Health Insurance Scheme (RAMU) continues to gain strong momentum in the Nahouri region. A supervisory mission, led by the Deputy Director General, Mr. Delwendé Serges Parfait Kagambèga, visited the area on November 18, 2025, to assess progress.

During the visit, the mission met with the local team responsible for information, awareness, and registration, led by Mr. Issaka Garango.

Mr. Garango praised the mobilization of administrative staff, who have been fully engaged since operations launched on November 10.

This momentum continued on November 19 with targeted awareness sessions. These meetings reached key audiences, particularly healthcare professionals and stakeholders in the legal sector, aiming to strengthen their understanding of the objectives and challenges of the RAMU system.

Campaign leaders highlighted that this strong participation reflects a collective commitment to support the implementation of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme, a major reform designed to improve access to healthcare across Burkina Faso.

title: RAMU Expansion: CNAMU Intensifies Registrations Across Provinces
excerpt: Ouagadougou, December 2, 2025 - As part of the expansion of the Universal Health Insurance (UHI) system, the National Health Insurance Fund (CNAMU) has deployed teams to five regions, covering approximately twenty…
title_en: RAMU Expansion: CNAMU Intensifies Registrations Across Provinces
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, December 2, 2025 - As part of the expansion of the Universal Health Insurance (UHI) system, the National Health Insurance Fund (CNAMU) has deployed teams to five regions, covering approximately twenty…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, December 2, 2025 - As part of the expansion of the Universal Health Insurance (UHI) system, the National Health Insurance Fund (CNAMU) has deployed teams to five regions, covering approximately twenty provinces, throughout November 2025. The main goal is to inform the population about RAMU, its benefits, and to register individuals so they can access the system’s services.

According to Jean-Baptiste Yameogo, technical advisor to the Director General of CNAMU and supervisor for the Boromo-Houndé-Orodara-Sindou region, discussions with the public and healthcare professionals revealed strong enthusiasm for RAMU, alongside questions about registration, enrollment, healthcare access, contributions, and system management in health centers. Mr. Yameogo assured that the State will ensure that everyone can contribute to financing Universal Health Insurance and access quality care.

As of November 18, 2025, over 293,000 people had registered since the launch of the program in September 2024.

For example, in the Kénédougou province, 1,658 individuals had registered, including 612 civil servants and their family members. Achieving this milestone enables CNAMU to prepare for the next phases, particularly the collection of contributions and disbursement of benefits.

Beneficiaries have welcomed this initiative, highlighting its advantages in reducing household financial burdens and promoting solidarity with the most vulnerable. During his visit to Sindou, Mr. Yameogo and his delegation also paid a courtesy call to the High Commissioner of Léraba province, Yacouba Sawadogo, who confirmed the smooth progress of registration activities in his province.

title_en: Decentralization of Civil Servant Career Paths: Regional Directors Prepared for Successful Implementation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through its Directorate General of the Civil Service (DGFP), organized an information and training session for…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through its Directorate General of the Civil Service (DGFP), organized an information and training session for regional directors on Friday, November 21, 2025, in Ouagadougou. The session focused on the implementation of the decentralization of civil servant career paths.

This initiative underscores the Ministry's commitment to improving human capital management and bringing public services closer to citizens.

In his address, the Director General of the Civil Service, Tégawendé Alfred Simporé, emphasized that the decentralization of career paths will enable the efficient issuance of promotion orders, step increases for decorations, and appointments of civil servants to permanent positions at the regional directorate level. He reaffirmed that this reform aims to make career management more efficient and better aligned with the needs of both civil servants and the administration.

The session also provided an opportunity to present to regional directors the legal framework for issuing career documents, including the required documents, standardized templates, and document processing workflows. The modules of the Integrated State Personnel Administrative and Payroll Management System (SIGASPE) were explained in detail to facilitate the practical implementation of the reform.

Despite his numerous commitments, the Minister for the Civil Service, Mathias Traoré, attended the session to encourage regional directors and discuss their concerns. He urged them to implement the reform diligently and effectively, for the benefit of civil servants and the broader public administration.

body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 21, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, accompanied by his counterpart from the Ministry of Health, Robert Lucien Jean Claude Kargougou, held a press conference on Friday, November 21, 2025, in Ouagadougou to present the implementation of the Universal Health Insurance Scheme (RAMU). The session aimed to inform the public about the details of this major social protection mechanism for citizens of Burkina Faso.

Minister Traoré emphasized that less than 10% of the population currently benefits from social security coverage, while direct household health expenditures reach 34%, well above the maximum threshold of 20% set by the World Health Organization (WHO).

According to him, the RAMU (Universal Health Coverage Scheme) offers a structured solution enabling every citizen to access healthcare without financial hardship, while integrating with existing social security systems and allowing citizens the option to purchase supplemental private insurance.

These services will be provided in healthcare facilities that have signed agreements with the National Universal Health Insurance Fund (CNAMU), covering both public and private sectors.

Public sector employees: 5% of gross salary

Self-employed workers in the formal sector: 15,000 CFA francs/month

Workers in the informal sector: 4,000 CFA francs/month

Government contribution: 4,000 CFA francs/month for low-income individuals

Benefits will commence on February 1, 2026, initially targeting civil servants in the Kadiogo and Guiriko regions, after at least three months of contributions. Registration is open at CNAMU headquarters in Ouaga 2000 and at the regional offices of labor and social protection.

title_en: Admission Results for Candidates on the Waiting List for Direct Entry Examinations, 2025 Session
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 23, 2025 - The admission results for the 2025 session for candidates initially placed on the waiting list for direct entry examinations, replacing candidates who withdrew, have been published.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 23, 2025 - The admission results for the 2025 session for candidates initially placed on the waiting list for direct entry examinations, replacing candidates who withdrew, have been published.

Candidates admitted to specialized education programs, particularly for the positions of Special Education Assistant and Assistant, are invited to contact the Gaoua School for the Training of Intermediate Managers in Social Work (EFCMTS) as soon as possible.

For agricultural programs, candidates admitted to the positions of Agricultural Technical Agent, Agricultural Technical Agent (VDP), Agricultural Training Assistant, Senior Agricultural Technician, and Senior Agricultural Technician (VDP) must report to the National School of Agricultural Training (ENAFA) to complete the necessary formalities before assuming their duties.

Candidates admitted to the positions of Economic Affairs Advisor and Labor Inspector are invited to contact the National School of Administration and Magistracy (ENAM) to finalize their registration and begin their training. Similarly:

Environmental Technicians should report to the National School of Water and Forestry (ENEF)

Senior Technicians in Livestock and Animal Health should report to the National School of Livestock and Animal Health (ENESA)

All admitted candidates are strongly urged to comply promptly with the instructions of their respective institutions to ensure the efficient and timely start of their training. These measures aim to guarantee the rapid integration of new professionals into their fields.

title_en: Labor Inspection: Burkina Faso Moves Toward Harmonized Practices
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through the Directorate General of Labor (DGT), launched on Monday a two-day workshop in Ouagadougou aimed at…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The Ministry of Public Service, Labor, and Social Protection (MFPTPS), through the Directorate General of Labor (DGT), launched on Monday a two-day workshop in Ouagadougou aimed at harmonizing the practices of labor inspection services across the country.

The opening ceremony was chaired by Jean-Marie Ki, Director of Studies and Regulations at the DGT, representing the Secretary General of the Ministry.

Designed as a platform for dialogue between labor inspectors and controllers, the workshop seeks to address the varying interpretations of certain provisions of the Labor and Social Security Code. Its ultimate goal: ensure coherent, standardized practices nationwide.

In his opening remarks, Mr. Ki stressed that the role of labor inspection has grown increasingly crucial in a context marked by rapid economic change, evolving work organization, and heightened expectations around social compliance. Labor inspection, he said, is at once “an instrument of social justice, a mechanism for preventing conflicts, and a guarantor of fundamental rights at work.”

He emphasized, however, that the effectiveness of this mission depends on ensuring that inspection practices are not only aligned with legal requirements but also uniform and predictable for all stakeholders.“This workshop is particularly important because it allows you to strengthen your shared understanding by reviewing your professional practices in light of national legislation, and by comparing your field experiences to identify both convergences and gaps that must be addressed,” he noted.

Calling on participants to engage in open, constructive dialogue, Mr. Ki underscored that harmonized practices are essential to improving the social climate and building an environment conducive to economic and social development-one rooted in legality, equity, and dialogue.

title: Burkina Faso: Public Service Minister Mathias Traoré Defends 2026 Priorities Before Budget Committee
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, appeared on Monday before the Finance and Budget Committee (COMFIB) of the Transitional Legislative Assembly…
title_en: Burkina Faso: Public Service Minister Mathias Traoré Defends 2026 Priorities Before Budget Committee
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, appeared on Monday before the Finance and Budget Committee (COMFIB) of the Transitional Legislative Assembly…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, appeared on Monday before the Finance and Budget Committee (COMFIB) of the Transitional Legislative Assembly to present the performance of his ministry’s 2025 budget and outline the priorities set for 2026.

Opening his presentation, the Minister expressed gratitude for the continued support of the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT), before reviewing progress under the Ministry’s flagship programs:

Committee members engaged in extensive discussions, raising questions on several sensitive and structural issues. Among the topics addressed were the implementation of the Universal Health Insurance (RAMU), the new targeted recruitment mechanism, the fight against fake diplomas, medical examinations for retirees, the rights of laid-off workers, enforcement of political neutrality within the civil service, and the overall status of the public workforce.

According to Traoré, the ministry has already initiated actions on all these fronts, and efforts will intensify in the coming year.

Looking ahead to 2026, the Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to advancing public service reforms, strengthening labor governance, and expanding social protection systems - all with the overarching goal of safeguarding the general interest of workers.

He also called for the continued backing of the Legislative Assembly, particularly to finalize the rollout of the RAMU, whose benefits are expected to take effect on February 1, 2026.

title: Occupational Health and Safety: Validation of Compliance Reports Underway
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Directorate General of Labor inaugurated a three-day workshop on Wednesday aimed at reviewing and validating compliance reports related to the alignment of national legislation with…
title_en: Occupational Health and Safety: Validation of Compliance Reports Underway
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Directorate General of Labor inaugurated a three-day workshop on Wednesday aimed at reviewing and validating compliance reports related to the alignment of national legislation with…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 26, 2025 - The Directorate General of Labor inaugurated a three-day workshop on Wednesday aimed at reviewing and validating compliance reports related to the alignment of national legislation with two critical International Labour Organization (ILO) conventions:

Convention No. 176, concerning safety and health in mines

Convention No. 187, concerning the framework for promoting health and safety at work

The objective of this workshop is to gather input from stakeholders across the sector to refine these strategic documents and strengthen the national occupational health and safety framework.

Representing the Secretary General of the Ministry of Labor, Employment, and Social Protection (MTEPPS), the Director General of Labor, Stella Somé/Zoungrana, emphasized in her opening address that occupational health and safety in the mining sector is a cornerstone of decent work. She highlighted:

The rapid expansion of Burkina Faso’s mining sector

Past tragedies in Perkoa and Gbomblora, which underscore the urgent need for a sustainable prevention framework

The discussions highlighted the magnitude of existing challenges, including:

Over 5,300 work-related accidents and occupational diseases recorded between 2021 and 2023

A financial cost exceeding 5.6 billion CFA francs for social security organizations

Despite existing progress, the Director General stressed the importance of strengthening the legislative and institutional framework to provide more effective protection for workers.

Finally, she explained that the assessments conducted during the workshop aim to:

Evaluate the feasibility of ratifying ILO Convention No. 176

Participants were encouraged to actively contribute to discussions, helping to consolidate these essential tools that fortify the national social protection system.

Ouagadougou, November 27, 2025 - The National Organizing Committee for the free annual medical examination for retirees and their surviving spouses, jointly led by CARFO and CNSS, held a review workshop this Thursday in Ouagadougou. The meeting brought together members of the national and regional committees to:

Present the activity and financial reports of the 11th edition

Evaluate results achieved to improve future campaigns

Representing the Secretary General of the Ministry of Public Service, the Director General of Social Protection, Oumarou Sawadogo, noted that the 2025 edition, despite some challenges, was conducted satisfactorily. He reported that no major incidents disrupted the activities, reflecting the commitment and professionalism of field teams.

Mr. Sawadogo highlighted the importance of this initiative, stressing that it allows retirees and their surviving spouses to benefit from an essential annual preventive health check-up. Finally, he invited participants to formulate realistic and constructive proposals to enhance the effectiveness of future editions. Through this initiative, the Ministry reaffirms its commitment to guaranteeing strengthened social protection for retirees across Burkina Faso.

title: Groundbreaking Ceremony for the Komsilga Sewage Sludge Treatment Plant
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - On the occasion of World Toilet Day, the Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, representing Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, officially…
title_en: Groundbreaking Ceremony for the Komsilga Sewage Sludge Treatment Plant
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - On the occasion of World Toilet Day, the Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, representing Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, officially…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - On the occasion of World Toilet Day, the Minister of Public Service, Labor and Social Protection, Mathias Traoré, representing Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, officially launched the construction of the future Komsilga sewage sludge treatment plant in the village of Kalzi.

The Minister of the Environment, Water and Sanitation

Representatives of ONEA (National Water and Sanitation Office)

In his address, delivered on behalf of the Prime Minister, Mr. Traoré emphasized that this project addresses an urgent need: strengthening sludge treatment capacity from septic tanks, as the Kossodo and Zagtouli plants are now insufficient to meet the growing demand.

For the Prime Minister, this new infrastructure embodies:

The commitment to ensuring universal access to safe sanitation by 2030

Contribution to a circular economy through the valorization of sludge as organic fertilizer

Mr. Traoré also stressed the shared responsibility of citizens and sanitation companies, urging households to:

Recognize that investing in latrines is investing in health and dignity

He further demanded impeccable professionalism from the companies tasked with operating the plant, noting that no shortcomings would be tolerated given the substantial financial investment by the state.

The Komsilga plant, scheduled to begin operations on September 30, 2026, was financed with 4.5 billion yuan.

title_en: Appeal Verdict in the Amidou TIEGNAN and Others Case: All Found Guilty
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The appeal trial concerning Amidou TIEGNAN, Philippe BAYOULOU, Pétronille TARPAGA/OUEDRAOGO, and Salifou OUEDRAOGO, prosecuted for embezzlement of public funds to the detriment of the…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 18, 2025 - The appeal trial concerning Amidou TIEGNAN, Philippe BAYOULOU, Pétronille TARPAGA/OUEDRAOGO, and Salifou OUEDRAOGO, prosecuted for embezzlement of public funds to the detriment of the Ministry of Humanitarian Action, concluded on Tuesday, November 18, 2025, before the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal. This case, closely followed by the public, involved appeals against the judgment of the first-instance court.

After examining the arguments, the Court of Appeal:

Upheld the first-instance court's decisions regarding objections of lack of jurisdiction, nullity, and statute of limitations

Reaffirmed that embezzlement of public funds is legally distinct from illicit enrichment, emphasizing that the two offenses should not be confused

All defendants were found guilty. However, the Court reviewed some of the sentences handed down at first instance, taking into account procedural considerations and arguments presented on appeal.

This decision is seen as an important step in the fight against corruption and malfeasance within public institutions.

The verdict was welcomed by the Ministry of Humanitarian Action and judicial observers, who view it as a strong signal supporting transparency and accountability among public officials.

title_en: Trial for Mistreatment of a 13-Year-Old Quranic Student: Court Declares Itself Incompetent
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 19, 2025 - The trial involving (H. A.), a Quran teacher accused of mistreating a 13-year-old Quranic student, opened on Wednesday, November 19, 2025, before the criminal chamber of the Ouagadougou…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 19, 2025 - The trial involving (H. A.), a Quran teacher accused of mistreating a 13-year-old Quranic student, opened on Wednesday, November 19, 2025, before the criminal chamber of the Ouagadougou High Court. The case has provoked significant public concern due to the seriousness of the alleged offenses.

The hearing was immediately suspended to allow the criminal court to rule on its jurisdiction, ensuring that it was the proper court to hear the matter. Upon resumption, the court declared itself incompetent, determining that the facts of the case fall under the jurisdiction of another judicial authority.

As a result, the proceedings will be referred to the competent court in accordance with applicable legal provisions.

title: Arbinda on the Brink of Collapse: Residents Issue Plea for Help
excerpt: Arbinda, November 18, 2025 - In Arbinda, located in the Sahel region of Burkina Faso, the humanitarian situation has become dire.
title_en: Arbinda on the Brink of Collapse: Residents Issue Plea for Help
excerpt_en: Arbinda, November 18, 2025 - In Arbinda, located in the Sahel region of Burkina Faso, the humanitarian situation has become dire.
body_en:
Arbinda, November 18, 2025 - In Arbinda, located in the Sahel region of Burkina Faso, the humanitarian situation has become dire. Isolated for months due to a suffocating blockade and cut off from all supplies, the town now faces a severe food crisis. On the morning of November 18, 2025, residents, weakened by hunger, took to the streets to issue a desperate plea for assistance.

With few options remaining, some residents said they might attempt to reach Djibo on foot, despite the high risks posed by insecurity and exhaustion. For many, staying in Arbinda feels like waiting silently for death, and this bleak reality is forcing families to consider unimaginable measures in the hope of survival.

A profound feeling of abandonment grips the population, who claim that the Burkinabe state has left them to face a crisis beyond their control. In a region already suffering from armed attacks and isolation, famine is now more severe than ever, plunging Arbinda into despair.

In a second video, local residents stated that this is the first time in their lives that Arbinda has faced such a catastrophic situation, marked by insecurity, hunger, and abandonment. Many expressed their anger toward Captain Ibrahim Traoré, whom they described as “the worst president to have led Burkina Faso.”

title: Diapaga Under Pressure: Growing Concerns in Eastern Burkina Faso
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 23, 2025 - Tension remains high in Burkina Faso’s Eastern Region following the attack on the town of Diapaga on Saturday, November 22.
title_en: Diapaga Under Pressure: Growing Concerns in Eastern Burkina Faso
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 23, 2025 - Tension remains high in Burkina Faso’s Eastern Region following the attack on the town of Diapaga on Saturday, November 22.
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 23, 2025 - Tension remains high in Burkina Faso’s Eastern Region following the attack on the town of Diapaga on Saturday, November 22. According to multiple local sources, JNIM fighters briefly seized full control of the town, holding it until nightfall before withdrawing. Eyewitness accounts describe a large-scale coordinated assault and highlight a significant breakdown in the organization of defense and security forces during the incident.

At the same time, a Burkinabe army aircraft has been conducting continuous flights between Fada N'Gourma and the eastern part of the province over the past three days (November 21-23, 2025). Several sources report that this aircraft is being used frequently to repatriate the remains of security personnel killed in combat. The unusual intensity and frequency of these flights are raising serious concerns among residents and analysts alike: Could the army be experiencing heavier losses than officially acknowledged in this border zone?

These developments cap a week already marked by multiple security alerts across the east. Between recurring attacks, suspicious militant movements, and a climate of rising tension, the population continues to live in a state of persistent insecurity. Meanwhile, local and national authorities are increasingly expected to provide a more structured, coordinated, and effective response to the expanding threats facing the region.

title: Burkina Faso - JNIM Claims Responsibility for a Series of Coordinated Attacks
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin) announced on Monday that it had carried out a deadly assault against a Burkinabe armed forces position in Bibilgo…
title_en: Burkina Faso - JNIM Claims Responsibility for a Series of Coordinated Attacks
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin) announced on Monday that it had carried out a deadly assault against a Burkinabe armed forces position in Bibilgo…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 24, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin) announced on Monday that it had carried out a deadly assault against a Burkinabe armed forces position in Bibilgo, located in Koulpélogo province. According to the group's statement, the attack left seven Burkinabe soldiers dead. The militants claim to have seized five Kalashnikov rifles, along with various military equipment, and to have destroyed several motorcycles belonging to the security forces.

On the same day, the Al-Qaeda-affiliated organization also claimed responsibility for two simultaneous attacks in Tapoa province, targeting auxiliary militia positions in the localities of Lényoussi and Worgouy, in the Fada N’Gourma area. According to their communiqué, these operations resulted in the deaths of ten auxiliary fighters. JNIM further stated that its attackers were able to seize five (5) additional Kalashnikov rifles, six (6) motorcycles, and other equipment before withdrawing.

These attacks, conducted in two geographically distant areas, reflect a continuing escalation of insurgent operations in eastern Burkina Faso, where armed groups have been intensifying their assaults on both the national army and auxiliary defense forces over recent months.

The incidents also highlight the persistent vulnerability of military positions and volunteer security posts in border regions, despite ongoing efforts by the Burkinabe state to stabilize the area and counter extremist activity.

excerpt: Dédougou, November 26, 2025 - The jihadist coalition Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) has claimed responsibility for a new attack carried out on Wednesday, November 26, against a local militia position in the…

excerpt_en: Dédougou, November 26, 2025 - The jihadist coalition Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) has claimed responsibility for a new attack carried out on Wednesday, November 26, against a local militia position in the…
body_en:
Dédougou, November 26, 2025 - The jihadist coalition Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) has claimed responsibility for a new attack carried out on Wednesday, November 26, against a local militia position in the locality of Berkoui, situated in the Dédougou region, in western Burkina Faso.

According to a statement released by the group, the assault resulted in the killing of two militia members stationed at the post. JNIM also claims to have seized two Kalashnikov rifles, eleven motorcycles, and various military and logistical equipment during the operation.

This latest attack adds to a series of recurring operations conducted by the group in western Burkina Faso, a zone where auxiliary forces and local self-defense groups remain highly exposed despite ongoing security efforts. The escalation highlights the continued difficulty faced by Burkinabè authorities in stabilizing regions outside the eastern and northern fronts, where insurgent activity is traditionally more intense.

title: Burkina Faso - Series of Deadly JNIM Attacks Rock the Eastern Region
excerpt: November 23, 2025 - The Eastern Region of Burkina Faso experienced a new surge of violence on Sunday, November 23, in a series of coordinated attacks attributed to Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM).
title_en: Burkina Faso - Series of Deadly JNIM Attacks Rock the Eastern Region
excerpt_en: November 23, 2025 - The Eastern Region of Burkina Faso experienced a new surge of violence on Sunday, November 23, in a series of coordinated attacks attributed to Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM).
body_en:
November 23, 2025 - The Eastern Region of Burkina Faso experienced a new surge of violence on Sunday, November 23, in a series of coordinated attacks attributed to Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). These incidents, spread across three provinces, left several civilians and state agents dead, while causing significant material destruction.

In Boudangou, armed individuals attacked the village, killing three civilians. Several shops were set ablaze during the assault, plunging the community into fear and deepening the displacement already affecting the area.

The situation in Komandougou remains unclear, with local sources providing conflicting accounts. While some report no fatalities, others mention multiple victims.Despite the uncertainty regarding the human toll, the burning of shops and several homes has been confirmed, highlighting the scale and brutality of the attack.

The deadliest of the attacks occurred in Tandyari, where gunmen targeted a forestry agent post. Approximately ten agents were reportedly killed. According to local sources, the attackers then seized weapons, ammunition, motorcycles, and various operational equipment before retreating.

title: Burkina Faso - JNIM Claims Responsibility for New Series of Attacks
excerpt: Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM has claimed responsibility for a new wave of coordinated attacks carried out on November 23 across multiple regions of Burkina Faso, according to a statement…
title_en: Burkina Faso - JNIM Claims Responsibility for New Series of Attacks
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM has claimed responsibility for a new wave of coordinated attacks carried out on November 23 across multiple regions of Burkina Faso, according to a statement…
body_en:
Ouagadougou, November 28, 2025 - The jihadist coalition JNIM has claimed responsibility for a new wave of coordinated attacks carried out on November 23 across multiple regions of Burkina Faso, according to a statement released on Friday.

In the eastern region, the group says it targeted the Komandougou military post, located in the commune of Fada N’Gourma. The assault reportedly left five Burkinabe soldiers dead and resulted in the destruction of a military vehicle. JNIM also claims to have seized a DJI drone, motorcycles, several AK-47 assault rifles with magazines, as well as additional ammunition.

In the central-eastern region, the group asserts it carried out another attack on a military position in the province of Koulpélogo, where seven soldiers were allegedly killed. According to its communiqué, the assailants recovered multiple assault rifles, magazines, a large quantity of ammunition, several heavy machine guns, and an RPG rocket launcher with its equipment.

These latest claims highlight JNIM’s capacity to operate simultaneously on several fronts and to seize significant quantities of military equipment. They also underline the mounting pressure on Burkina Faso’s armed forces in the eastern and east-central regions, where attacks continue to intensify despite ongoing security operations.

title: Burkina Faso - Tapoa on the Verge of Security Collapse
excerpt: November 30, 2025 - The security situation in the province of Tapoa has reached an alarming breaking point, with local sources reporting that more than 95% of the territory is now under the control of armed groups.
title_en: Burkina Faso - Tapoa on the Verge of Security Collapse
excerpt_en: November 30, 2025 - The security situation in the province of Tapoa has reached an alarming breaking point, with local sources reporting that more than 95% of the territory is now under the control of armed groups.
body_en:
November 30, 2025 - The security situation in the province of Tapoa has reached an alarming breaking point, with local sources reporting that more than 95% of the territory is now under the control of armed groups. The Burkinabe army maintains only a minimal presence in three localities - including Diapaga - and even there, its hold is described as extremely fragile.

The town of Diapaga has been attacked repeatedly in recent weeks. The military detachment has been overwhelmed, civilians and security personnel killed, and shops and warehouses looted. Videos filmed and circulated by the assailants themselves illustrate the extent of state erosion in the area. In Kantchari and Partiaga, the situation is equally dire: although military outposts remain, soldiers reportedly avoid venturing more than one kilometer from their bases due to the constant threat of ambushes.

Patrols have been reduced to cautious movements within city centers, with no real capacity for wider deployment. Meanwhile, armed groups are imposing - without resistance - a form of mandatory levy, described by residents as a “zakat” of 50,000 FCFA per inhabitant across the province. This practice underscores the extent of their administrative and coercive control.

The humanitarian situation is deteriorating just as rapidly. Only the primary healthcare centers (CSPS) in Diapaga and Kantchari remain functional, and even these operate with severely limited resources. All other health facilities in Tapoa are closed. Mortality rates are rising, particularly among pregnant women and children, due to the collapse of essential medical services.

The portrait emerging from Tapoa is that of an isolated, exhausted province on the brink of total breakdown. A massive and coordinated intervention is urgently needed to prevent the complete security and humanitarian collapse of the region.

title: Burkina Faso - New Episode of Forced Displacement in Tapoa
excerpt: Tapoa, November 30, 2025 - A new wave of forced displacement struck the province of Tapoa on Sunday, as residents from seven villages in the commune of Botou were expelled by fighters from JNIM, according to several…
title_en: Burkina Faso - New Episode of Forced Displacement in Tapoa
excerpt_en: Tapoa, November 30, 2025 - A new wave of forced displacement struck the province of Tapoa on Sunday, as residents from seven villages in the commune of Botou were expelled by fighters from JNIM, according to several…
body_en:
Tapoa, November 30, 2025 - A new wave of forced displacement struck the province of Tapoa on Sunday, as residents from seven villages in the commune of Botou were expelled by fighters from JNIM, according to several local sources. Confronted with direct threats from armed groups, villagers fled en masse toward Botou, placing the town under intense strain as it struggles to absorb the sudden influx of displaced families.

Botou, the largest commune in Tapoa - home to more than forty-two villages - is now facing growing humanitarian pressure. These mass displacements underscore the rapidly worsening security situation in this border zone with Niger, where armed groups are steadily tightening their grip on rural communities.

The latest expulsions highlight how insurgents are expanding their territorial control, deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis across the province and leaving thousands increasingly vulnerable.

The period from November 17 to 30, 2025, was defined by a dual dynamic in Burkina Faso: an aggressive pursuit of state sovereignty and diplomatic realignment on the international stage, contrasted sharply by persistent humanitarian and security crises on the ground.

1. Consolidation of the AES and Diplomatic Diversification Diplomatically, the government focused heavily on cementing the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). The preparatory meetings in Ouagadougou and the establishment of the "Daandè Liptako" joint radio station signal a rapid move toward operationalizing the confederation ahead of the December summit in Bamako. Simultaneously, Burkina Faso diversified its strategic partnerships, ratifying a nuclear energy agreement with Russia and strengthening economic and diplomatic ties with Belarus, Iran, and Slovakia.

2. Major Domestic Reforms Domestically, the government advanced significant structural reforms aimed at social protection and administrative efficiency. The final preparations for the Universal Health Insurance Scheme (RAMU), set to deliver benefits by February 2026, represent a major shift toward social welfare. Additionally, efforts to decentralize the civil service and harmonize labor inspections reflect a push to modernize public administration.

3. The Security and Humanitarian Challenge However, these institutional advances face the harsh reality of insecurity. While the state builds long-term frameworks, immediate stability remains fragile. The dire humanitarian situation in Arbinda, marked by blockade and famine , and continued attacks by armed terrorist groups in the North, highlight the disconnect between central governance achievements and the struggles of remote populations.

Outlook As Burkina Faso moves into December, the focus will shift to the second session of the AES College of Heads of State. The government’s ability to reconcile its ambitious geopolitical vision with the urgent need to secure territory and alleviate the suffering of besieged communities, such as those in Arbinda, will be the defining challenge of the coming weeks.
